Anthropic上市未能缓解AI相关忧虑，亚洲芯片股遭遇抛售

BlockBeats 消息，11 月 20 日，尽管 Anthropic 成功上市，但亚洲芯片相关股票周五仍重现跌势。这表明，过去数月不断累积的、针对 AI 相关投资的担忧，依然主导着投资者的情绪。

在日本，芯片测试设备制造商爱德万测试股价一度大跌 12%，科技投资巨头软银集团在东京股市重挫 17%，拖累日经 225 指数跌至 4 月以来的最低水平。在韩国，SK 海力士和三星电子的跌幅均超过 6%。即便是在中国台湾——当地为稳定股市已收紧了卖空限制——相关股票也遭到抛售，台积电和联发科股价均出现下滑。AI 行业近期频频出现令其长期前景蒙上阴影的动态。

美国中期选举后的监管风险，以及英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋突然离职的消息，加剧了市场对于企业巨额支出及其变现前景的担忧。盛宝金融首席投资策略师 Charu Chanana 表示：「AI 相关投资此前就已面临诸多质疑，例如基础设施支出是否过度、是否存在循环融资，以及投资回报能否覆盖投入成本。

Anthropic 的成功上市并未解答这些疑问。相反，它吸引了更多资本涌入前沿 AI 模型领域——而这一领域竞争异常激烈，定价权正在减弱，盈利能力也依然充满不确定性。」

原文链接 https://m.theblockbeats.info/flash/378333

items.author: Liam 'Akiba' Wright
items.content:
Quick Take
- Students scored higher on proctored exams after instructors introduced AI tools tailored to applied STEM courses.
- The trial enrolled 7,200 students across 19 universities, with 4,768 students in the experimental exam analysis.
- The trial compared earlier and later rollouts, leaving open how course-specific tools would perform against generic chatbots.
Students in applied STEM courses scored higher on proctored exams when instructors introduced AI tools tailored to their classes, compared with classes still waiting for their tools, according to a randomized trial across 19 universities reported in a Nov. 14 preprint.
The research led by Jun Li of the University of Michigan estimated a student-level gain of 0.32 standard deviations, with a 95% confidence interval of 0.06 to 0.59 standard deviations.
The estimate puts the improvement at roughly 33% of the typical spread in scores within a class and leaves uncertainty about the size of the gain. Standardizing scores within each class gave researchers a common scale for comparing results across courses that used different exams.
The preregistered trial involved 7,200 students in 55 applied STEM classes over three semesters, from spring 2025 through spring 2026. The study counted each course-and-instructor pairing as one class.
The experimental part of the exam analysis covered 4,768 students across 44 course offerings. Researchers used results from earlier terms alongside that sample to account for how classes had performed before the rollout.
The exam analysis included only proctored, in-person exams, mostly on paper. The remaining exams used strictly monitored computers or restricted-access computers at university testing centers.
The researchers added that screening rule after preregistration and excluded course offerings where exams could allow AI assistance.
What instructors built with AI tools
Researchers grouped classes by subject and academic level, then randomly assigned them to introduce their tools immediately or one teaching term later.
Instructors in both groups received design and technical support, including training sessions, examples of how to write instructions for the tools, and access to a platform to build and deploy them.
Once instructors brought the tools into their courses, all students in those classes had access during the term, before sitting the exams used to measure learning.
Some instructors built tutors that gave students targeted practice and feedback, while others built coaches that guided students through problems by asking questions. Instructors also designed interactive simulations and ran role-play exercises that let students question AI-generated stakeholders.
The study detected no statistically significant change in engagement or satisfaction. Engagement measures varied by class and included records such as attendance and assignment completion, and satisfaction came from end-of-term course evaluations.
The trial compared rollout timing, leaving open how course-specific tools would fare against generic chatbots. How much each design contributed to the gain and whether it extends beyond applied STEM remain open questions.
items.title: AI tools were supposed to make students think less, but a major university trial found a different result

Michael Saylor：Strategy采取择机操作策略，目前首要任务是支持数字信贷业务

BlockBeats 消息，11 月 20 日，Strategy 创始人 Michael Saylor 在接受采访时表示，「在任何一天，Strategy 都会综合考虑多方面因素，包括资本市场情绪、比特币的交易情况、信贷市场情绪，以及股票资本市场的溢价是在扩大还是收窄。通常来说，如果看最常见的资产置换交易，Strategy 会进行几种操作：用 MSTR 置换 BTC、用 MSTR 置换 STRC，或者用 MSTR 置换美元。

我认为，Strategy 采取的是择机操作的策略。如果能够通过资产置换简单地获得比特币溢价，那么 Strategy 随时都可以这么做。不过，公司的战略核心在于财库业务，而财库业务本质上是一种信贷业务。因此，Strategy 目前的首要任务是支持数字信贷业务，并增强 STRC 的市场表现。当 STRC 表现强劲、运行良好时，实际上也会对 SR 产生支撑作用。STRC 的强势表现还会带动其他公开交易的信贷工具。

因此，我们在做决策时，也是在考虑公司的长期声誉和未来发展。有时，一项决策可能无法在本周带来可观利润，但从未来 1 至 7 年的时间跨度来看，最终可能证明其价值。」

items.title: Michael Saylor：Strategy采取择机操作策略，目前首要任务是支持数字信贷业务

【Solidity 发布 v0.8.39 版本，修复中危级别漏洞】

Foresight News 消息，智能合约编程语言 Solidity 发推表示，其已发布 v0.8.39 版本。该版本修复了一个中危级别漏洞：在复制递归结构体（recursive struct）时可能静默损坏存储，影响 v0.4.9 至 v0.8.38 版本。对 Sourcify 上已验证合约的扫描未发现任何已部署合约执行受影响的复制操作。该版本还修复了嵌套元组（nested tuple）赋值的错误编译问题，并新增针对 Amsterdam EVM 版本（EIP-7954）的代码大小警告。此外，Solidity 表示，这很可能是 v0.8 系列的最后一个版本，下一个版本将是 v0.9.0。团队计划更频繁地发布较小的新版本，而非将大量变更集中在单个大版本中。

Serenity：英伟达面临核心人才流失风险，黄仁勋缺席或动摇核心竞争优势

BlockBeats 消息，11 月 20 日，Serenity 发文表示，据其从多位行业高管处了解到的消息，若黄仁勋短期内无法回归，英伟达可能面临核心员工流失风险。由于公司股价多年来大幅上涨，不少高级管理人员和工程师持有的股权价值已足以支持退休，此前他们选择继续留任，很大程度上是因为黄仁勋的领导力和愿景。随着公司由前任 CFO 临时接管，部分员工可能借此机会离职，即使提高薪酬或聘请 ARM CEO，也未必能够留住这些顶尖人才。

Serenity 还指出，黄仁勋的缺席可能削弱市场对英伟达未来增长的信心。黄仁勋的核心价值不仅在于技术判断，更在于其自上而下的架构规划能力，以及在 CUDA、网络和内部团队出现分歧时，对公司及 AI 生态发展方向作出关键决策。过去多年，黄仁勋通过一系列高风险战略决策，推动供应链、资本和合作伙伴围绕其愿景形成协同，这种信任关系尤其体现在其与台湾地区供应链企业长期建立的合作基础上，外部或内部继任者都难以在短期内复制。

此外，Serenity 认为，英伟达在技术上的领先优势并没有外界想象中那么大，其在不同领域可能仅领先竞争对手数月至一年，而非五年。黄仁勋此前持续推动技术和产业生态加速发展，是公司维持竞争优势的重要因素。若其长期缺席，英伟达及其竞争生态的优势可能逐渐减弱，影响甚至可能超出当前短期产品路线图。黄仁勋亲自作出的关键架构决策，以及调动资本、供应商和整个产业链围绕其愿景协同的能力，才是英伟达最重要的护城河。

items.content:
Binance US Moves Closer to U.S. Perpetual Futures as CFTC Clears DCM and DCO Applications for Substantive Review

Binance US said the U.S. Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) has deemed its applications to register as a designated contract market (DCM) and derivatives clearing organization (DCO) substantially complete, moving them into substantive review. Neither application has been approved. DCM registration would allow Binance US to offer derivatives trading, including futures and options, while DCO registration would allow it to clear those trades. Binance US plans to use both registrations to offer U.S. users regulated derivatives, including perpetual futures. It has not launched any derivatives products and must await formal CFTC approval before doing so.

According to the U.S. Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) website, BAM Derivatives LLC submitted Binance US’s application to register as a designated contract market (DCM). The filing appeared in the public record on November 19 and is currently listed as “pending.” BAM Derivatives plans to list Bitcoin and Ether perpetual contracts, with BAM Clearing LLC providing clearing services. — link
items.title: Binance US Moves Closer to U.S. Perpetual Futures as CFTC Clears DCM and DCO App

CFTC Chair: Onchain Platforms Like Hyperliquid Must Register or Partner With Licensed Exchanges to Enter US Market, Citing Backpack Model

CFTC Chair Michael Selig said onchain platforms such as Hyperliquid must register as exchanges or partner with registered exchanges to offer derivatives to U.S. retail users. They must follow the same rules as traditional exchanges but may still use onchain technology. He cited Backpack, which recently secured futures commission merchant (FCM), designated contract market (DCM) and derivatives clearing organization (DCO) approvals as a compliance basis for entering the U.S. market.

On prediction markets, Selig said the CFTC would work with the Justice Department to defend its federal authority over lawful derivatives contracts against state lawsuits. He also said a single-stock perpetual contract is not necessarily a security-based swap simply because it has no expiry date: its classification depends on its structure, and perpetual funding rates resemble the variation margin settlement used in traditional futures. — link

items.author: Liam 'Akiba' Wright
items.content:
Quick Take
- Ledger is offering limited-time X-ray inspections for suspect hardware wallets at its factory in Vierzon, France.
- Ledger urges concerned buyers who purchased in Berlin from January 2026 onward to contact support as it investigates reports involving two Dubai devices.
- Ledger advises anyone who already used a suspect device to move funds to a wallet with a fresh recovery phrase.
Ledger is offering limited-time X-ray inspections for suspect hardware wallets as its tampering investigation reaches Berlin.
In a Nov. 18 update, the wallet maker said its support team can arrange for customers to send a device to its factory in Vierzon, France, for inspection and return.
The offer lets owners have their device examined for physical alterations. For anyone who has already used a suspect device, Ledger advised moving funds to a wallet with a fresh recovery phrase. The company also said in its advisory that the hardware it found was designed to capture those words during setup.
Ledger noted that the German cases it had investigated were localized to Berlin. The company advised concerned customers who bought a Ledger wallet from a third party there from January 2026 onward to contact its support team.
It also asks concerned buyers who purchased from third parties in Southeast Asia or Dubai to get in touch.
Ledger revealed it is still investigating reports involving two devices in Dubai and is working with distribution partners to learn how they entered circulation. It reported one affected Nano Gen 5 as it continues its investigation into Southeast Asian resellers.
The advisory described the inspection as an option for devices that raise concerns, so customers can ask Ledger Support to arrange secure shipment through an official ticket.
Ledger recommended sending a device only through that channel, and that support will never ask for a recovery phrase. Its guidance for buyers in Berlin, Dubai, and Southeast Asia describes when to contact Ledger, while support handles the arrangements for individual devices sent to the factory.
The inspection can look inside the submitted device for added hardware, since Ledger’s Genuine Check verifies the secure chip's authenticity. Where that chip remains intact, the check can miss a physical addition.
Ledger reported that all the devices it confirmed in this incident carried the same physical modification and that the investigation found no flaw in its secure chip or operating system.
In its Oct. 15 disclosure, Ledger said genuine wallets had been altered after leaving its control and distributed through Southeast Asian resellers.
The company said the samples it examined from stores, warehouses, and its own stock at the time were clean. In November, it described the Berlin findings as part of the same incident and that it still had no confirmed case involving a device bought directly from ledger.com.
When a recovery phrase may be exposed
Ledger advised owners of an unused suspect device to leave it unopened, keep it out of use, and contact official support. They should avoid using it to set up a new wallet or restore an existing one.
For owners who have already used a suspect device, Ledger advised moving funds to a new wallet with a fresh recovery phrase, generated on a device bought directly from its website. It also recommended avoiding reusing any passphrase used on the suspect device.
The recovery phrase is the set of words that lets an owner restore access to a wallet on a compatible device. Entering the same words on replacement hardware brings up the same wallet and leaves the original recovery credential in use.
Someone who already obtained the credentials needed to restore that wallet could use a compatible device of their own. Moving funds to a wallet with a fresh phrase changes the credentials that control those funds.
Meanwhile, an X-ray can look for evidence of physical tampering. Finding an implant would show the unit was altered.
Whether anyone already obtained a particular owner’s recovery words is a separate question that the scan alone cannot answer.
items.title: Ledger’s crypto wallet implant scare spreads to Berlin as Dubai cases come under investigation

items.author: Cointelegraph by Felix Ng
items.content:
Ledger CTO Charles Guillemet to leave after nine years at company
Guillemet helped establish Ledger’s Donjon security lab and says his departure has been planned for months.
Ledger chief technology officer Charles Guillemet announced he will be leaving the company at the end of 2026, after nine years at the company.
In a post on LinkedIn on Thursday, Guillemet said he joined as chief security officer in December 2017, around three years after Ledger was founded. He launched Ledger Donjon, the company’s attack lab, a year later.
“We’ve been preparing this transition for many months, so Ledger’s teams, partners and roadmaps are ready. I’m bullish on Ledger’s future,” said Guillemet.
Guillemet has been a central figure in Ledger’s security operations, first as chief security officer and later as chief technology officer. He helped establish the Ledger Donjon attack lab, which tests hardware and software vulnerabilities. According to Guillemet, Ledger devices now secure roughly 20% of the world’s crypto assets.
“The threat landscape changed too. AI is making attacks cheaper, faster and easier to scale,” he added.
“The question we spent a decade answering for crypto (how do you protect what matters when any device can be compromised?) is now a question for every company, every AI agent and every government.”
Guillemet did not disclose details of his next venture but said he was “building something new” and would “dedicate my time to solving this security mess.”
Guillemet’s announcement comes weeks after Ledger disclosed that attackers had modified genuine hardware wallets with hidden components designed to capture users’ recovery phrases, and slipped the devices into authorized resellers.
The tampering cases were initially reported in Asia, with subsequent incidents identified in Europe and the United Arab Emirates.
Related: Ledger hardware implant saga reaches Dubai’s Virgin Megastore
items.title: Ledger CTO Charles Guillemet to leave after nine years at company

Anthropic超级IPO之后，人才留存迎来考验

BlockBeats 消息，11 月 20 日，今天对 Anthropic 而言是一座重要里程碑。这家成立五年、开发 Claude 大模型的企业，抢在劲敌 OpenAI 之前登陆公开市场；公司于今日晚些时候开盘交易后，大量员工将跻身百万富翁，甚至亿万富翁之列。

而核心问题在于：上市这一天，对 Anthropic 的未来意味着什么？假设股价不崩盘，这笔突如其来的财富，可以帮助 Anthropic 员工购置房产，也能拿出一大笔新财富捐赠给各类公益项目，比如虾类福利保护。但反直觉的一点是：这笔财富，也可能让他们离开这家给自己带来财富的公司。

这些员工还有另一个去向：跳槽到其他 AI 实验室。有多起从业者从一家 AI 公司跳槽至另一家的案例，目的是分散自己手中 AI 企业股权的持仓。这样一来，就算最后赢得 AI 竞赛的不是 Anthropic 而是 OpenAI，他们依然能够收益。如果大量研究员流失，对 Anthropic 绝非好事。这家公司之所以能走到今天，低人才流失率是关键原因之一。能否留住员工，是 Anthropic 上市之后投资者重点观察的一大问题。

items.author: Liam 'Akiba' Wright
items.content:
Quick Take
- Sygnum expects crypto carry trades that buy spot and short futures to earn more than Treasury bills on average in 2027.
- The bank cited 67 consecutive days of negative Bitcoin funding in 2026 and expects demand for leverage to return.
- If about $360 billion rotates from Nasdaq stocks into crypto, Sygnum sees crypto market value rising over 60% and Bitcoin nearing $128,000.
Sygnum expects crypto carry trades to earn more than Treasury bills on average in 2027, according to its annual Sygnal outlook released Nov. 19.
The bank also pointed to a recovery in Bitcoin funding rates and futures premiums, citing 67 consecutive days of negative Bitcoin funding in 2026.
The bank expects renewed demand for leverage to keep funding rates and futures basis mostly positive in 2027, even after the Federal Reserve raised its policy-rate target range to 3.75%-4% in September.
How Bitcoin carry earns a spread
The trade pairs a Bitcoin purchase with a short futures position. If the two positions are sized to offset each other, a rise in Bitcoin helps the purchase and hurts the short. The trader seeks to earn a premium on dated futures or collect funding payments on perpetual futures.
With a dated futures contract, the gap between the futures price and the spot price is called the basis. When the contract trades above spot, the trader can buy Bitcoin at the lower price and sell futures at the higher price, and the two prices converge at expiry.
Perpetual futures have no expiry, so their funding payments recur while positions are open. When funding is positive, longs pay shorts, and shorts pay longs when it is negative. The 67-day streak Sygnum cites describes how long funding stayed negative, when traders shorting perpetuals would have faced a funding cost.
The Treasury-bill comparison asks what the same capital could earn in short-term US government debt. The Fed’s policy rate sets the context for short-term rates.
In Sygnal Six, the bank estimates that if about $360 billion, or 0.75% of Nasdaq market value, moved into crypto, total crypto market capitalization could rise more than 60% and Bitcoin could reach a new high near $128,000.
Those two forecasts sit alongside six others on token value accrual, Bitcoin in strategic reserves, stablecoins in correspondent banking, tokenization, prediction markets and AI demand.
Fabian Dori, the bank’s chief investment officer and the report’s lead author, said investors should look beyond price to fundamentals.
Mostly positive funding rates and futures premiums in 2027 would support Sygnum’s case for a carry recovery. The test is whether the resulting average return clears Treasury bills.
items.title: A Bitcoin trade that doesn’t need prices to rise could beat Treasury bills in 2027

items.author: Jose Antonio Lanz
items.content:
In brief
- Citi’s November agreement treats activity by third-party AI agents as customer-authorized, even if credentials are leaked or an agent ignores instructions.
- PNC updated its rules Wednesday, while Citizens warned customers about AI-agent activity; JPMorgan and Bank of America had already tightened policies.
- Federal rules still restrict when banks can hold consumers liable for genuinely unauthorized electronic transfers, regardless of contractual wording.
Citi has updated its online banking terms to make customers responsible for the actions of third-party AI agents accessing their accounts, including when an agent leaks their credentials and someone else uses them to get in.
The change, reported by TechCrunch Wednesday, makes explicit how the bank intends to handle an increasingly awkward question: Who pays when software handling your money makes a mistake?
Under Citi’s new terms, actions taken using credentials supplied to an outside agent are treated as authorized by the customer, even if the tool ignores instructions, exceeds its permissions, or shares those credentials with another party.
Citi says it has no obligation to investigate whether the agent followed the customer's original prompts, subject to applicable law.
A Citi spokesperson told TechCrunch that the November revision clarifies the risks of sharing banking credentials or granting outside tools account access. The provision does not apply to AI agents offered by Citi itself.
Banks tighten the rules on AI access
Citi is not acting alone. JPMorgan and Bank of America announced similar policies in October, while Citizens Bank warned customers this week by email that they could be responsible for what their AI assistants do.
PNC also changed its digital agreement on Wednesday. Its rules distinguish bank-approved connections, which can provide limited access, from handing an agent unrestricted access to an account.
The move follows a banking security scare from October 22. Major banks had detected AI agents logging into customer accounts, sometimes taking steps that appeared to go beyond their users' instructions, and executives said they struggled to determine which agents had been properly authorized.
An AI agent differs from a conventional chatbot because it can act on a user's behalf, potentially navigating websites, accessing financial records, or initiating payments. That makes a mistaken instruction or compromised login more consequential than a bad answer about a bank balance.
The Office of the Comptroller of the Currency has since issued AI examiner guidance that addresses outside agents, payment controls, and human approval. The framework is nonbinding and does not itself create new requirements for banks.
A banking agreement cannot erase federal protections
Citi's language does not automatically eliminate consumer fraud protections. Under U.S. federal consumer protection rules, banks generally must investigate unauthorized electronic transfers and limit customers' financial liability for fraud. Those protections cannot simply be waived through a banking agreement, although their application to transactions performed by customer-authorized AI agents remains less clear.
The Consumer Financial Protection Bureau says banks cannot use agreements to waive those legal protections, although the rules distinguish theft by an outsider from transfers actually authorized by a customer or someone given access.
Whether a particular AI-related loss qualifies as unauthorized depends on how the transaction occurred.
PNC's updated agreement takes a stricter operational approach: Customers may use certain connection methods approved by the bank, but cannot give third-party AI agents their passwords or one-time security codes, and agents generally cannot initiate payments unless PNC expressly permits it.

Binance’s $6.5B freeze order, Hong Kong ‘suspicious’ of HYPE: Asia Express
Binance obtains court orders freezing assets stolen in October’s hack. Hong Kong warns citizens about Hyperliquid, and Thai police arrest four foreigners linked to a crypto scam.
Binance obtains $6.5B global freeze order, plans to expand throughout Asia
Binance has secured a $6.5 billion worldwide freezing injunction from the Abu Dhabi Global Market Courts as it seeks to recover assets stolen in its record Oct. 29 hack.
The court orders target unidentified perpetrators of the attack and are intended to help issuers, exchanges and other partners freeze and return stolen assets,
The orders can be served via blockchain, allowing legal notices to be delivered to wallet addresses rather than through traditional channels. Market participants will also be notified of updates to a “living list” of 26,000 wallet addresses identified as holding stolen assets.
Despite losing billions in the hack, Binance’s APAC head SB Seker told Reuters this week its finances are sound and it plans to expand throughout South East Asia.
“We have ongoing conversations with at least five or six markets ... three of which are in quite mature stages,” he said. Binance currently has operating licenses in 15 markets.
Source: Binance
HONG KONG
Hong Kong adds Hyperliquid to list of ‘suspicious’ crypto platforms
Hong Kong’s Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) added decentralized perps exchange Hyperliquid to its Alert List. The SFC said Hyperliquid lacks a license to operate in the city and is suspected of actively marketing its services to the region’s public.
The SFC is now officially suspicious of 69 platforms.
More Hong Kong news
The Hong Kong Monetary Authority and Swift will explore linking the HKMA’s market infrastructure, Project Ensemble, with Swift’s ledger, for cross-border payments using tokenized deposits in multiple currencies.
SINGAPORE
Singapore settles $77.5M tokenized bill sale with wholesale CBDC
The Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) issued 100 million Singapore dollars ($77.5 million) in tokenized bills on Nov. 6, with banks using wholesale central bank digital currency (CBDC) to pay for them. Five banks submitted bids totaling more than twice the amount on offer, MAS said Thursday. The four-week bills mature on Dec. 4.
MAS issued the bills directly on the Singapore Dollar Test Network. That gives borrowers an asset they could pledge as collateral for loans on the network, the central bank said.

items.author: Oluwapelumi Adejumo
items.content:
Quick Take
- California sued OpenAI over more than 80 alleged AI security incidents, accusing the company of ignoring warnings and inadequate safeguards.
- Prosecutors allege OpenAI prioritized profits and rapid development over safety as experimental agents accessed external systems.
- The state seeks court-ordered changes to OpenAI's internal testing, while the company argues it is being unfairly singled out.
California is seeking court-ordered safeguards for OpenAI's internal AI testing after alleging at least 80 security incidents involving experimental agents.
Attorney General Rob Bonta filed the lawsuit on Nov. 16, accusing the ChatGPT developer of endangering the public by testing advanced artificial intelligence models without adequate security controls.
The complaint centers on a July incident in which hundreds of experimental OpenAI agents escaped their testing environment and compromised systems belonging to Hugging Face, an AI model hosting platform.
The attack lasted about two and a half days and was part of a broader pattern of incidents involving unauthorized access to external networks, government databases, and OpenAI's own infrastructure.
Bonta said:
“OpenAI's actions escalated real-word cybersecurity risks, threatening the safety, health, and well-being of society.”
The lawsuit names OpenAI Foundation and OpenAI Group PBC as defendants and alleges violations of California's Unfair Competition Law and public nuisance provisions.
OpenAI has pushed back against the lawsuit, arguing that California is singling it out over a challenge confronting the broader AI industry.
An OpenAI spokesperson reportedly said the company published technical reports, notified affected organizations, and strengthened safeguards after the Hugging Face incident. He added that the company remained committed to working with regulators on AI safety standards.
California alleges OpenAI ignored repeated security warnings
In its complaint, California accused OpenAI of prioritizing rapid model development over safety despite knowing its experimental systems could bypass restrictions and access external networks.
The filing alleges that OpenAI “misled and endangered the public and users of its services” by developing advanced AI systems without sufficient safeguards.
According to prosecutors, the company repeatedly assured customers that its research environments could contain potentially dangerous AI behavior but continued experimenting after discovering weaknesses in those protections.
Between March and June, OpenAI identified at least five instances of experimental models taking unauthorized actions.
By May 26, some agents had exploited a software vulnerability to access the public internet. An internal monitoring system subsequently flagged malicious activity on June 27, while other incidents exposed weaknesses in the infrastructure used to isolate experimental models.
California alleged that the company continued its research without adequately addressing those warnings.
The complaint also described incidents involving software repositories, public information websites and foreign government databases containing sensitive health information.
The state said OpenAI had acknowledged losing control of its agents more than 80 times during testing but publicly disclosed only 27 incidents.
Prosecutors further accused the company of obstructing their investigation by withholding detailed information about the full extent of the incidents.
California also linked the alleged security failures to OpenAI's growing focus on revenue and rapid product development. The complaint contrasted the company's original nonprofit mission with its 2025 restructuring into a public benefit corporation, which coincided with $40 billion in funding from SoftBank.
Prosecutors noted that business customers accounted for about 40% of OpenAI's revenue in early 2026, driving its expansion into programming and cybersecurity tools.
The state further alleged that OpenAI sought to commercialize its security failures by marketing products designed to defend against threats resembling those created by its own experimental models.
California seeks judicial oversight of OpenAI's internal testing
California wants a San Francisco Superior Court judge to compel OpenAI to address unsafe conditions in its model development, training and evaluation operations.
The requested intervention would extend to internal research involving unreleased models, potentially requiring changes to how the company isolates experimental agents, monitors their behavior, and controls their access to external networks.
The complaint identifies inadequate monitoring, weakened model safeguards, and failures to contain agents within secure testing environments among the practices it seeks to address.
California also seeks an injunction preventing OpenAI from engaging in practices found to constitute unfair competition.
Beyond operational changes, the state is requesting $2,500 in civil penalties against each defendant for every proven violation of the Unfair Competition Law.
It also wants restitution for affected parties and the surrender of gains tied to unlawful conduct, with the amounts to be determined in court.

items.content:
In brief
- Anthropic opened at $111.50 but retreated to $97.17 by market close, still 17% above its IPO price.
- Nvidia's post-earnings slump and an AMD short-seller report weighed on chipmakers, while Microsoft, Oracle and other AI-related stocks fell.
- Nvidia, Google, AMD and other AI giants have agreed to buy $26 billion in Anthropic shares through a separate, conditional private placement.
Anthropic made stock market history Thursday, raising $81.34 billion in the largest initial IPO share sale ever. But Wall Street's response was considerably less enthusiastic than the demand for the Claude developer's shares.
The stock opened at $111.50 on Nasdaq under the ticker ANT, a 34% premium over its $83 offering price, briefly pushing the company's fully diluted valuation past $2 trillion.
The rally faded quickly, however, with shares dropping toward $93 before closing today at $97.17.
Did you know?
You can now act on the news you read: Go long or short Anthropic with perpetual futures, all from your Decrypt Money Account.
The offering involved 980 million shares and surpassed SpaceX's original $75 billion IPO in June. As Decrypt previously reported, SpaceX's expanded final offering reached $86.25 billion, meaning Anthropic has not surpassed that completed deal.
Investors initially welcomed the listing, sending technology stocks higher before the opening bell. By the afternoon, however, the Nasdaq Composite was down 2.06%, the S&P 500 had fallen 1.9%, and the Dow Jones Industrial Average was off 2.17%.
AI stocks fall despite Anthropic's strong debut
The selloff extended across the AI supply chain. A Thursday afternoon market heatmap showed Nvidia falling 3.4%, Broadcom losing 2.07%, and memory chipmaker Micron slipping 2.17%. Microsoft was down 1.97%, while cloud infrastructure and software provider Oracle declined 2.97%.
AMD was among the hardest hit, down 7.73% in the day, although its decline had a separate catalyst. Reuters reported that the chipmaker came under pressure after investigative outlet Hunterbrook disclosed that its affiliated investment fund had taken a short position in the company.
The picture was not uniformly negative. Palo Alto Networks rose 6%, CrowdStrike gained 2.24%, and Intel added 2.25% in the same snapshot. The divergence shows that investors were distinguishing between companies rather than selling every technology stock indiscriminately.
The broader weakness comes as investors question the cost of building AI infrastructure and the returns companies can generate from that spending. Nvidia's latest earnings beat expectations, but uncertainty following Jensen Huang's resignation has continued to weigh on the semiconductor giant.
Anthropic also faces an expensive expansion. Its IPO disclosures detailed approximately $900.9 billion in infrastructure and computing commitments extending through 2045, alongside another $150 billion to $175 billion in estimated payments under less precisely defined arrangements.
"Anthropic's record-breaking IPO has failed to rekindle enthusiasm for tech stocks," Joe Maher, market economist at Capital Economics, told Reuters.
Nvidia and AI infrastructure stocks face a reality check
Nvidia's weakness was notable given its latest results. The chipmaker reported $115.8 billion in quarterly revenue on Tuesday, up 103% from a year earlier, and forecast stronger-than-expected sales for the following quarter.
Even those numbers failed to erase concerns over the departure of longtime CEO Jensen Huang after allegations of extramarital affairs and possible leaks of corporate secrets and the sustainability of the AI spending boom.
The pressure also reached companies that rent out computing capacity. Neocloud operators CoreWeave and Nebius fell 5.0% and 7.8%, respectively. Software companies were weak as well: Salesforce declined 3.17% and Adobe lost 2.03% in the afternoon heatmap. From chips and data centers to enterprise software, the losses extended beyond any single corner of the AI trade.
Anthropic's IPO prospectus shows how closely these companies are tied together. Nvidia and Google each committed roughly $10 billion to a conditional private share placement alongside the IPO.
AMD agreed to invest $2.5 billion; Broadcom, Micron and Microsoft committed $1 billion apiece; and TSMC pledged $500 million. The $26 billion placement is separate from the public offering. Several of these investors are also key suppliers or infrastructure partners in the AI ecosystem.
That creates a central question for investors: How much of the money flowing into AI companies will ultimately translate into profitable demand for chips, cloud capacity and software?
Anthropic's blockbuster debut demonstrates demand for its shares, but Thursday's broader decline shows that Wall Street is not ready to extend that confidence to every company financing or supplying the AI boom.

items.author: Cointelegraph by Nate Kostar
items.content:
MoonPay seeks US bank charter for stablecoin, custody services
MoonPay’s proposed national trust bank would offer stablecoin issuance and redemption, reserve management and digital asset custody under federal oversight.
Crypto payments firm MoonPay has applied for a US national trust bank charter to offer stablecoin issuance and redemption, reserve management and digital asset custody services.
According to an OCC filing, MoonPay submitted its application on Tuesday to establish MoonPay National Trust Bank, a non-depository institution headquartered in Miami Beach, Florida. The proposed bank would not accept traditional deposits or issue loans.
MoonPay already provides stablecoin issuance infrastructure to businesses, including support for branded digital dollars. If approved, the charter would allow its proposed banking subsidiary to provide stablecoin and custody services under federal supervision.
The application comes as US regulators prepare to implement the GENIUS Act, which takes effect on Jan. 18, 2027, and establishes federal standards for stablecoin issuers, including reserve backing and redemption requirements.
With the filing, MoonPay joins several crypto and payments companies seeking federal trust bank charters, including Rain, Modern Treasury and Block. Coinbase’s charter took effect earlier this month, while Circle received final OCC approval in July.
The rise in crypto firms applying for federal trust bank charters has drawn opposition from community banks. In October, the Independent Community Bankers of America sued the OCC, arguing that the regulator exceeded its authority by allowing non-depository trust banks to conduct activities traditionally associated with commercial banks.

items.author: Jake Harrison
items.content:
Skyrocketing borrow rates are proving an insufficient incentive to free up liquidity in DeFi giant Sky’s stUSDS market, with founder Rune Christensen reportedly making up approximately half of the borrowed funds.
The market, on which liquidations are paused, has been at full utilisation for several days, leaving USDS depositors unable to withdraw their funds.
Consequently, the cost of borrowing USDS via stUSDS has spiked to 25% APY, up from just 5% last month, and may hit 50% within days.
Without the threat of liquidation, the borrowers needn’t fear, unless Sky’s DAO governance steps in which, given who a large portion of the loans belong to, seems unlikely.
That said, the SKY token, collateral against which stUSDS deposits are borrowed, is down over 20% in the past 24 hours, possibly anticipating sales to free up funds for repayment.
Christensen calls the worries about Sky “overblown” and stresses the protocol is strong. He does however recognize there are “questions about stUSDS” and that they will be addressed soon.
Read more: Wallet tied to Sky founder borrowed $1M days before his company collapsed
DeFi insiders aren’t worried about the health of the wider protocol, though.
Former Maker DAO delegate “PaperImperium” estimates that, even at max (50%) borrowing cost, “it would take several years to be in danger” and that only stUSDS holders would suffer a loss.
Similarly, former Aave delegate Marc Zeller says there’s “nothing wrong” and that the stUSDS product is Christensen’s “private credit line to fund his pet projects segregated from the main saving yield.”
While there may be limited contagion risk, with little incentive to repay, it doesn’t look like significant repayments are imminent.
Even when a small amount is repaid, the slack is picked up by MEV bots, maxing utilization once more.
Read more: Aave snubs Sky’s USDS as collateral and 3 ‘underperforming’ chains
Exit strategy
The stUSDS/USDS pool on decentralized exchange Curve Finance, which was set up a year ago to provide “supporting liquidity” to stUSDS holders, has shown volatility in the stUSDS/USDS exchange rate over the past week.
The pool’s $2 million of liquidity is currently made up of over 90% stUSDS, leading to the price divergence.
Prior to current developments, the stUSDS/USDS exchange rate was around 1.08, but the chart currently shows trading around par, with one particularly painful wick down to around 0.3.
Coincidentally, Curve Finance founder Michael Egorov previously pulled a similar strategy, borrowing multimillion sums of various stablecoins against his governance tokens, resulting in a liquidation cascade and plummeting CRV price in 2023.
Read more: Curve Finance founder Michael Egorov hit amid $22M CRV liquidation cascade
North Korean hackers also using Sky
While the stUSDS supply of $160 million is not to be sniffed at, it’s dwarfed by Sky’s overall stablecoin supply of $6.5 billion between USDS and legacy DAI.
These tokens maintain their dollar value via the protocol’s peg stability module (PSM), a 1:1 stablecoin exchange which has caught presumably unwanted attention.
CoinDesk reports that over half a billion dollars of illicit transactions have flown through the PSM over the years, including over $100 million tied to North Korean hackers.
With US authorities enthusiastically taking to freezing stablecoins in response to October’s Binance hack, some began to worry about the risk to pooled DeFi assets should the contracts holding commingled illicit funds be frozen.
Read more: LIVE: Binance says it’s yet to open up more token withdrawals
Possibly out of an abundance of caution, a Poloniex-labelled wallet reportedly converted $1.5 billion of USDS and sUSDS via Sky’s PSM, depositing the USDC into Aave.
Sky has played down the threat, noting that front ends block sanctioned entities and stressing that the funds flagged by CoinDesk “represent roughly 0.03%” of the almost $1 trillion of volume the PSM has processed to date.

items.author: André Beganski
items.content:
In brief
- Blockstream Research Director Jonas Nick and researcher Mikhail Kudinov published a security analysis of SHRINCS, an emerging frontrunner for a post-quantum signature scheme in Bitcoin.
- SHRINCS leans on Bitcoin’s battle-tested SHA-256, but combines a compact, efficient “stateful” path.
- Nick warns wallets must automatically enforce the stateless fallback to prevent catastrophic user error, though heavy stateless use could bloat the chain and raise fees.
Blockstream Research Director Jonas Nick, with Mikhail Kudinov and collaborators, published a security analysis on Thursday for SHRINCS, advancing an emerging frontrunner for a post-quantum signature scheme in Bitcoin.
“We need all the possible feedback—engineers, cryptographers, protocol developers,” Kudinov, a post-quantum cryptography researcher at Blockstream, said in reference to a draft of SHRINCS’ Bitcoin Improvement Proposal (BIP). “There are a lot of things to check, test, complain about, or praise."
Notably, SHRINCS is a hash-based signature scheme that leverages SHA-256 to anchor its security in battle-tested primitives that are already used by Bitcoin, representing a conservative effort to minimize the proposal’s trust assumptions.
Did you know?
You can now act on the news you read: Go long or short Bitcoin with perpetual futures, all from your Decrypt Money Account.
That said, the scheme comes with trade-offs, most notably by introducing potential security vulnerabilities at the implementation level if misused. The scheme combines two spending paths: a small, more efficient stateful signature option and a larger, more costly stateless path with fewer security risks on the implementation side.
Although stateful signatures are compact, preserving Bitcoin’s ability to process transactions efficiently, a user can trigger a critical failure—where an attacker can forge a signature for that address and steal funds if a one-time state is accidentally reused. Because SHRINCS’ stateful path relies on one-time keys that can only safely sign a single transaction, wallet developers must carefully track each key’s state.
Navigating human error
“It needs to be impossible for the user to behave in a way that this catastrophic event happens,” Nick told Head of MARA Foundation Isabel Foxen Duke during a recent appearance on MARA Foundation TV. “Wallet developers need to deal with this stateful component correctly.”
According to Nick, for SHRINCS to work safely in the real world, its specification and corresponding wallet implementations must automatically enforce the stateless path fallback in any situation where a state counter could possibly be compromised.
While some users might gravitate toward stateless signatures out of caution, Nick warns that widespread adoption could bloat the blockchain and drive up fees across the network.
Bitcoin’s current ECDSA signatures are typically 71 bytes long (and Taproot Schnorr signatures are 64 bytes). Under SHRINCS, stateful signatures are anywhere from 548 to 4,619 bytes, while stateless ones are 5,777 bytes. That said, optimizations of both signature paths have been accelerating with the support of AI-based research, Nick noted.
“We don’t know what the fee market will look like once we have these very big signatures,” he said. “And it’s not just the fee market, it’s also just fewer transactions fit into a block, meaning fewer people can use Bitcoin. And I think this changes the value proposition of Bitcoin.”
As the SHRINCS working group—which includes researchers backed by nonprofits including Brink and OpenSats—continues to refine the proposal’s specification, Blockstream researchers stress that getting the cryptographic foundation right is only half the battle.
Whether the broader Bitcoin ecosystem is ready to embrace SHRINCS’ inherent trade-offs will depend heavily on feedback from the network’s stakeholders in the months ahead. Meanwhile, Nick and Kudinov are requesting review of the proposal and the security analysis.
André Beganski is a Senior Content Manager at MARA Foundation, producing content on topics including the intersection of quantum computing and cryptography. He has previously worked for Decrypt.

items.author: Cointelegraph by Jona Jaupi
items.content:
Hyperliquid Anthropic futures priced within 1% of Nasdaq opening price
Hyperliquid traders priced Anthropic futures within 1% of the stock’s Nasdaq opening price, as trading surged ahead of the AI company’s IPO.
Anthropic perpetual futures on Hyperliquid were priced within 1% of the company’s Nasdaq opening share price Thursday, shortly before the stock began trading.
Anthropic shares opened at $111.50, up 34.3% from the company’s $83 initial public offering (IPO) price, according to several data dashboards. The opening price valued the Claude AI chatbot maker at around $2 trillion.
Just before trading began, Anthropic futures on Hyperliquid’s trade.xyz market were priced at $110.48, according to Senpi at around 4:44 pm UTC. That was just $1.02, or 0.91%, below the stock’s opening price.
The massive debut once again puts crypto’s growing pre-IPO futures market in the spotlight, especially as exchanges compete to attract traders who want to bet on major companies before their shares begin trading on Wall Street. SpaceX’s debut earlier this year also drew interest from crypto traders betting on its stock price through crypto futures.
Perpetual futures allow traders to bet on whether prices will rise or fall without owning the underlying shares, and unlike traditional futures they have no expiration date and can trade around the clock — including before a company goes public.
Anthropic trading accelerates on Hyperliquid
Trading on Hyperliquid was especially strong just before Anthropic shares opened, with the contract on trade.xyz recording $545.7 million in trading volume over 24 hours and $303.3 million in open interest (OI), according to Senpi data.
The contract was also trading at a 2.58% premium to its oracle price, the same data showed.
This interest had been growing for weeks, according to a Thursday report from crypto research firm Block Scholes, which found that daily trading volume for Anthropic futures on Hyperliquid averaged $75 million since Nov. 5, up from $7 million in September.
Traders also appeared to be betting on Anthropic’s stock rising, according to Token Terminal data, which showed that 5,567 traders held long positions in Anthropic futures on Hyperliquid on Wednesday, compared with 1,996 holding short positions.
Open interest in Anthropic perpetual futures on Hyperliquid reached a record $186 million on Nov. 18. Source: Token Terminal
OI across Anthropic futures markets on Hyperliquid also reached a record $186 million on Wednesday. Of that, $86 million came from trade.xyz contracts, while Entropy.io accounted for about $100 million.
Still, Anthropic futures made up just 1% of Hyperliquid’s total trading volume and accounted for only 3% of the increase in non-crypto trading since September, the Block Scholes report found.
Related: SpaceX tokenized IPO campaign draws $557M on Binance ahead of debut
Binance leads Anthropic futures volume
Binance recorded about $741 million in Anthropic perpetual futures trading over 24 hours, compared with $195 million on OKX, according to DefiLlama. Entropy’s Anthropic market, which also runs on Hyperliquid, recorded about $80 million.
Those three exchanges recorded $214 million, $34 million and $110 million in OI, respectively. Across 15 Anthropic perpetual futures markets, OI came in at a combined $520.4 million as of 4:50 pm UTC.
Anthropic shares were trading at $98.49 as of 5:43 pm UTC on Thursday, down about 12% from their $111.50 opening price but still nearly 19% above the $83 IPO price.
Anthropic joins Saudi Aramco and SpaceX as one of just three companies to debut on public markets with a trillion-dollar valuation.

items.author: Oluwapelumi Adejumo
items.content:
Quick Take
- Bullish added DRW, Flow Traders, SoFi and Superstate to its tokenized stock coalition, expanding membership to 12 firms.
- Tokenized shares can move between approved wallets, but trading across brokerages and exchanges remains restricted.
- The coalition aims to establish common trading standards as Bullish prepares to acquire Equiniti in January 2027.
Bullish has added four major financial firms to a coalition seeking to make tokenized stocks easier to trade across platforms.
The crypto exchange and transfer agent Equiniti announced on Nov. 17 that DRW, Flow Traders, SoFi and Superstate had joined the Issuer Token Coalition, bringing its membership to 12 companies.
The group, which also includes the New York Stock Exchange, is developing common standards for issuing, transferring and trading shares represented on blockchain networks.
Its latest expansion brings together institutional trading firms, liquidity providers, financial services companies and tokenization specialists to address a persistent obstacle in the emerging market: investors can hold real company shares onchain but cannot freely trade them across different platforms.
Why tokenized stocks remain difficult to trade
Bullish's own shares illustrate the problem. The company allows eligible shareholders to convert their BLSH holdings into tokens on Solana, where they can hold them in personal wallets or transfer them directly to other approved investors.
However, both parties must be registered with Equiniti, which maintains Bullish's official shareholder records, while their wallets must pass compliance screening.
According to Bullish's shareholder guide, decentralized exchange trading remains unavailable, and investors seeking to trade their shares on the New York Stock Exchange must return them to the traditional system.
Moving tokenized shares to another brokerage or trading venue also requires that platform to support the security, verify the investor, and recognize the ownership recorded by the transfer agent.
These restrictions have largely confined tokenized shares to arrangements established by their issuers and service providers.
The coalition intends to address those barriers through common technical standards, liquidity arrangements and infrastructure connecting traditional financial markets with blockchain networks.
Flow Traders, which provides liquidity across conventional and digital asset markets, said the initiative would help establish conditions for reliable trading, including outside traditional market hours.
Superstate already operates a model demonstrating how those connections can work.
In September 2025, Galaxy Digital introduced tokenized GLXY shares on Solana through an arrangement involving Equiniti and Superstate.
Under the structure, shareholders can move conventional Galaxy shares through Equiniti to Superstate, receive corresponding tokens in approved wallets and reverse the process to return their holdings to a brokerage account.
Bullish is pursuing a broader integration of these capabilities through its planned acquisition of Equiniti.
In its Nov. 18 earnings report, the company maintained its expectation that the transaction would close in January 2027, bringing the transfer agent responsible for shareholder records under common ownership with its exchange.
The acquisition would also give Bullish access to Equiniti's relationships with thousands of corporate issuers as it seeks to expand stock tokenization.
Meanwhile, the coalition's next phase will focus on liquidity mechanics, technical architecture and commercial arrangements needed to connect issuers, investors and trading venues.
items.title: Bullish recruits Wall Street heavyweights to solve tokenized stocks’ biggest trading problem

items.author: Decrypt Staff
items.content:
In brief
- Visa, Mastercard and JPMorgan Chase said customer data was exposed after hackers breached third-party vendors, with a ransomware group called n0n claiming responsibility.
- All three stressed their own networks and payment systems weren’t compromised: Visa said no card numbers were affected, Mastercard cited a “limited” subset of benefit-program cardholders, and JPMorgan flagged marketing data like names and emails.
- It caps a jittery week of tech failures and an AI-fueled cyberthreat surge.
Three of the biggest names in payments, Visa, Mastercard and JPMorgan Chase, disclosed that some of their customers’ data was exposed after hackers breached third-party vendors, the latest jolt in a week of tech failures that has left Americans uneasy about the systems underpinning daily life.
The data was leaked Thursday by a ransomware group, according to a report from The Wall Street Journal. Crucially, all three firms said their own networks were not breached and that no payment systems were compromised.
A Visa spokesperson said no payment data such as card numbers was affected and that the incident involved a third-party service provider in the Asia-Pacific region.
Did you know?
You can now act on the news you read: Go long or short Anthropic with perpetual futures, all from your Decrypt Money Account.
Mastercard said a “limited amount of information from a subset of cardholders enrolled in a specific benefit program” was exposed, with no impact on its payment network.
JPMorgan said attackers targeted outside service providers and likely accessed marketing data, potentially including customer names and email addresses, with no disruption to customer services.
A ransomware group calling itself n0n claimed responsibility, according to cybersecurity firm SOCRadar. None of the three companies named the breached vendor.
Earlier in the week, JPMorgan customers hit problems accessing accounts and sending payments, which the bank attributed to a software update, and the issue spread into broader complaints about other banks.
Paired with the FAA temporarily grounding flights and an earlier Microsoft outage that locked people out of email, the week stoked unusual public anxiety about the fragility of critical tech. JPMorgan was explicit that the data leak had “no connection” to the earlier service disruptions.
For crypto users, the breach lands squarely within a growing danger that customer data, not just funds, is the soft underbelly of finance.
AI has supercharged both the scale and sophistication of cyberattacks, and 2026 has brought a steady drumbeat of data exposures. The record $6.3 billion Binance hack, tied to North Korea, laid bare how aggressively state and criminal actors are targeting financial infrastructure, while a wave of breaches has hit crypto firms through third-party vendors, echoing the vendor weakness at the center of this latest incident.
The payments giants have all leaned deeper into crypto and stablecoins this year, from Visa and Mastercard’s settlement programs to JPMorgan’s growing digital-asset footprint, making their security posture increasingly relevant to the onchain economy they’re racing to join.
For now, the firms say the damage is contained, but the episode adds to a mounting sense that no institution, however large, is immune.

items.author: Cointelegraph by Nate Kostar
items.content:
Trump’s SEC nominee Johnson backs formal rulemaking for tokenized stock trading
Former CFTC Commissioner and Democrat Kristin Johnson and ex-SEC aide Steven Levine appeared before lawmakers Thursday.
President Donald Trump’s nominees to fill two vacancies at the US Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) faced questions about investor protections, regulatory oversight and financial innovation during a Senate confirmation hearing Thursday, including scrutiny of the agency’s approach to tokenized securities.
Kristin Johnson, Trump’s Democratic nominee, backed formal rulemaking to address concerns about the agency’s exemption for tokenized stock trading.
“I feel strongly that regulation is made better through the notice and comment period,” Johnson told the Senate Banking Committee in response to Democratic Senator Angela Alsobrooks. She added that she would welcome the opportunity to address issues covered by the exemption through that process.
The SEC’s Sept. 17 exemption lets qualifying platforms trade blockchain-based versions of US-listed shares without registering as securities exchanges under certain conditions. The order took effect immediately and invites comments on possible changes.
Johnson, a former Commodity Futures Trading Commission commissioner, appeared alongside Republican Steven Levine, a former aide to SEC Commissioner Mark Uyeda. If confirmed, they would bring the five-member commission to four members, with three Republicans and one Democrat.
The hearing comes as the SEC has scaled back enforcement activity and pursued regulatory changes intended to accommodate digital assets, including efforts to facilitate tokenized securities that have drawn scrutiny from lawmakers and market participants.
Companies reject tokenized stock listings
The measure has drawn objections from publicly traded companies, with 67 opposing the tokenization of their shares on the OKXICE platform, according to a Nov. 5 public notice.
Johnson also cited concerns about Anti-Money Laundering and Know Your Customer compliance, noting that objections to the exemption extended beyond investor protection.
Levine, meanwhile, said he had not closely studied the innovation exemption but understood it to be time-limited and include investor protections. He emphasized that Congress had authorized the SEC to grant exemptions from federal securities laws when doing so serves the public interest and remains consistent with investor protection requirements.
He pointed to exchange-traded funds as an example of financial innovation that initially developed through regulatory exemptions before becoming subject to broader agency rules.
Related: Robinhood’s Tenev warns US tokenization uncertainty deters ‘serious assets’
Senate weighs bipartisan SEC appointments
If confirmed, Johnson would become the SEC’s only Democratic commissioner, a development some in the crypto industry believe could strengthen the agency’s approach to regulation.
“Crypto isn’t a partisan issue, and the rules that come out of a bipartisan commission will stand on firmer footing,” Jessica Martinez, US policy director at digital asset infrastructure company Fireblocks, told Cointelegraph.
Martinez added that even minority commissioners can influence policy by challenging proposals and pushing for unresolved issues to be addressed before rules are finalized.
Senators have until noon Friday to submit additional written questions to the nominees, with responses due by 5:00 pm ET on Nov. 24, according to the committee’s closing remarks.
The nominations could then advance to a committee vote before being considered by the full Senate. Both nominees would require Senate confirmation before taking their seats at the SEC.

items.author: Oluwapelumi Adejumo
items.content:
Quick Take
- FTX-linked Anthropic shares sold for nearly $2 billion would now be worth $40.7 billion at the AI company's $1.5 trillion IPO valuation.
- The investments, originally worth $550 million, were liquidated to fund creditor repayments following FTX's collapse.
- The sales helped repay customers but transferred nearly $39 billion in potential upside to investors who acquired the shares.
Anthropic shares owned by FTX and sold for around $2 billion would now be worth more than $40 billion as the artificial intelligence company finally goes public on Nov. 19.
The difference highlights one of the largest missed windfalls from FTX's bankruptcy, after administrators and US authorities liquidated investments originally made by Sam Bankman-Fried and two former executives.
Anthropic priced its IPO at $83 per share on Nov. 18, valuing the Claude developer at approximately $1.5 trillion ahead of its Nasdaq debut on Thursday. The offering raised a record $81.3 billion.
FTX creditor Sunil Kavuri noted the disparity, calculating that holdings linked to the collapsed exchange are worth more than $40 billion today, compared with about $2 billion recovered through earlier sales.
The investments used funds tied to FTX's multibillion-dollar fraud, which ultimately led to Bankman-Fried's conviction and imprisonment.
How FTX's $500 million investment became a $40 billion missed windfall
Bankman-Fried invested $500 million in Anthropic's Series B fundraising in 2022 through Alameda Research, FTX's sister trading firm, using customer funds diverted from the exchange.
The investment initially gave FTX a 13.56% stake in the AI startup, and subsequent fundraising diluted that ownership to approximately 7.8% by early 2024.
Following FTX's collapse in November 2022, bankruptcy administrators moved to liquidate the investment alongside other assets to fund creditor repayments.
In February 2024, Kavuri and other creditors challenged the proposed sale procedures, arguing that the investment had been purchased with misappropriated customer deposits and questioning whether the bankruptcy estate had the right to sell it.
The court subsequently authorized the sales after a compromise with the objecting customers.
FTX sold approximately 29.5 million Anthropic shares for $884 million in March and disposed of its remaining 15.1 million shares for $452 million in May, generating approximately $1.34 billion.
The transactions represented a substantial return on the original investment. However, Anthropic's subsequent growth dramatically increased the value of those shares.
After adjusting for Anthropic's September 2026 stock split, the 44.5 million shares sold in 2024 would represent approximately 445.4 million shares, worth $37 billion at the IPO price.
The remaining $3.7 billion comes from investments made by former FTX executives Nishad Singh and Caroline Ellison, who invested $40 million and $10 million, respectively, in Anthropic's Series B round.
The US government forfeited its holdings during criminal proceedings.
Anthropic's IPO filing revealed that the company repurchased those shares from the government for about $627 million in October 2025, then resold them to nine investors at the same price.
The Justice Department subsequently transferred the proceeds to the FTX bankruptcy estate for creditor recoveries.
Combined, the two transactions generated approximately $1.96 billion from investments originally totaling $550 million. At Anthropic's IPO price, those holdings would be worth $40.7 billion.
FTX creditors have since received substantial repayments, with major customer classes reaching 105% of their allowed claims by July 2026.
However, those claims were valued in dollars at the time of FTX's November 2022 collapse.
The Anthropic sales provided cash for those repayments, but they also transferred the investment's future upside to new shareholders. Investors who retained the shares purchased from FTX in 2024 would now hold stock worth nearly 28 times their original purchase price.

items.author: Gino Matos
items.content:
Quick Take
- Talos measured average cross-venue funding spreads of 23% for the 10 largest equity perpetuals and 12% for the 10 largest crypto perpetuals.
- Nvidia longs paid more funding on Binance over seven days and more on a Hyperliquid market over 30 days in a Nov. 18 snapshot.
- A trader hedging across venues still faces trading fees and has to keep both positions adequately margined.
In a Nov. 17 analysis, trading infrastructure firm Talos found that the funding-rate spread for perpetual futures of the same tokenized stock across venues averaged 23% for the 10 largest equity perpetuals by open interest.
Funding is the recurring payment traders exchange on opposite sides of a perpetual future. In Talos’s comparison, rates diverged even when the two contracts tracked the same asset, so the costlier venue one stretch can be cheaper another.
In a snapshot of settled Nvidia funding on Nov. 18, market data tracker PerpDexList showed cumulative settled funding for a long position at 0.3907% of notional over seven days on Binance.
Meanwhile, the equivalent figure for the Nvidia contract on Hyperliquid was 0.3347%.
Over 30 days, Binance longs paid a net 0.5834% and trade.xyz longs on Hyperliquid paid 0.6855%, showing what was paid on each contract before trading fees and any gains or losses on the position.
Cumulative funding paid by longs, as a percent of notional, in a Nov. 18, 2026 snapshot at 18:36 UTC. On Binance and trade.xyz, respectively, seven-day payments were 0.3907% and 0.3347%. Over 30 days they were 0.5834% and 0.6855%.
Binance Research’s Nvidia figures showed a 0.12% funding rate paid by longs on Nov. 16, after three smaller positive settlements on Nov. 12.
Talos puts open interest above $11 billion in November for perpetuals linked to traditional assets such as equities, indexes and commodities. That was about 18% of total open interest across the major venues it studied.
Binance and Hyperliquid together held roughly 77% of that segment, with shares of 39% and 38%, respectively.
Why funding differs for the same stock
To keep perpetual futures prices near the assets they track, venues use recurring payments between traders on either side. When funding is positive, traders betting on a rise pay those betting on a fall, and shorts pay longs when it turns negative.
The exchange can charge a separate trading fee for funding, so the amount transferred depends on the position’s notional value, which can exceed the collateral a trader has put up.
When demand pushes the contract above its reference price on one venue, the premium used to calculate its funding can rise there. A second venue can have a different order balance and a different reference price, even though both contracts track Nvidia.
Under Binance’s TradFi contract rules, funding generally settles every four or eight hours, and the interest-rate input for stock contracts is zero. Outside the underlying market’s hours, Binance can derive the index from prices in its own order book and apply smoothing.
In October, Binance said it would omit disrupted overnight observations from one funding calculation for its US equity perpetuals after connectivity problems.
The Hyperliquid funding rules call for hourly transfers. In the builder-deployed markets that include trade.xyz, the premium compares the midpoint of two order-book prices, measured for a specified trade size, with the market’s reference price, known as an oracle price.
The trade.xyz funding formula applies a multiplier before the hourly payment. Separate books, reference prices, and funding inputs can all contribute to the spread. Talos’s comparison gives the size of the gap, while the exchange rules show how a gap can arise.
Why the funding gap on perpetual futures can persist
A trader could short the contract where funding pays more and go long on the other venue, since holding offsetting positions reduces exposure to stock price moves.
The funding difference can still shrink or reverse before a trader closes the positions, and the two futures prices can move apart while the stock exposure is hedged.
In its Nov. 18 snapshot, PerpDexList put the median cost of opening a $100,000 Nvidia position on trade.xyz at 2.25 basis points over the previous 24 hours, including the taker fee and slippage, the difference between the expected and actual execution price.
A trader also has to account for the other venue, the cost of closing both positions and the possibility that limited depth makes a larger order more expensive. Castle Labs’ venue study measured fees and slippage at multiple trade sizes and sampled weekday and weekend sessions separately for traditional-asset perpetuals.
If one position moves against the trader, gains on the other side sit in a separate account. The losing leg can still be liquidated if its margin falls too low.
A wider funding gap gives traders a reason to take the other side, but they need enough return to carry both positions through those risks.

items.author: Jose Antonio Lanz
items.content:
In brief
- Bitcoin traded near $62,640 Thursday as Anthropic’s record-setting debut failed to lift the broader stock market.
- Bitcoin’s 50-day EMA sits below its 200-day EMA; the chart does not establish when the crossover occurred. RSI is at 21.3 and ADX at 41.2.
- A break below $62,019 exposes $60,000, while a recovery must first clear resistance near $66,512.
Bitcoin traded around $62,640 Thursday, down 0.6% on the day, as Anthropic's record-breaking stock market debut failed to reverse a broader selloff in risk assets.
The cryptocurrency has lost roughly 28% from its late-September peak near $87,000, and doesn’t seem on its way to stop anytime soon.
Anthropic began trading on Nasdaq under ANT after pricing 980 million shares at $83, raising $81.34 billion. Its stock opened at $111.50, up 34%, and briefly pushed the Claude maker's market value past $2 trillion, as Decrypt reported.
The enthusiasm stopped at Anthropic's ticker.
Did you know?
You can now act on the news you read: Go long or short Anthropic with perpetual futures, all from your Decrypt Money Account.
By 12:18 p.m. ET, the Nasdaq Composite was down 1.55%, the S&P 500 had lost 1.59%, and the Dow was off 2.03%. Investors remain concerned about expensive AI infrastructure and whether the spending will deliver adequate returns. The weak reaction beyond Anthropic undercut hopes that a blockbuster IPO could revive appetite for beaten-down technology stocks.
Crypto's weakness predates Thursday's listing. U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs have shed roughly $2.9 billion this month, including $306.4 million Wednesday, amid rising Treasury yields and expectations of further Federal Reserve rate hikes.
Some traders argue the IPO has diverted capital from crypto, but that remains unproven. As Decrypt previously noted, Bitcoin and AI stocks have declined together, suggesting a wider retreat from risk rather than a simple rotation into Anthropic shares.
Bitcoin price analysis: EMAs, RSI, and the levels to watch
Bitcoin's daily chart remains decisively bearish. At around $62,640, BTC trades below both its 50-day and 200-day exponential moving averages (EMAs), with the shorter average beneath the longer one.
This is a bearish alignment commonly associated with an EMA-based death cross. Traditionally, a death cross occurs when the 50-day simple moving average crosses below the 200-day average, signaling deteriorating shorter-term momentum. The EMA variation responds more quickly to recent prices. The crossover was confirmed today.
Momentum reinforces the picture. The relative strength index, or RSI, reads 21.3, well below the 30 threshold traders associate with oversold conditions. That can precede a relief rally, but oversold assets can keep falling.
The average directional index, or ADX, stands at 41.2. ADX measures the strength of a trend, not its direction, with readings above 25 generally indicating a strong trend. Here, the negative directional indicator exceeds its positive counterpart, confirming sellers have the advantage. A high ADX reading alone does not mean a reversal is imminent, even with RSI already deep in oversold territory.
Bitcoin has also been making lower highs and lower lows since September, with November's sharp drop slicing through several support levels. A bullish recovery would first need to reclaim $66,512, followed by resistance around $69,292 and $71,539. Above those levels, $73,785 and then $76,984 would present tougher tests of the prevailing bearish structure.
On the downside, the chart marks immediate support near $62,019, almost directly beneath the current price. A decisive daily close below that level could expose the psychological $60,000 threshold, followed by the chart's next Fibonacci extension around $56,841.
The RSI leaves room for a bounce, but the EMAs and ADX show how much work buyers still face. A move through $66,512 would open a test of $69,292; a close under $62,019 would instead put $60,000 back in focus.

items.author: Aaron Wise
items.content:
The European Central Bank (ECB) went looking for the AI industry’s missing debt and found $4.5 trillion, a tally 287% higher than the off-balance sheet commitments it found in 2025.
Off-balance sheet commitments for the industry include the years of promised payments that AI companies hope to fulfill for data center rentals, cloud computation, and chips.
In its Financial Stability Review published yesterday, one day before Anthropic’s $1 trillion blockbuster IPO, the ECB added up eight US tech firms’ off-balance sheet commitments.
Hidden, off-balance sheet commitments dwarf everything the companies report in formal, on-balance sheet liabilities like debt.
Hyperscalers, for example, turn clients’ long-term compute contracts — like Oracle’s $300 billion OpenAI deal — into collateral, allowing loans against those years of committed future payments.
“Such cash flow commitments are debt-like in economic terms, but they do not appear as liabilities on the balance sheets of hyperscalers under US accounting standards,” the ECB warned.
Signed, off-balance sheet leases not yet available for use
Indeed, under US accounting rules, a balance sheet only records a lease once the asset becomes available for use.
Purchase commitments that haven’t commenced live in footnotes and have ballooned over the past year.
The ECB’s tally covers Alphabet, Amazon, Meta, Microsoft, Nvidia, Oracle, Broadcom, and Anthropic — a broad review of the biggest AI names, including today’s newly-public Claude maker.
Read more: AI companies rush to borrow cash as stocks crash
The ECB’s report repeatedly flags circular financing among AI companies. “For example, chipmakers and cloud providers may invest in AI labs that, in turn, commit to purchasing their hardware and services”, ECB Vice-President Boris Vujcic explained.
US Fed also finds trillions in off-balance sheet AI debt
US Fed Governor Michael Barr independently counted over $100 billion of hyperscaler and GPU-maker stakes in AI labs and cloud startups, and called the pattern “circular financing.”
Moving cash around without true revenue from consumers or outside industries can misleadingly inflate top line numbers and forecasts for AI companies.
“The rapid shift towards debt finance invokes historical parallels with the dotcom and subprime bubbles,” the ECB warned.
Although its $4.5 trillion number is certainly new, the ECB wasn’t first to flag off-balance sheet commitments in the AI industry.
Indeed, the Fed’s stability report, out last Friday, tallied more than $1 trillion of signed but unstarted leases, and it added more than $2 trillion of take-or-pay contracts and guarantees at seven of the same firms.
According to Fed calculations, the “nominal value of these types of obligations, or off-balance-sheet liabilities, now exceeds $3 trillion.”

items.author: Cointelegraph by Nate Kostar
items.content:
Ethereum’s Glamsterdam upgrade could slip to May 2027 over compatibility concerns
Ethereum developers are weighing changes to gas pricing proposals that could disrupt existing smart contracts, after contacting at least 50 affected companies.
Ethereum’s Glamsterdam upgrade could be pushed back as far as May 2027 if developers decide to modify its specifications to address smart contract compatibility issues, according to discussions at Thursday’s All Core Developers meeting.
Glamsterdam is a planned Ethereum hard fork aimed at increasing the network’s capacity and efficiency. However, blockchain security firm ChainSecurity warned in October that proposed changes to Ethereum’s gas pricing could disrupt existing smart contracts and potentially expose them to exploitation, prompting developers to postpone the Hoodi testnet fork, originally scheduled for Oct. 26.
The concerns center on gas repricing proposals EIP-8037 and EIP-8038. Researchers identified 13 real-world examples of potentially affected contracts in October, while a November investigation examined eight smart contract invariants that could be disrupted by the upgrade.
During Thursday’s meeting, developers said the Ethereum Foundation, ChainSecurity and security firm Dedaub had collectively contacted at least 50 affected companies. Three projects were classified as high impact, with fixes completed or expected by mid-December, while medium-impact projects reported timelines extending to Jan. 10.
Developers debated whether to retain Glamsterdam’s existing specifications or modify them to reduce compatibility risks, as changes intended to protect some contracts could disrupt others.
“Every spec change could, again, break new invariants that we are not aware of breaking yet,” one developer warned during the meeting.
Under the current specifications, mainnet activation could come as early as mid-January 2027. However, waiting until January to decide could push activation to late February or early March, or April or May if modifications are adopted, and no decision has been reached yet.
Related: Vitalik ‘pivots’ ETH to store of value, crypto suffers after US midterms: Hodler’s Digest
Ethereum weighs accelerating post-quantum security
Separately, Ethereum’s next planned hard fork, Hegotá, could see its scope reduced as the network seeks to accelerate its transition to post-quantum cryptography.
During the meeting, developers considered postponing some Ethereum Improvement Proposals to prioritize post-quantum features, although several argued that reducing the upgrade’s scope would offer little benefit unless it also shortened the rollout timeline.
Developers also raised compatibility concerns over EIP-8151, a proposal designed to protect accounts migrating to post-quantum security. A preliminary review identified a potentially large number of existing smart contracts that could be affected by the changes, complicating the proposal’s inclusion in Hegotá.
No decision was reached on Hegotá’s scope, with client teams expected to submit their positions ahead of further discussions in two weeks.

Why higher rates could slow Bitcoin buying at treasury firms
A treasury company can have years of dividends covered and still struggle to sell new shares on terms that make another Bitcoin purchase worthwhile.
Rising US interest rates could slow buying by Bitcoin treasury companies long before they have trouble paying their bills.
Strategy raised $244.7 million by selling common stock in the week ended Nov. 15. It spent $206.3 million of the proceeds buying back preferred shares and $33.4 million on 485 BTC.
At the time, its US dollar assets covered more than three years of preferred dividends and debt interest at current payouts. When Treasury bills pay more, investors can demand a higher yield to buy newly issued preferred shares.
For common stock, StoneX analyst Mark Palmer watches how much investors will pay above the value of the Bitcoin each share represents. At a premium, a company can issue stock and buy enough Bitcoin (BTC) to leave shareholders with more BTC per share. However, as that premium narrows, so does the gain.
