items.author: Decrypt Agent
items.content:
In brief
- The International Organization of Securities Commissions warned that a sufficiently capable quantum computer could undermine the cryptography that protects financial markets.
- IOSCO said such machines don't yet exist, citing conservative estimates of 2030 to 2035, while some industry participants urged firms to plan for five years.
- It flagged blockchains as particularly hard to migrate, with post-quantum signatures 35 to 40 times larger and upgrades requiring hard forks.
Financial markets, including crypto, need to start preparing now for quantum computers capable of breaking the cryptography that secures them, according to the world's main forum for securities regulators.
A "sufficiently capable" quantum computer could undermine widely used public-key cryptography that supports critical functions across financial markets, the International Organization of Securities Commissions (IOSCO) said in a report published on Thursday. The cyber readiness challenge posed by quantum computing "is immediate and requires action," it said.
"Practical quantum computers capable of compromising widely used cryptography do not yet exist, but the scale and duration of the transition mean the financial sector should start preparing today," IOSCO Board Chair Jean-Paul Servais said in a statement.
The 63-page report cited conservative estimates that such machines could emerge between 2030 and 2035. Several industry participants consulted by IOSCO went further, arguing that firms should prepare for the possibility that they arrive within five years, potentially accelerated by AI.
Blockchains face a heavier lift
IOSCO said the migration may be particularly challenging for blockchains, because cryptography is embedded in their core architecture and any change requires coordinated action across decentralized networks. Public blockchains such as Ethereum, Solana and Tron rely heavily on elliptic curve cryptography to verify identities and validate transactions, and a powerful enough quantum computer could derive private keys from exposed public keys, a scenario known as "Q-Day."
Swapping in quantum-resistant signatures comes at a cost. Signatures under ML-DSA-44, a post-quantum standard from the U.S. National Institute of Standards and Technology, are about 2,420 bytes, roughly 35 to 40 times larger than today's 64-byte elliptic curve signatures, the report said. It cited evidence from a quantum-resistant Solana testnet that saw throughput fall by about 90% when post-quantum signatures replaced existing ones.
Because the cryptography sits in transaction formats and consensus rules, replacing it requires hard forks, and decentralized networks have no way to force quick adoption, making migration "slow and fragmented," IOSCO said. Accounts and smart contracts still controlled by vulnerable keys could stay exposed after a network adds quantum-resistant options, and the path to quantum resistance for Bitcoin wallets remains uphill.
Wallet makers face their own trade-offs. SHRINCS, the leading candidate for a post-quantum Bitcoin signature scheme, offers "stateful" signatures that are about 10 times smaller but can expose funds to theft if keys are reused beyond a set signing budget, Trezor CTO Tomáš Sušánka has said. Trezor is considering making the larger, safer stateless option the default, and hardware wallets will also need post-quantum cryptography for firmware and device authentication, he added.
The report distinguished "on-spend" attacks, in which an attacker races to exploit a public key revealed by a pending transaction, from "at-rest" attacks on keys left exposed for longer. Dormant or abandoned coins pose a particular problem where their holders can't move them. Crypto firms have formed a quantum alliance as some 6 million BTC sit in exposed addresses, and Bitcoin developer Cory Fields has proposed "quantum landmines" to make attacks on such coins costly.
Layer-2 networks are not insulated either. Optimistic rollups could face forged signatures during their dispute windows, typically seven days on Ethereum, and many zero-knowledge rollups use SNARK proofs that rely on elliptic curves. Hash-based STARK proofs are more resistant, but a rollup is only as safe as the layer-1 contracts, bridges and governance keys it depends on, the report said.
Developers are already working on fixes. Researchers have proposed several ways to make Bitcoin quantum-safe, StarkWare has shown a quantum-safe Bitcoin transaction, and Ethereum co-founder Vitalik Buterin has said the network is betting its future on quantum resistance.
'Crypto-agility'
IOSCO said firms should migrate to post-quantum cryptography and build "crypto-agility," the ability to update cryptographic systems without major redesign. Quantum key distribution could complement those measures on selected high-security channels, it added.
Most preparations across financial markets are still at an early stage, focused on awareness, governance, training and identifying vulnerable systems, according to the report, which drew on a March 2026 survey of members of IOSCO's Fintech Task Force and discussions with experts. Some respondents described "quantum-procrastination," in which firms put off action while waiting for clearer regulatory signals or wider adoption.
No surveyed jurisdiction reported operational deployment of quantum computing in regulated financial services. The watchdog also urged regulators to act against "quantum washing," in which firms overstate the role, maturity or performance of quantum technology. IOSCO said it will treat quantum as a priority in 2027, focusing on raising awareness across the financial ecosystem.
Quantum hardware is advancing quickly. IBM has claimed a trusted quantum advantage, and Google has said it has cracked some of the field's biggest bottlenecks.

items.author: Cointelegraph by Christina Comben
items.content:
Ethereum’s new DeFi security tool raises questions over censorship
Phylax’s system lets decentralized protocols block potentially harmful transactions, but raises questions about potential censorship and Ethereum’s concentrated builder market.
Phylax’s new security system could help decentralized finance (DeFi) protocols stop malicious transactions before they settle.
That may bolster crypto’s defenses against North Korean hackers and United States-sanctioned actors, but it may also introduce a way to freeze smart contract functions without explicitly giving anyone the power to do so.
And that’s the kind of control that raises concerns the system could end up as a centralized tool for law enforcement rather than decentralized finance.
“The question is not just whether there is risk, but if it’s acceptable risk,” says Stefanie Boss, co-author of research on censorship resistance and compliance behavior in Ethereum’s consensus mechanism.
“In this case, I’d lean toward that it is acceptable, as the goal is to make the network safer and more aligned with the network and application values,” she says.
A security mechanism with a potential freeze risk
Announced on Nov. 10, Phylax’s integration with block builder Titan Builder, allows Ethereum applications to define rules that exclude transactions that may produce harmful outcomes during block construction.
Titan, which Phylax says produces one in every two Ethereum blocks, checks transactions against those rules before including them in its blocks.
The idea is to prevent exploits from settling rather than relying on monitoring systems or emergency interventions after an attack has begun. “Our mission: stop users from losing money to hacks and errors in DeFi,” the announcement said.
Related: Fears of AI-driven DeFi hack epidemic overstated for now — but not for long
In a blog Phylax uses the scenario of a vulnerable vault that could mistakenly release $1 million to a user whose shares are only worth $1,000. With the system in operation, a circuit breaker could cap the amount leaving the vault in a single transaction, preventing the funds from being drained.
Similar safeguards could also potentially limit losses in major hacks like the $6.3 billion Binance hack or the $380 million Bitget exploit, where malicious actors drained exchange wallets and were able to move large amounts of crypto through decentralized protocols.
Phylax says hacks should not settle. Source: Phylax Systems.
While preventing malicious transactions would be a win for the crypto space, digital assets lawyer Gabriel Shapiro warned that applications using the system could become effectively freezable if builders stopped providing the required attestations.
He explained that smart contracts can be configured to reject transactions unless they are included in blocks from builders that have performed the required security checks. If those builders stopped providing attestations, protected functions could keep rejecting transactions until they resumed.
Related: DeFi TVL drops 39% in 2026 amid market downturn and record hack activity
Phylax founder and chief executive Odysseas Lamtzidis says protocols can avoid that risk by allowing transactions to go through even when the system’s security checks are unavailable.
“The sane default we provide and suggest to protocols is a fail-open behavior,” he tells Magazine.
But that safeguard is optional, leaving individual protocols to decide how much priority to give security over availability. “Some protocols might choose to prioritize safety over liveness,” Lamtzidis says.
He also says protocols can decide whether their smart contracts are immutable or can be changed through governance.
Shapiro says fail-open protections should be mandatory and changes to the safeguards should be subject to time delays to prevent protocols from removing them immediately.
Ethereum’s builder concentration problem
There is also a broader concern about whether the system could reinforce Ethereum’s already heavily concentrated block-building market.
Fan Zhang, an Ethereum researcher, says Phylax’s technology is only becoming practical now because of that concentration. “We finally have a way to implement this effectively,” he says, “but sadly only because of how centralized Ethereum’s builder market has become.”
Zhang says Phylax’s approach has “appealing security benefits, especially in the age of AI bots being able to find bugs faster than ever.”
But he warns that introducing additional code at such a critical point in transaction processing creates new failure modes, including implementation errors and builder signing-key theft, loss or impersonation.
“I think the community is very concerned about centralized builders and is making efforts to address them. So I’m concerned that these efforts may undermine each other,” he adds.
Related: FBI blames North Korea for record $6.3B Binance hack
Ethereum researcher Sen Yang tells Magazine, “If major protocols rely on a small number of builders for security enforcement, this could give those builders a competitive advantage and further exacerbate market concentration.”
Phylax announces its circuit breaker system. Source: Phylax Systems
He says Ethereum’s proposed enshrined proposer-builder separation (ePBS) upgrade, slated for inclusion in the upcoming Glamsterdam upgrade, may reduce reliance on third-party relays, “but it does not directly address builder market concentration.’’
Yang says transactions excluded by dominant builders could still be included by non-censoring builders, potentially causing delays rather than permanent exclusion.
Where does security become censorship?
Phylax argues that its system does not introduce a new authority over Ethereum transactions because applications themselves define the rules. The technology is “explicitly opt-in,” Lamtzidis says.
He compares the checks to conditions already written into smart contracts. “It’s no different than a ‘require()’ statement,” he says. “Censorship implies arbitrary decision-making or coercion.”
Zhang makes a similar distinction between applications voluntarily filtering transactions and external parties imposing censorship. “Applications willingly signing up for filtering is fine, as a user can walk away from such applications,” he says. “It’s externally forced censorship that’s the problem. That’s where I’ll draw the line.”
Boss says rules targeting a transaction’s outcome are less concerning than those targeting who is making it. “In this case, it is also result-driven, which is often considered less risky,” she says.
She considers the security objective legitimate, arguing that “the harm of those hacks is much higher than the harm of this type of exclusion.”
But she warns that rules could also be used to enforce sanctions or politically motivated exclusions.
“It is important to ensure that there are proper safeguards in place to make sure that these rules will remain fair and designed for security,” she says.
Magazine: Banks are banning AI agents over security... and competition concerns

items.author: Liam 'Akiba' Wright
items.content:
Quick Take
- Bitcoin rebounded from roughly $62,000 on Nov. 15 and 18, with the second session closing nearer its low.
- Glassnode’s relative loss reading reached levels seen near past lows, while CryptoQuant put 30-day net losses at $8 billion.
- Easing daily losses, a narrower Coinbase discount and sustained spot buying would strengthen the case that the rebound can hold.
The Bitcoin rebound from just above $62,000 was weaker the second time. The bounces came on Nov. 15 and 18, and the second session closed closer to its low. By then, a CryptoQuant measure showed the steepest losses since mid-August on older coins that moved. The next question is whether spot buyers can absorb that pressure for more than a day.
The Nov. 15 and Nov. 18 lows were $62,006 and $62,063 on CoinGlass’s Binance BTC/USDT daily candles, which start at midnight UTC. Bitcoin finished the first day at $65,351 and the second at $63,068.
In a Nov. 19 analysis for CryptoQuant, Woominkyu put 30-day net realized losses at $8 billion, well short of two earlier 2026 readings. Glassnode’s Nov. 17 report found losses at levels it had seen around past market bottoms when measured against a year’s worth of realized profits.
How the two loss gauges work
Both gauges start from an estimate of what investors gained or lost when coins moved. Glassnode compares realized losses with profits taken over the previous year. On that relative measure, the weekend selloff reached readings Glassnode associated with lows in 2018, 2020, 2022 and early 2023.
CryptoQuant’s series tallies profits and subtracts losses over a rolling 30-day period. On that measure, net losses hit $30 billion on Feb. 20 and $18 billion on June 30. Even with a smaller monthly reading, losses were concentrated in the latest selloff. The four days from Nov. 15 to Nov. 18 produced $5 billion in net losses, more than half the 30-day figure.
A burst of losses can look extreme against a year’s profits while the month’s net dollar loss stays smaller than it was in a previous selloff. Earlier gains still in the 30-day window can offset part of the recent losses. Neither gauge sets a threshold Bitcoin has to reach before the price can stabilize.
Woominkyu’s Nov. 19 CryptoQuant Quicktake lists net losses of $30 billion on Feb. 20, $18.4 billion on June 30, and $8.4 billion in its latest reading.
That pressure reached coins that had been idle for more than 155 days. CryptoQuant’s long-term-holder spent output profit ratio fell to 0.73 on Nov. 18, its lowest since mid-August, according to Woominkyu’s analysis. The reading implies roughly 73 cents in value when those outputs moved for each dollar of value when they were created. The series measures only older outputs that moved, including transfers that can occur without a trade on an exchange.
The spot market gave a more tentative signal. Glassnode saw Bitcoin briefly trade at a premium on Coinbase around the Nov. 15 low before slipping back to a discount. Woominkyu put the Nov. 18 reading for CryptoQuant’s Coinbase Premium Index at minus 0.14%. That index compares the dollar price on Coinbase with the USDT price on Binance. It helps gauge relative buying pressure across venues using prices alone.
Glassnode also reported that buyer-initiated spot trades outweighed seller-initiated trades over the day leading into its Nov. 17 snapshot. Sustained buying in completed spot trades would give the rebound more weight. Standing buy orders can still be withdrawn.
What would make the Bitcoin rebound hold
The New York Fed calendar scheduled initial jobless claims and the Philadelphia Fed manufacturing survey for 8:30 a.m. ET on Nov. 19. Because the reports share a release time, a move in the two-year Treasury yield could reflect either or both. The yield was 4.80% on Nov. 18, unchanged from the day before in the Treasury’s daily series.
Bitcoin can respond quickly to a change in rate expectations. Daily on-chain readings take longer to fill in. If Bitcoin’s price stays above the recent lows, watch whether daily net losses ease and the older-coin ratio moves back toward 1, where spending and creation values are equal. A narrower Coinbase discount alongside sustained spot buying would add evidence that buyers can absorb the supply. A daily close near $62,000 while losses deepen and the discount persists would leave the rebound on weaker footing.

--- Top Comments ---

[xorcist]: Isn't this what something like psnup (or pdfbook or similar tools) does, which you probably already have at your command line, at least if you've printed things like man pages or latex documents? It was pretty normal to use and saved lots of paper when you could print your documentation 8-up, but it let you rotate, scale and place each page arbitrarily. I believe users of the more GUI-oriented operating systems like Windows or Mac eventually got it integrated in their printing dialo...

[staplung]: For the curious, the generalized process of reordering and potentially rotating pages so that when printed and folded (and optionally gathered into signatures) is called impositioning. There is specialized software with a variety of options that will do this for an input document. Bookbinder JS is a nice web-based tool that will do this for you too, though I'm not sure it covers the exact folding algorithm described in this article.  https://momijizukamori.github.io/bookbi...

[addled]: My high school geometry teacher would let us use an index card of notes during exams. She had a student years prior show her this folding technique and asked if he could use it for the test.  Not only did she allow it, but she taught it to every class going forward for those that wanted to put in the extra effort. My buddies and I spent so much time trying to come up with modifications to use more area of the page.  Some of them even worked!

[baud9600]: I’m bothered that this piece doesnt mention pocketmod, which I think is where the folding idea came from? The fold image looks very similar! I used this 20 years ago and still do sometimes:  https://pocketmod.com/

[bthallplz]: I really love this form factor and how inexpensive it could be to print small books. Does anyone have any suggestions for ways to estimate how many words could fit per page while still being decently readable, depending on different fonts a person uses? A step further: a markdown editor with a preview of how the printed out document would read would be nice.

阿里电话会：或下调20GW数据中心目标及资本开支，预计2028年下半年现金流转正

BlockBeats 消息，11 月 19 日，阿里巴巴管理层在第二财季财报电话会上表示，受全球不同区域算力政策变化影响，公司长期 20GW 数据中心建设目标存在下调可能，整体资本开支计划也可能相应降低。同时，阿里将加快以平头哥为核心的国产算力供应链建设。管理层预计，2027 年及 2028 年上半年将是本轮算力投入的高峰期。在国产算力供应链持续放量、并按既定节奏推进的假设下，公司有望于 2028 年下半年实现现金流转正。2028 年之后，随着国产算力供应链规模化扩张，阿里预计将逐步走过 AI 基础设施投入强度最高的阶段。

本季度，阿里资本开支为 505 亿元，低于上一季度的 677 亿元，但同比大幅增长，主要受到算力规模爬坡、芯片等组件价格上涨，以及增加 CPU 算力储备以应对 AI 智能体需求等因素推动。同期自由现金流净流出 345 亿元，去年同期净流出 218 亿元，主要原因是云基础设施投资增加。

增长目标方面，管理层表示，全球算力供应新规对明年产品和服务的影响仍存在较大不确定性，但国产算力推进进度超出此前预期。阿里给出的 2028 财年云业务增速目标为 30%—45%；随着 2028 自然年国产算力产品持续放量，云业务增速有望重新恢复至 50% 以上。公司同时重申，2030 自然年外部云收入目标为 1000 亿美元，长期利润率超过 20%。

本季度，阿里 AI、云与算力服务板块收入同比增长 53% 至 610 亿元，外部客户收入同比增长 64% 至 470 亿元，连续第十个季度加速增长。剔除算力设备解决方案后，外部客户经常性收入同比增长 67% 至 370 亿元。AI 相关产品收入达到 179 亿元，连续第十三个季度实现三位数增长。

Morning Minute is a daily newsletter written by Tyler Warner. The analysis and opinions expressed are his own and do not necessarily reflect those of Decrypt. And check out our daily news show 'FOMO HOUR' covering all of the top stories and market action.
GM!
Today’s top news:
- Crypto majors are flat ahead of ANT IPO, stocks up big; BTC at $63.8k
- ANT jumps to $105 on Hyperliquid pre-IPO debut, starting at $83
- Gemini ships Gemini 4 Neon, new top model; speculation of RSI
- Fed Governor Waller calls for 50 bps hike in December to “shock people”
- Variational announces $110M raise at $1.5B valuation
Gemini Tops the Benchmarks as Anthropic Prices at $83
Google shipped Gemini 4 Neon on Wednesday, its fourth frontier model release in three weeks, and on the eve of the heavily anticipated Anthropic IPO.
This isn’t just a normal model release. For one, it’s incredibly good. Neon posts 61 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index against 59 for Claude Opus 5.5 and 57 for GPT-6.2 Sol. It takes the Vals Index at 70.9%, AutomationBench at 56.3% against Opus 5.5’s 42.5%, and GraphWalks long-context retrieval at 95.2% against Opus 5.5’s 66.8%.
Beyond just the outperformance, Google has been releasing at a pace nobody else is matching. It dropped Argon in mid-October. Carbon on October 28. Hydrogen last week. Google owns its silicon, its data centers, and its distribution, and it is using all three to iterate faster than labs that rent compute. And it has some speculating that Google has already achieved RSI (recursive self-improvement), the final step ahead of super intelligence.
So Google has caught up at the top of the AI race. Just in time for the ANT IPO.
Anthropic will be priced at $83, 6.4% above the top of its $70 to $78 range, valuing the company around $1.5 trillion fully diluted. On the 825 million shares in the original terms, that’s roughly $68.5 billion raised, and about $94.5 billion counting the separate $26 billion private placement from its compute suppliers. It trades Thursday on Nasdaq as ANT. Notably, ANT has been trading on Hyperliquid in the $90-$100 range for the past week but popped to $105 this morning.
The valuation math is a 55% step-up from the $965 billion May round and about 25% below the $2 trillion Anthropic was reportedly chasing in September. Revenue ran $33.2 billion through nine months against $2.5 billion a year earlier, a 13x increase. Annualize that and $1.5 trillion is roughly 34 times sales.
That’s a steep raise given the macro backdrop and the Fed calling for more hikes for longer. AI stocks have been shaky over the past month and even moreso since Jensen Huang left Nvidia. Not the most confident market headed into the 2nd $1T+ IPO of the year.
So what does it mean for today’s price action? Personally, I expect a pop to the $95-$105 level that Hyperliquid has been pricing out for weeks, and it likely sees a spike higher. But there will be massive volatility, and it’s very likely to trade under that $83 level over the coming days and weeks. Especially given the new (surprise) headwinds from Google with its outperforming model.
We will find out soon enough. Good luck to everyone trading it today.

Investigation: Sky (Formerly MakerDAO) Peg Stability Module Processed $518M in Transactions Linked to Illicit Wallets, Including $101.9M Tied Directly to North Korean Hackers

According to CoinDesk, an investigation by crypto risk analytics firm Inca Digital found that the Peg Stability Module (PSM) of Sky (formerly MakerDAO) has processed $518 million in transactions involving 422 wallets linked to illicit activities—including hacks, phishing attacks, and sanctioned entities—with $101.9 million directly tied to North Korean hackers. Within 10 days following the 2025 Bybit hack, associated wallets converted $91.5 million in assets through the PSM.

Currently, Sky's PSM holds approximately $2.7 billion in USDC within a single Ethereum address; if Circle were to blacklist that address at the request of law enforcement, the entire reserve could be frozen, potentially impairing redemptions and the peg stability of DAI and USDS. In response, the Sky Frontier Foundation stated that the flagged transactions do not mean all funds were stolen assets, noting that the volume accounts for less than 0.06% of PSM's over $930 billion in cumulative volume and occurred almost entirely via third-party DEX aggregators rather than Sky's official website, which implements wallet screening. — link

items.author: Decrypt Agent
items.content:
In brief
- Binance has secured a $6.5 billion worldwide freezing order from Abu Dhabi courts against the unknown perpetrators of its October 29 hack.
- The order can be served via the blockchain and is backed by a constantly updated list of 26,000 wallet addresses holding stolen assets.
- About $2.85 billion linked to the hack has been frozen so far, and U.S. prosecutors have won authorization to seize or restrain $1.2 billion of the frozen funds.
Binance has secured a $6.5 billion worldwide freezing order against the hackers behind last month's attack on the exchange, which the FBI has blamed on North Korea.
The injunction was issued by the courts of the Abu Dhabi Global Market (ADGM) against the unknown perpetrators, Binance's lawyers at Gibson Dunn confirmed, according to City AM.
The order breaks new legal ground. It can be served directly via the blockchain, and market participants will be notified of a "living list" of 26,000 wallet addresses identified as holding stolen assets, Gibson Dunn partner Kendall Day said. That will enable "those assets to be frozen rapidly even as they are laundered at pace," Day said.
Binance has also secured proprietary injunctions and delivery-up orders, including against parties holding frozen assets who are not accused of wrongdoing, according to City AM. Decrypt has reached out to Gibson Dunn for comment.
"We will continue using every lawful tool available to trace, freeze and recover stolen assets, support our partners in returning funds where possible, and keep those assets out of the hands of the attackers," Dugan Bliss, Binance's deputy general counsel, said in a statement reported by Bloomberg.
Chasing the stolen funds
The FBI has attributed the October 29 hack to TraderTraitor, a group linked to North Korea, which has denied involvement. The attackers gained access after an engineer was phished through a fake job offer, according to Bloomberg. The Secret Service has joined the FBI's investigation.
About $2.85 billion in funds connected to the hack has been frozen, including by Ripple and World Liberty Financial, according to Bloomberg. Stablecoin issuers Tether and Circle froze $2.7 billion shortly after the attack, and the Justice Department said last week it had obtained court authorization to seize or restrain $1.2 billion of that.
The hackers have used thousands of wallets and multiple blockchains to launder the rest, and wallets linked to the hack began moving Ethereum again this week after two weeks of inactivity.
Binance has said it fully covered the $6.3 billion in customer assets affected and absorbed the losses itself.

Anthropic或面临巨额抛压，数十亿股将陆续解禁

BlockBeats 消息，11 月 19 日，据彭博社报道，Anthropic 上市首日允许创始人、员工及其他现有股东额外出售最多 3.16 亿股。未来数月，随着限售期分批届满，以及公司于 2027 年初公布 2026 财年业绩，数十亿股内部持股将陆续解除限售，后续买盘能否承接潜在供应成为市场关注焦点。

Anthropic 非创始人员工在首个交易日最多可出售个人持股的 10%，在 2026 财年业绩公布后可再出售最多 35%。不过，获准出售或股份解禁并不意味着股东必然减持，实际流入市场的股份数量仍取决于其出售意愿及届时股价。Anthropic 此次 IPO 最终定价为每股 83 美元，高于此前 70 至 78 美元的发行区间。按包含未归属股权激励在内的完全稀释股本计算，公司估值达 1.5 万亿美元。

彭博社评论员 Chris Hughes 认为，此次定价基本公允，但未给新股投资者留下明显折价。包括风险投资者 Jack Selby 在内的市场人士此前已警告解禁带来的供应压力，相关预期理论上已反映在发行价中；但若股东集中兑现收益，而承接资金不足，股价仍可能承压。与此同时，今年 6 月上市的 SpaceX 也将迎来现有股东减持窗口，两家公司的股份供应释放在时间上存在重叠。为筹集数据中心及 AI 基础设施建设资金，部分科技巨头也从回购股票转向增发融资，Meta 上月的股权融资即为一例。

高盛策略师预计，2027 年美国股票净供应量增幅或创 2000 年以来新高。不过，高盛认为，供给增加虽然会压制估值，但尚不足以终结美股牛市，因为科技巨头以外的其他行业回购活动仍然稳健。Anthropic 已向投资者表示，若条件允许，希望避免上市后短期内再次进行股权融资，更倾向于借助上市便利通过债务市场募资。面对庞大的 AI 算力基础设施支出承诺，其实际融资路径仍将取决于经营现金流与资本市场环境。

items.content:
Hong Kong adds Hyperliquid to list of ‘suspicious’ crypto platforms
Hong Kong’s securities regulator said Hyperliquid has no local license and may have promoted its trading services to investors in the city.
Hong Kong’s Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) added Hyperliquid, a decentralized exchange for perpetual futures, to its Alert List on Wednesday.
The SFC said Hyperliquid lacks a license to operate in the city.
The entry names both Hyperliquid and Hyperliquid Hong Kong, while identifying the exchange’s trading site. The SFC said it suspects Hyperliquid of running a trading platform in Hong Kong, claiming to run one there or actively marketing its services to the Hong Kong public.
The SFC’s list of suspicious virtual asset trading platforms now has 69 entries.
Cointelegraph contacted Hyperliquid for comment but did not receive an immediate response.
The Monetary Authority of Singapore added Hyperliquid to its Investor Alert List on June 26. The list includes firms that investors may mistakenly believe the central bank regulates. Hyperliquid said at the time that it never claimed to hold a Singapore license.
Related: Crypto.com to withdraw Hong Kong consumer app citing regulatory changes

items.author: Cointelegraph by Helen Partz
items.content:
GTA VI publisher racks up nearly 3x Nvidia’s tokenized stock volume
Tokenized Take-Two shares drew $249.5 million in DEX volume Wednesday, nearly three times the $88.1 million for tokenized Nvidia shares.
Tokenized shares of Grand Theft Auto VI publisher Take-Two Interactive recorded nearly three times the trading volume of tokenized Nvidia shares on decentralized exchanges (DEXs) as the blockbuster began its global rollout.
Trading volume for tokenized Take-Two (TTWO) shares surged 578% to $249.5 million on Wednesday, up from $36.8 million a day earlier, according to Token Terminal data. Tokenized Nvidia (NVDA) recorded $88.1 million in DEX volume despite ranking first by market cap at $399.4 million.
The surge made TTWO the most-traded tokenized stock tracked by Token Terminal that day, accounting for roughly 42% of the $590.7 million in DEX volume.
Tokenized stocks are blockchain-based assets that track the value of publicly traded shares, allowing investors to gain exposure through crypto trading platforms. Their onchain trading volumes do not represent transactions in the underlying shares on traditional stock exchanges.
Take-Two shares on the Nasdaq rose 6.2% to close Wednesday at $216.61, according to Yahoo Finance. Shares gave back some of those gains Thursday, falling 4% to $208 in premarket trading as of 7:02 a.m. ET.
GTA VI, which Citi analyst Jason Bazinet estimated cost about $1.4 billion to make, ends a 13-year wait for a sequel to GTA V. PlayStation and Microsoft’s Xbox both said it was the most preordered game in the history of their respective stores.
Backpack leads tokenized TTWO trading
Most of the tokenized TTWO trading was in a Solana-based asset offered by Backpack Securities, a platform operated by crypto exchange Backpack. The token accounted for about $239 million, or 96%, of the day’s trading volume.
Over the past 30 days, tokenized NVDA shares recorded about $2 billion in DEX trading volume, compared with $808.1 million for tokenized TTWO shares.
The GTA VI launch has also attracted crypto scammers. Blockchain security company Blockaid said in a Wednesday X post that it had flagged more than 8,800 GTA-themed tokens on Solana as malicious, suspicious or spam, alongside hundreds of social media posts promoting fake airdrops and preorders.
Separately, four US senators questioned the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) on Monday about potential gaps in investor protections and anti-money laundering safeguards under its new tokenized securities exemption.
Related: Fed’s Waller cites Binance hack in warning over tokenized finance
items.title: GTA VI publisher racks up nearly 3x Nvidia’s tokenized stock volume

items.author: Gino Matos
items.content:
Quick Take
- NYSE owner ICE is partnering with Trade[XYZ] to bring Hyperliquid-based perpetual futures to the US through a regulated trading venue.
- Trade[XYZ] controls 97.6% of HIP-3 trading volume, handling $4.9 billion daily, but its offshore liquidity will not automatically transfer to the US.
- ICE must attract enough buyers and market makers to build a liquid US market, with regulatory approvals and trading depth still uncertain.
Intercontinental Exchange (ICE), the New York Stock Exchange’s owner, is working with Trade[XYZ] to bring Hyperliquid-based perpetual futures to the US.
The proposed venue would have to attract its own buy and sell orders, Hyunsu Jung, CEO of Nasdaq-listed Hyperion DeFi, told CryptoSlate.
Jung said firms quoting on both the proposed US venue and existing overseas markets could help keep prices close if the venues match orders and handle funding similarly.
The amount a trader can buy or sell at those prices would depend on the orders available on the US market. Jung’s company builds on Hyperliquid and earns revenue from work in its ecosystem.
How a separate US market would work
ICE announced the agreement on Oct. 29 and said it would be the exclusive operator of the regulated markets, using a dedicated retail venue and clearing structure separate from its institutional futures business.
ICE also announced a minority investment in Trade[XYZ], subject to regulatory approvals, including approvals needed to support leveraged trading. ICE’s announcement sets out who would operate and clear the market, leaving the trading rules and exact order-book design unspecified.
Perpetual futures let traders take positions on the price of a reference asset through a contract with no set expiration date. Trade[XYZ] already offers contracts on equities, stock indexes, commodities and currencies to eligible customers outside the US.
ICE expects customers who pass identity checks to access the proposed market through participating futures brokers, formally known as futures commission merchants, and also expects its joint venture with OKX to help distribute the contracts.
That route depends on separate approvals for the venture’s broker-dealer and futures commission merchant businesses.
The existing HIP-3 design gives each builder-deployed venue its own order books and margining on Hyperliquid’s shared trading infrastructure.
In its November quarterly filing, Hyperion DeFi described ICE and Trade[XYZ]’s plan in the context of HIP-3, an optional extension that lets operators control access. The filing tied the plans it discussed to regulatory approvals, finalizing the extension, and making it available on the live network.
An order book records what buyers and sellers are willing to trade at each price, so a buy order posted outside the US would be available to traders on that book. To complete a trade on a separate US venue, a customer would need a matching order on the US book.
If a comparable contract traded at a higher price on one venue, a firm able to trade both could buy on the cheaper venue and sell on the more expensive one. Those trades would tend to bring the two prices closer.
A market maker that takes the other side of a customer’s trade in the US could manage some of the resulting exposure overseas if it can access both venues.
Jung said margin and leverage rules for futures broker accounts would help determine how much liquidity firms can provide. Margin is the collateral a firm sets aside to support a position, and the more collateral a trade requires, the more of a firm’s capital it ties up.
Trading is already concentrated
Trade[XYZ] recorded over $4.9 billion of the $5 billion traded across tracked HIP-3 venues in the 24 hours through Nov. 18, representing 97.6% of the total. EntropyIO, the next-largest venue by volume, accounted for 2.3%, according to UnderHyper’s venue breakdown.
UnderHyper’s measure of rolling dollar volume counts completed trades across the HIP-3 venues it tracks.
Jung attributed Trade[XYZ]’s lead to listing key markets early and making them available in the Hyperliquid interface traders already used.
ICE hopes to reach US customers through brokers and distribution partners, but the size of that customer base and how often it trades will become clear only if the US venue opens.
If the US venue opens, traders will be able to judge its liquidity by the gap between the best buy and sell prices and how much they can trade near those prices. The test for ICE will come when traders try to move a large position near the price they first saw.
items.title: NYSE owner targets Hyperliquid’s $5 billion trading boom, but the liquidity may not follow

美国成立「威胁阻断中心」，将联合交易平台与支付机构追踪诈骗资金

BlockBeats 消息，11 月 19 日，美国国土安全部与司法部于当地时间 11 月 18 日宣布启动「威胁阻断中心」（TDC），打击针对美国民众的网络诈骗和加密资产盗窃。该中心将为逾 30 家联邦机构及 440 多个州和地方合作单位提供共享的调查工具和情报。

调查人员将与加密货币交易平台、支付服务商和社交平台共享线索，以便拦截欺诈转账、冻结涉案资金或移除诈骗账号。执法部门将继续调查，并依法申请法院授权查扣资产。

TRM Labs 是该中心的主要私营部门合作伙伴，其 Ardence 平台将用于处理受害者报案、追踪加密资金并梳理犯罪网络。采购记录显示，TRM Labs 于今年 7 月获得约 9466 万美元的合同，履行期至 2027 年 8 月 29 日。

FBI 数据显示，2025 年共收到 181,565 起涉及加密货币的投诉，报告损失超过 110 亿美元，其中加密投资诈骗约占 72 亿美元。FBI 自 2024 年启动的预警行动已通知逾 8000 名受害者，估计帮助避免逾 5 亿美元的进一步损失。

Solana Unveils 2027 Roadmap, Doubling Compute Capacity and Cutting Unit Consumption by 80%

Following the Alpenglow upgrade, Solana core development team Anza has outlined its 2027 technical roadmap for Solana across four pillars: Performance (doubling network compute capacity and cutting compute unit consumption by 80% for token account transactions); Expressivity (adding vector processing for models running fully onchain, raising the per-transaction account limit from 64 to 96, and reading account data directly rather than copying it to reduce data movement per transaction); Market Structure (building on Alpenglow with faster block distribution and introducing Constellation for clearer ordering rules and greater validator competition); and Resilience (simplifying the protocol with fewer special cases to make future changes safer). — link

items.content:
Sky稳定币兑换模块被曝涉5.18亿美元非法关联交易，27亿枚USDC储备面临潜在冻结风险

BlockBeats 消息，11 月 19 日，链上风控机构 Inca Digital 的一份调查显示，Sky Protocol 的锚定稳定模块（PSM）曾处理 422 个与黑客、钓鱼活动或受制裁实体等有关联的钱包的交易，累计约 5.18 亿美元，其中 1.019 亿美元与朝鲜相关活动直接关联。这两项数字统计的是关联钱包经该模块进行的交易额，并不意味着所有资金均已被认定为赃款，也不代表 Sky 遭到攻击。

调查发现，在 Bybit 于 2025 年 2 月遭遇约 15 亿美元资产失窃后的 10 天内，曾收到相关被盗资产的钱包通过 Sky 的 PSM 完成了约 9150 万美元的交易。另一家链上调查机构 Nominis 应 CoinDesk 要求分析了涉及 320 多个链上地址的 560 多笔交易，也确认了相关钱包与朝鲜黑客活动的联系。

潜在冻结风险来自储备集中。PSM 为 Sky 旗下稳定币 DAI 和 USDS 提供兑换流动性，帮助维持美元锚定。调查称，相关储备约有 27 亿枚 USDC 集中在同一个以太坊地址。若 USDC 发行方 Circle 因法院命令或执法请求冻结该地址，正常储备也可能一并无法动用，导致模块的双向兑换中断，并给 DAI 和 USDS 的流动性及锚定带来压力。这是调查提出的风险情景，并非储备已被冻结。

Inca Digital 警告，即使储备未被冻结，交易所和机构合作伙伴也可能加强资金来源审查，或限制与 Sky 的业务往来。CoinDesk 举例指出，Galaxy Digital 持有价值约 1 亿美元的生息稳定币 sUSDS，而 Sky 生态内的 Grove 已向 Galaxy 提供 5 亿美元的信贷额度。Coinbase 则对相关 USDC 储备余额支付奖励，但其发言人表示，这些资产由客户自托管，Coinbase 无权调动。

原文链接 https://m.theblockbeats.info/flash/378225

Anthropic IPO获约5000亿美元认购需求，指数基金首月或买入2.77亿股

BlockBeats 消息，11 月 19 日，据《金融时报》报道，尽管不少投资者对 Anthropic 的高估值、巨额资本开支和模型同质化风险存有疑虑，他们仍将其视为一只「必买股」。Anthropic 将 IPO 发行价定为每股 83 美元，高于此前 70 至 78 美元的区间，发行规模也从原方案上限约 640 亿美元扩大至约 810 亿美元，完全摊薄估值约为 1.5 万亿美元。承销商据悉获得约 5000 亿美元的认购需求，但认购订单可能被高报，不能等同于上市后的实际买盘。

Anthropic 是首家登陆公开市场、业务聚焦前沿 AI 模型开发的大型公司。投资者此前可通过谷歌、亚马逊等公司间接参与这一赛道，但这与直接持有 Anthropic 不同。对基金经理而言，即便对发行价有疑虑，若不配置而股价随后大涨，也可能面临业绩落后于同行的压力。

指数基金可能带来另一批买盘。Intropic 估计，若 Anthropic 符合相关指数的纳入条件，指数追踪基金可能在上市首月分四次买入约 2.77 亿股，相当于扩大后基础发行股数的约 28%。对这些基金而言，是否买入取决于指数规则，而非对估值的判断。

上市后也可能出现较大卖盘。部分非创始人内部人士最多可从首个交易日起出售所持股份的 10%，合计约 3.16 亿股，按发行价计算价值约 260 亿美元。这些股份具备出售资格，不代表持有人已经卖出。若首日表现强劲，部分获配基金也可能选择获利了结。

此外，同步进行的 260 亿美元私募配售包含芯片、算力和晶圆代工供应商。这些战略投资方一边向 Anthropic 投资，一边也是其基础设施开支的受益方，买入动机与普通基金不同。此次 IPO 能以更高价格扩大规模，并不意味着上市后仍有同样强的买盘；真正的考验是，尚未获配的投资者是否愿意在更高价位继续买入。

items.content:
Anthropic前员工：Amodei曾谈公司未来可能比政府更强大，超级AI就像「魔戒」

动察 Beating AI 快讯，Anthropic 即将上市，不少员工有望一夜暴富。但《纽约时报》采访发现，一些人眼下更关心的是：如果公司率先造出超级智能，究竟会获得多大的权力？

《纽约时报》专栏作者 Jasmine Sun 在过去两年采访了数十名 Anthropic 创始人、员工和离职者。一位匿名离职员工透露，CEO Dario Amodei 曾谈到，Anthropic 未来可能比政府更有权势，因此需要与各个国家建立自己的关系。

另一位离职员工则用《指环王》里的「魔戒」比喻超级智能。谁先造出来，谁就可能掌握最危险的网络武器、治愈各种疾病的方法，以及一支不知疲倦的 AI 大军。如此强大的力量一旦集中在少数人手中，掌握它的人是否值得信任，就变得至关重要。

Amodei 对这场竞赛的态度也发生了明显变化。2022 年，他曾公开表示，Anthropic 不应该抢跑，也不该训练远比同行更大的模型。当年，公司甚至因为安全顾虑，暂缓向公众推出 Claude，随后 OpenAI 凭借 ChatGPT 抢占了市场先机。

如今，Amodei 认为 AI 竞赛已经无法阻止。如果 Anthropic 不率先研发出最先进的模型，其他公司也会继续推进。只有保持领先，Anthropic 才有足够的影响力，推动整个行业采用更安全的做法。

这种使命感也深入了 Anthropic 的招聘流程。公司有一道著名的面试题：如果为了 AI 安全放慢研发，导致你的股票价值归零，你还愿意在这里工作吗？研究团队甚至会拒绝技术能力出众、但不认同公司理念的候选人。

随着公司快速扩张，内部开始出现分歧。一些早期员工担心，新加入的销售和市场人员只是冲着高薪与股票而来，未必真正相信公司的安全使命。还有员工主张立即停止训练更强的 AI，即使 OpenAI 等竞争对手不会跟着停，但遭到 Amodei 否决。

Anthropic 即将通过 IPO 获得巨额资金，继续购买算力、研发更强的模型。与此同时，公司还在争取国会给予反垄断豁免，以便未来能够与其他美国 AI 实验室协调放慢研发。

Sweden’s H100 could tap Bitcoin trading pool to fund share buybacks
Shareholders will vote Dec. 7 on whether H100 can buy back up to 10% of its shares, potentially using a Bitcoin pool that lost about 30 BTC in Q3.
Swedish Bitcoin treasury company H100 Group said Thursday it could use Bitcoin from its trading pool to fund share buybacks if shareholders approve the plan next month.
The pool lost about 30 Bitcoin (BTC) in the third quarter and held 233.4 BTC as of Sept. 30, H100 said in its quarterly report. The company held another 3,243.4 BTC in its long-term treasury.
Shareholders will vote Dec. 7 on whether to authorize the board to buy back up to 10% of H100’s shares. H100 would pay shareholders in cash. New Swedish rules allowing companies on the NGM Growth Market to buy back their own shares take effect Dec. 5.
CEO Eirik Grøttum said in September that buybacks could make sense when H100 shares trade below net asset value.
H100 shares (NGM:H100) were up 6.5% at 1.53 Swedish kronor as of 11:45 a.m. Stockholm time Thursday (10:45 UTC), valuing the company at about $170 million. The 3,476.8 BTC it held on Sept. 30 would be worth about $222 million at Thursday’s Bitcoin price of $63,871.
The company reported a third-quarter net profit of 147.9 million kronor ($14.5 million) after recording a preliminary noncash gain of 171 million kronor on its August acquisition of Norwegian Bitcoin company NSD AS. Its operations lost 13.5 million kronor ($1.3 million) in the quarter.
The deal added 2,455 BTC to H100’s holdings. BitcoinTreasuries ranks H100 third among Europe’s publicly traded Bitcoin holders, behind Germany’s Bitcoin Group SE and France’s Capital B.

items.author: Decrypt Agent
items.content:
In brief
- GameStop CEO Ryan Cohen said publishers are making a mistake by releasing games only as digital downloads, on the eve of GTA 6's digital-only launch.
- Cohen said the shift has hurt both consumers and GameStop, whose sales of pre-owned products fell 32% year over year in its latest reported quarter.
- He has met with Rep. Ritchie Torres, who is backing a bill that would require gaming companies to give buyers ongoing access to the games they purchase.
GameStop CEO Ryan Cohen has criticized video game publishers for abandoning physical discs, as Grand Theft Auto 6, one of the most anticipated games ever made, launches on Thursday as a digital download only.
"When you buy a game, you should be able to sell it, trade it or lend it to a friend," Cohen told Bloomberg. "Unquestionably, the decision to move to all digital has hurt consumers, and it's also hurt GameStop."
Cohen declined to name specific companies, but Take-Two Interactive is releasing the $80 game only as a download, with retailers selling boxes containing download codes. Asked about presales, Cohen said: "It's a code in a box. I mean, we're selling a lot of it."
Take-Two declined to comment to Bloomberg.
Trade-ins under pressure
The shift hits a core part of GameStop's business. Pre-owned and refurbished products made up 22% of the retailer's sales, about $171 million, in the quarter that ended August 1, down 32% from a year earlier, according to Bloomberg.
Cohen said he has spoken with publishers, who he argued benefit from limiting trade-ins because used copies compete with new sales. "They're taking away competition," he said.
Sony announced in July that it will stop producing physical discs for new PlayStation games in January 2028, a move experts have said will hit low-income gamers hardest. PlayStation founder Ken Kutaragi has dismissed the backlash as a "mentality issue," while an Infinity Ward veteran said publishers have pushed to cut discs since 2007.
The fight over game ownership
Cohen said he has met with Rep. Ritchie Torres (D-NY), who is backing the Power to the Players Act, which would require gaming companies to give consumers ongoing access to the titles they buy. "A game that can be taken away the moment a company pulls the plug is not a purchase. It is a rental disguised as a sale," Torres said in October.
In Europe, the Stop Killing Games campaign gathered 1.3 million signatures for a European Citizens' Initiative calling for publishers to keep games playable after support ends.
The question of whether buyers own digital games has also reached the courts. Sony has argued in court that digital games can't be owned, prompting some in the crypto industry to pitch blockchain-based ownership as a fix.
Cohen's GameStop has also made bets beyond gaming. The company bought 4,710 BTC for more than $500 million in 2025, and in March moved all but one of them into a covered call strategy on Coinbase Prime to generate income. In May, after eBay rejected its takeover offer, GameStop sought shareholder approval to raise its authorized share count to 2.5 billion as it built a stake in the online marketplace.

IOSCO警告：先进量子计算机或在五年内破解金融业常用加密技术

BlockBeats 消息，11 月 19 日，国际证券委员会组织（IOSCO）11 月 19 日发布报告称，部分行业专家认为，未来五年内可能出现足以破解金融系统广泛使用的公钥密码技术的量子计算机。目前尚无已知量子计算机具备这种能力，五年是风险估计，并非确定时间表。但银行、支付网络和区块链的安全系统迁移可能耗时多年，IOSCO 呼吁金融机构现在就开始准备。

IOSCO 在这份 63 页的报告中指出，多数受观察机构仍处于排查易受影响的系统、培训员工或制定迁移计划的阶段，真正开始测试或部署抗量子方案的机构相对较少。一些机构已经意识到风险，却仍在等待监管要求更明确或技术更成熟。同日，英国央行、金融行为监管局和审慎监管局发布联合指引，建议金融机构梳理现有密码系统、制定分阶段替换计划，并评估技术供应商的准备情况。

对比特币和以太坊而言，风险主要涉及用于授权交易的数字签名。如果未来出现足够强大的量子计算机，公钥已公开的钱包可能面临私钥被推导、资产被盗的风险。即使区块链支持抗量子签名，未迁移到安全地址的旧钱包也不会自动受到保护。比特币开发者 Jameson Lopp 等人提出，在过渡期结束后限制未迁移的易受攻击资产继续使用旧签名转账；反对者认为，这可能阻止合法持有人动用自己的比特币。该方案仍是提案，并非已生效的网络规则。

迁移也可能带来性能和成本压力。IOSCO 援引的研究显示，部分抗量子签名的数据大小约为主流区块链现用签名的 35 至 40 倍。在一项 Solana 测试网实验中，换用抗量子签名后，交易吞吐量下降约 90%。这一数字来自特定测试，并非 Solana 主网的实际表现，也不代表其他抗量子方案会出现同等降幅。

OpenAI总裁Greg持有近300亿美元OpenAI股权，Sam后悔：当年该听他的

动察 Beating AI 快讯，11 月 18 日，OpenAI CEO Sam Altman 和总裁 Greg Brockman 一同出席《纽约时报》DealBook 峰会。主持人 Andrew Ross Sorkin 当面提起两人的巨大财富反差：Greg 持有价值约 300 亿美元的 OpenAI 股权，Sam 却没有直接持股。

主持人问，这是否影响两人的关系？将来 OpenAI 上市，Sam 会不会也获得同等规模的股权？

Sam 表示，两人的关系完全没有受到影响，但没有回答自己未来是否会拿股权。

Greg 随后透露，当年筹划公司架构时，他曾明确建议 Sam 接受股权。这也是两人少有的分歧之一。但 Sam 坚持不拿，Greg 最终尊重了他的选择。

Sam 听完承认：「我当初真该听 Greg 的。」他还表示，不拿股权这件事后来给他带来了不少麻烦。

Sam 前不久刚解释过后悔的原因。今年 10 月，他接受《Vanity Fair》采访时表示，当初拒绝股权，是希望自己能够不受个人经济利益影响，为人类的未来做决策。但他发现，这个决定反而破坏了外界对他的信任。

他还曾公开抱怨，人们很容易理解一个 CEO 为赚钱而努力，却很难相信有人只是因为喜欢技术、希望影响技术和社会的发展，才如此投入工作。

items.author: Jacob Lyon
items.content:
The European Commission has been targeted in a cyberattack that may have seen some employees’ personal data stolen, according to Politico.
The cyberattack reportedly disrupted the Commission for 10 days and affected Sysper, the HR management portal it uses to process payslips and leave requests. It also affected its medical reimbursement system MyPMO.
Security checks were upped in response, and the commission’s Corporate Management Board called urgent meetings to discuss the “ongoing cyber incidents.”
Both Sysper and MyPMO are mostly functioning again. An EU official told the Politico, “The Commission believes it has contained most of the attack, but the full extent of any damage remains unclear.”
Read more: European supermarket fridges hacked again
The European Commission suspects that an AI-powered tool called ARTEX gave the hackers a way to identify vulnerabilities in its IT systems.
As for whether or not personal data was breached, investigators are still figuring it out, and the commission doesn’t know yet.
This incident is just another in a string of cybersecurity breaches that have plagued Western infrastructure over the past few months, including hacked fridges and crypto malware deployed across hundreds of major big-name websites.

谷歌推出Stitch Loop：AI全天盯着线上数据，自动找问题、改代码、验证效果

动察 Beating AI 快讯，Google Labs 推出新实验产品 Stitch Loop，让 AI 智能体在软件上线后继续工作。原来的 Stitch 主要负责设计界面，新产品则能持续监测真实运营数据，发现问题、修改代码，再检查改动有没有效果。

开发者只需设定目标，比如提高购物网站的结账转化率。Stitch Loop 就会分析用户行为、运行日志和反馈，寻找影响转化的问题，提出改进方案。用户选定方案后，AI 会在隔离的云端环境中编写代码，提交 PR（代码修改请求），等待人工审核。

改动上线后，AI 还会继续追踪指标。如果效果不理想，就寻找下一轮改进机会。即使目标达成，也会持续监测，防止效果回退。

Stitch Loop 默认提供三类自动优化任务：网络安全、运行速度和无障碍适配。其中，安全任务结合 Gemini 4 Carbon 与 Google DeepMind 的 CodeMender，自动扫描代码漏洞并提出修复方案。

它支持连接 GitHub，通过 180 多种集成、MCP 和命令行工具获取产品数据，也能为 Antigravity 等编程智能体提供持续更新的产品上下文。

谷歌此前的 Jules 已能定期执行安全修补、性能优化等任务，但该产品已于 11 月 11 日转为只读，计划年底关闭。Stitch Loop 进一步把代码维护与真实业务指标结合起来。

目前 Stitch Loop 仍处于实验阶段，全球用户均可申请加入候补名单，符合条件的 Google AI Ultra 订阅用户享有优先体验资格。

Claude Code推出实验性Code Mode：一次调用多个工具，长任务可后台执行

动察 Beating AI 快讯，Anthropic 为 Claude Code 加入实验性 Code Mode，已在 11 月 12 日发布的 v2.1.323 中上线，目前需要手动开启。

启用后，Claude 可以先编写 JavaScript 脚本，再通过脚本连续、并行调用多个工具，还能把工具返回的数据先处理好，只将必要结果交给模型，从而减少模型请求和 Token 消耗。

Anthropic 如今才将其集成进 Claude Code，目前仍处于实验阶段，需要手动开启。

items.author: Gino Matos
items.content:
Quick Take
- Bitcoin hovered near $62,000 as Fed minutes revealed overwhelming support for further rate hikes, while gold and silver suffered steep losses.
- Rising Treasury yields and a stronger dollar threaten Bitcoin as stablecoin supply shrinks by $16 billion and ETF investors withdraw over $310 million.
- Bitcoin faces a potential liquidation wave between $59,500 and $62,200, raising concerns that another decline could trigger more forced selling.
Bitcoin, gold, and silver had already fallen on Wednesday before the Federal Reserve released its October meeting minutes.
Almost all participants at the October meeting judged that further rate increases would likely be appropriate in the months ahead under their baseline outlooks for inflation and employment.
Bitcoin traded in the $62,000 zone for most of the day after the minutes, while spot gold closed down 3% to $3,741.82 an ounce, and silver fell 5.3% to $44.88 an ounce. Gold had touched its lowest level since September 2025 earlier in the session.
Even after the minutes, CME FedWatch odds were 92% for a quarter-point hike in December and 8% for a half-point move.
Analysts linked the drop in bullion to the stronger dollar, rising Treasury yields and expectations of tighter policy. Gold pays no interest, so rising yields increase the cost of holding it instead of putting cash into interest-bearing assets.
The Silver Institute’s 2026 market forecast projects a 3% decline in overall industrial use, even as demand outside photovoltaics is expected to grow 4.5%. The institute still expects total silver demand to exceed supply by 35 million ounces this year.
The October minutes show a committee that held its target range at 3.75% to 4.00% by a 10-2 vote.
Lisa Cook and Beth Hammack preferred a quarter-point increase, while a couple of participants said a move larger than 25 basis points could warrant consideration at the next meeting if inflation data were unfavorable.
Bitget analyst Lewis Huang shared in a note that the record points to wider backing for a hike than the vote count shows. He said:
“The minutes suggest broader support for an October hike than the 10–2 vote alone implied—and that was before payrolls and CPI both came in hot. Governor Waller has said a half-point increase should be considered; evidence that other officials were already open to that scale of tightening in October could push the odds of a 50-basis-point move higher.”
Huang pointed to yields and the dollar as the channel into Bitcoin, saying that a further rise in yields and the dollar would add pressure to Bitcoin, which is now trading well below its 200-week moving average near $68,000. Gold could also struggle if real yields keep climbing.
Fabian Dori, chief investment officer at Sygnum Bank, sees the same path. He said:
“Markets already price a run of hikes into next year, and the minutes suggest the committee was leaning that way even before October’s hot CPI.”
Dori added that this likely keeps long-term yields and the dollar firm, and the question for Bitcoin is whether debasement concerns and advancing institutional adoption can outweigh it.
Fed staff also outlined that falling prices could force investors to sell assets to cut borrowing, while withdrawals could force fund managers to raise cash.
In very severe scenarios, sales by hedge funds, bond mutual funds and target-date funds could be large enough to impair market functioning. Staff were concerned that selling into a falling market could push prices down further and strain trading.
What would signal a Bitcoin rebound?
A softer dollar and lower Treasury yields would ease some pressure on markets, and Bitcoin’s own demand gauges give investors another way to judge a rebound.
Farside Investors’ ETF flow table shows over $310 million in net outflows from US spot Bitcoin funds on Nov. 17 and 18.
Glassnode’s Nov. 17 analysis estimated that about 20% of the coins held by short-term holders were acquired between $62,000 and $66,000. That puts Wednesday’s reported price near the low end of a range where many recent buyers entered.
Using the same Nov. 17 data, Glassnode modeled a cluster of potential long liquidations between $59,500 and $62,200, where a renewed decline could force some leveraged positions to close.
Glassnode puts short-term holders’ overall cost basis at $74,100, and a return to that level would bring recent buyers back around break-even as a group.
Huang named the weekend low as the level to watch:
“For Bitcoin, a break below the weekend low near $62,000 could extend the sell-off,” he said.
Stablecoin supply had shrunk 4.2% over 90 days, and Bitcoin briefly traded at a premium on Coinbase around the November low before slipping back to a small discount relative to the global price.
Georges Chouchani, founder and CEO of Euclid, links the minutes to that cash shortage:
“The minutes show support for a hike went well beyond the two officials who voted for one in October, so markets start pricing more hikes after December.”
He said that this keeps yields and the dollar firm, and it hits a crypto market already short of cash. Stablecoin supply, the dollar tokens crypto trades with, has fallen by about $16 billion over the past month, its steepest drop since June 2022, so there are fewer buyers to absorb the selling, and Bitcoin takes the hit.
A premium that holds, sustained ETF inflows, or a leveling off in stablecoin supply would give investors more evidence that demand is returning.
items.title: Bitcoin faces fresh $60,000 threat as Fed minutes reveal overwhelming support for more rate hikes

 https://arewemlsyet.com/  I applaud the people working on Matrix, it worthy project, but I feel the E2EE issues are at a level close to negligence.

分析：BTC高成本套牢盘割肉持续，承接区逐步下移，短期宜「多看少动」等待恐慌出清

BlockBeats 消息，11 月 19 日，链上分析师 Murphy 发文称，通过 URPD 数据观察当前比特币筹码的移动轨迹与情绪反馈。首先，短期持有者（STH）的筹码总量每天在增加，这意味着长期持有者（LTH）持续派发的速度快于 STH 持币满 6 个月转化为 LTH 的速度，供大于求令价格持续承压，STH 净增长在 11 月 13 日达到近 1.5 万枚的峰值。其次，高成本区的套牢筹码仍在持续割肉离场，主要集中在 75,000 至 81,000 美元区间，目前尚未看到明显减缓的趋势。同时，市场的承接区间正逐步下移，从 12 至 14 日的 65,000 至 72,000 美元下移至 15 至 17 日的 58,000 至 72,000 美元，且承接量较前几天有所减弱，显示部分资金开始变得谨慎。

整体来看，短期内市场情绪对多头不利，派发没有明显减弱，承接盘显得犹豫，但市场仍未放弃抵抗。分析师指出，目前 81,000 美元以上的套牢盘已减少抛售，接下来重点为等待 75,000 美元以上的恐慌盘彻底释放。在一轮猛烈的快速下杀中，「边打边退」也许是最明智的选择，当前依然维持「多看、少动」的观点，只能用时间慢慢消化抛压，还远没有到大举反攻的时候。

OpenAI董事长创办的AI客服公司，半年估值拟翻倍至300亿美元

动察 Beating AI 快讯，OpenAI 董事长、Salesforce 前联席 CEO Bret Taylor 创办的 AI 客服公司 Sierra，正洽谈融资约 15 亿美元，目标估值高达 300 亿美元。

Lightspeed、Greenoaks 和 Benchmark 正考虑投资，谈判仍处于早期。Sierra 今年 5 月刚以 158 亿美元估值融资 9.5 亿美元。仅过半年，估值就有望接近翻倍。

Sierra 成立于 2023 年，专门帮企业部署 AI 客服。它的智能体不仅能接听电话、回答问题，还能连接企业内部系统，处理退款、订单变更等事务。客户包括摩根大通、Cigna 等大型企业，部分业务按 AI 成功解决的问题收费。

它的收入增长也很快。Sierra 今年 10 月披露，年化经常性收入（ARR）已超过 4 亿美元，短短 5 个月翻了一倍。仅第三季度就新增超过 1.5 亿美元。按目前披露的收入规模计算，300 亿美元估值约相当于 ARR 的 75 倍。

竞争对手 Decagon 也在筹备新一轮数亿美元融资，其今年第二季度末年化收入约 1 亿美元，预计年底达到 1.75 亿至 2 亿美元。

BlockBeats 消息，11 月 19 日，DEGEN 创始人 Jacek 发文表示，将暂时搁置 POOF 和 POV 的活跃开发与推广，把精力集中在 DEGEN 以及更广泛的 Base 生态。其称两者并非就此终止，也不意味着今后不会再推进，只是眼下需要更有选择地分配时间和资源。Jacek 介绍，DEGEN 财库持有 POOF 总供应量的 50%，其中 20% 以财库资金在公开市场买入，其余 30% 存放在流动性池中。POV 网站将继续运行，他仍看好观点市场这一方向，但现阶段选择把重心放在别处。

Jacek 表示，希望 DEGEN 继续成为 Base 上具有辨识度的社区品牌，但需要走出最初的 Farcaster 用户圈，接触新进入链上的人群，并加强品牌、IP 和内容建设，计划与动画团队合作并于明年初发布更多内容。其同时提到，Yeetr 仍将作为独立项目推进，DEGEN 持有者已可在该平台质押 DEGEN。若产品形成有规模的业务，打算将费用和利润再投入产品增长，其中一部分可能用于回购 DEGEN，但目前尚未到这一阶段。DEGEN 相关账号将专注品牌、内容和社区，其个人账号则跟进 Yeetr 进展。

items.content:
IOSCO warns quantum upgrades could slow blockchains, leave security gaps
A Solana test network ran about 90% slower with quantum-resistant signatures, and wallets that keep using older keys could remain vulnerable.
The International Organization of Securities Commissions (IOSCO) warned that upgrading blockchains to withstand quantum attacks could slow transactions and raise fees.
In a report released Thursday, IOSCO said some quantum-resistant digital signatures take up far more space than those used to authorize transactions today. Larger signatures mean fewer transactions can fit in each block, which could increase congestion, push up fees and require more storage.
IOSCO cited an experiment in which a test version of Solana ran about 90% slower with quantum-resistant signatures.
No known quantum computer can break the cryptography that secures these networks today. IOSCO urged firms to start preparing now because the transition could take years.
IOSCO said layer-1 networks use cryptography both to authorize transactions and to reach agreement on which blocks to add. Even after an upgrade, funds in dormant wallets and applications could remain vulnerable if they still rely on older keys.
Layer-2 networks can use quantum-resistant proofs to verify transactions and still depend on vulnerable systems to settle those transactions, move assets between chains or approve upgrades.
In April, Bitcoin advocate Samson Mow warned that larger post-quantum signatures could reduce Bitcoin’s throughput and that rushed fixes might introduce new vulnerabilities.
In October, Starknet’s community backed research into becoming an independent, quantum-resistant layer-1 network, following concerns over its reliance on Ethereum’s security upgrade timeline.
Ethereum researcher Justin Drake has since outlined a 2028 post-quantum transition target, ahead of the network’s existing 2029 roadmap.
Related: AI poses greater threat to Bitcoin than quantum computing, Swan founder says
items.title: IOSCO warns quantum upgrades could slow blockchains, leave security gaps

豆包音视频通话模型开放API：AI能边看边听边说，还会主动开口

动察 Beating AI 快讯，11 月 19 日，火山引擎正式开放豆包实时音视频模型 SeedRealtime 1.0 的 API。该模型今年 8 月就已在豆包 App 上线，如今第三方开发者也能将这套实时视频通话能力接入自己的产品。

SeedRealtime 将摄像头画面、声音和时间顺序放进同一个端到端模型。AI 可以一边观察、一边听用户说话，同时判断该什么时候开口，减少传统语音识别、视觉理解、语音合成等多个模块串联带来的延迟和信息损失。

官方演示中，用户把整颗咖啡豆倒进咖啡机的萃取手柄，AI 不等提问就主动提醒先研磨。逛博物馆时，用户只需提前交代要找哪件文物，模型便能持续观察镜头，在目标出现时主动提醒。它还能分辨多人对话，在嘈杂环境中避免被旁人的闲聊误触发。

字节跳动今年 8 月公布的人工评测显示，相比多个模型串联的方案，SeedRealtime 的音视频对话节奏问题减少约一半，抢话、回应迟缓和背景噪声误触发等现象明显减少。

items.author: Decrypt Agent
items.content:
Bitcoin is struggling to hold the $64,000 level as investors continue to pull money from spot Bitcoin ETFs and brace for another interest rate hike from the Federal Reserve.
The leading cryptocurrency was trading at around $63,800 on Thursday, down 1% on the day and 13% over the past week, according to Decrypt data. It has hovered between roughly $63,000 and $65,000 since the weekend, briefly dipping below $63,000 and touching a 24-hour low of $62,068, per CoinGecko data.
"Bitcoin remains under selling pressure," Daniela Hathorn, senior market analyst at Capital.com, told Decrypt, noting that it has fallen roughly 26% from its late-September peak near $87,000. "Elevated Treasury yields, dollar strength and expectations of further Fed tightening are weighing on risk appetite, while the broader technology selloff has added to the pressure."
ETF outflows mount
U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded $306.4 million in net outflows on Wednesday, after $239.9 million on Tuesday, according to SoSoValue data. The funds have seen outflows on nine of the past 10 trading days, with Monday's small $8 million inflow the only exception, and have lost about $2.9 billion so far in November. Their total net assets have fallen to $77.7 billion. Bitcoin miners have added to the selling, with major miners including Riot and MARA selling some of their holdings to fund a shift into AI infrastructure.
Monday's brief inflow "does not signal a market inflection point," Tim Sun, senior researcher at HashKey, told Decrypt. Net short positions in Bitcoin futures held by leveraged funds on CME have fallen to their lowest level since early 2023, and futures basis yields have narrowed, he said, indicating that hedge funds have largely unwound the basis trade that paired spot ETF purchases with short futures. That means the current outflows are mainly driven by investors actively cutting their Bitcoin exposure, Sun said.
"If macro expectations do not improve, investors may shift from buying the dip to selling into rallies, creating additional overhead resistance on subsequent rebounds," he added.
"Recent Bitcoin ETF outflows and leveraged liquidations" have amplified the decline, Hathorn said. "Despite stronger Nvidia earnings, the market has struggled to stage a significant rebound, suggesting confidence remains fragile. A sustained recovery may require renewed ETF inflows and a more supportive interest-rate outlook."
Some traders have also pointed the finger at Anthropic's upcoming IPO for drawing money away from crypto, though analysts have disputed that the listing is draining crypto liquidity, attributing it instead to ETF outflows, forced selling and rising interest rates.
Traders see a 90.7% chance that the Fed will raise rates by a quarter point at its December 9 meeting, and a 9.3% chance of a half-point hike, according to CME FedWatch. The odds of a half-point move have risen from 6.5% a day earlier. Fed Governor Christopher Waller has called for an even bigger, half-point increase, unless policymakers signal another rise in January.
Levels to watch
Hathorn said $64,000 is the immediate level to watch, followed by support around $62,000 and the psychological $60,000 mark. A sustained recovery above $66,000 to $68,000 could ease selling pressure, "but the broader trend remains bearish while lower highs persist," she said.
Onchain analytics firm Glassnode said in its weekly report on Tuesday that the crash had pushed investors’ realized losses to levels seen only near past market lows in 2018, 2020, 2022 and early 2023, a sign of capitulation. Bitcoin is now holding a dense block of recent buyers between $62,000 and $66,000, which grew by about 66,000 BTC during the two days of heaviest selling, Glassnode said. But a daily close below that block could set off a fast drop toward the June low of $58,500, and the Realized Price, the average price at which all Bitcoin last moved, at $53,700.
Traders on Decrypt Predict see a 43% chance that Bitcoin will fall to $60,000 at some point before the end of November, and a 12% chance that it will drop as low as $55,000. They give just a 2% chance that it will climb back to $82,500 this month.
There are some signs of support. About 1.1 million BTC, roughly 5.5% of supply, last changed hands at prices between $60,000 and $64,000, and that band has grown by more than 25,000 BTC in recent days, according to Neil Steinhardt, head of Nexo U.S., in a note shared with Decrypt Wednesday. A dense base of holders with costs near current prices "can act as a support zone, though it is not a floor," he wrote.
Bitcoin has also held up better than gold. The amount of gold one Bitcoin buys rose above its 200-day average this week, to about 17.1 ounces, around 40% above its March low, Steinhardt said.

items.author: Liam 'Akiba' Wright
items.content:
Quick Take
- CoinShares raised $19.3 million in October by selling its entire treasury Ethereum position and half its treasury Solana.
- Quarter-end assets under management rose to $7.4 billion, while management fees held at $19.1 million as the rally came late.
- CoinShares had $358.1 million of net digital assets on loan at September’s close, leaving it exposed to borrower defaults.
CoinShares Chief Executive Jean-Marie Mognetti said on Nov. 18 that October’s sale of the firm’s entire corporate treasury Ethereum position and half its treasury Solana freed up $19.3 million for potential share repurchases.
The company’s third-quarter earnings show how its shareholders remain exposed to crypto prices through its remaining holdings and the fees it charges on investment products.
CoinShares raised $16.6 million from the Ethereum sale and $2.7 million from Solana. Together, they amounted to about 48% of the board’s $40 million repurchase authorization.
The board approved the program on Oct. 22, and CoinShares announced it on Oct. 27, with a run time until the next annual meeting, expected in the second quarter of 2027. Purchases depend on market conditions, blackout periods, and trading-volume limits.
Before the sale, CoinShares held $43.2 million in treasury digital assets, including 235 Bitcoin worth $19.6 million, as of Sept. 30, according to its interim financial statements.
The treasury also held $17.6 million in Ethereum and $5.9 million in Solana at that date. The October disclosure identified sales of Ethereum and Solana, with half the Solana position retained.
The filing separately lists $4.1 billion of digital assets held for operations as of Sept. 30, including $880.5 million of Ethereum and $407.8 million of Solana. Some of those assets back exchange-traded products or hedge its obligations to product holders.
How crypto prices still reach earnings
Assets under management climbed from $5.5 billion at the June close to $7.4 billion at the September close.
The $125 million in quarterly net inflows accounted for about 7% of the increase, with price appreciation adding roughly $1.75 billion, based on CoinShares’ first-half and nine-month figures. At its CoinShares Physical platform alone, prices added $938.4 million and net inflows added $77.8 million.
CoinShares reported that management fees held at $19.1 million in both quarters. The fees accrue on daily assets, and the late-quarter rally lifted the September closing balance more than the average fee base.
The total also includes seed assets that pay no fees, with CoinShares reporting $6.4 billion in fee-paying assets at quarter-end.
The asset manager had $358.1 million of digital assets on loan as of Sept. 30, after accounting for expected credit losses, up from $69.8 million at the end of 2025. Some loans are unsecured, so the firm can lose money if a borrower defaults.
Management said it shifted Ethereum from staking into lending during the third quarter, and the loan book earned $4.3 million in interest that quarter, alongside $2.8 million in staking revenue.
Stronger lending and trading lifted capital markets segment revenue and gains to $17.8 million from $4.9 million in the second quarter.
The third-quarter segment figure comprised $8.6 million in revenue and $9.2 million in operating gains. CoinShares reported $27.7 million in consolidated revenue, including asset management fees.
An unrealized $9.6 million gain came from the gap between the value of cash-redeemable XBT certificates and the assets CoinShares holds to hedge them. The gain was reflected in the company’s $28.4 million of operating income and excluded from the $17.8 million segment figure.
A $14.4 million treasury revaluation gain was recorded below operating income and helped lift net income to $39.6 million.
CoinShares said its expanded monthly tracker adds lending, staking and treasury figures to the existing product assets and flows data.
That gives investors a way to track what the company holds and what it puts to work, while measuring buyback execution separately by the shares the company reports purchasing.
items.title: CoinShares unloads $19.3M in ETH and SOL, yet keeps crypto risk

By its nature, the leaking memory is very repetitive and easily compressed. Right now this daemon has tried to claim 2.5GB of memory, but it's been compressed to a mere 450MB of actual memory! And because it's a memory leak, it never accesses this old stuff, so it never gets decompressed. Only 20MB of RAM is held that isn't compressed. Of course, it w...

[Lio]: RAM compression sounds very useful but the thing I really need extra RAM for is local inference. Since the models are effectively highly compressed data already my assumption is that RAM compression won't help improve that much (I'm assuming unified memory here as per the Framework Desktop).  A bit like trying to compress a JPEG in a zip file. Could anyone comment on that?

[hedgehog]: As others have noted zswap is usually a better choice than zram, additionally depending on your situation it may be worth checking which algorithm it's using as there are a few choices (zstd, lz4, etc) and the defaults vary by distro. zstd is the right choice IMO unless you're in a situation where you know better.

For browser tabs, though, I think a better solution is automatic tab closing, using something like the Tab Wrangler extension for Chrome. Collecting tabs comes naturally; we’re much worse at closing them.

items.author: Cointelegraph by Zoltan Vardai
items.content:
Singapore settles $77.5M tokenized bill sale with wholesale CBDC
MAS issued the bills directly on its test network, which it plans to rename SG Digital Ledger and use for settlement beyond the trials.
The Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) issued 100 million Singapore dollars ($77.5 million) in tokenized bills on Nov. 6, with banks using wholesale central bank digital currency (CBDC) to pay for them.
Five banks submitted bids totaling more than twice the amount on offer, MAS said Thursday. The four-week bills mature on Dec. 4.
MAS issued the bills directly on the Singapore Dollar Test Network. That gives borrowers an asset they could pledge as collateral for loans on the network, the central bank said.
Singapore began experimenting with blockchain-based bank payments in 2016. In 2025, banks used the test network and MAS-issued digital currency to settle overnight loans.
MAS now plans to turn the Singapore Dollar Test Network, where the bills were issued, into a settlement system for financial institutions, Managing Director Chia Der Jiun said Thursday at the Singapore FinTech Festival. The network will be renamed SG Digital Ledger.
“As the use of tokenized assets and digital money grows, trusted settlement on CBDC will be needed,” Chia said. “It underpins settlement finality and confidence, especially for large value settlement.”
In 2027, MAS plans to issue more tokenized bills, bring more financial institutions into the trials and expand the bills’ use as collateral.
Related: Singapore advances asset tokenization with new MAS frameworks
items.title: Singapore settles $77.5M tokenized bill sale with wholesale CBDC

数据：10枚以上比特币钱包数创年内新高，但整体供应量仍在流失

BlockBeats 消息，11 月 19 日，市场情绪分析机构 Santiment 发布数据，持有 10 枚以上 BTC 的「10+ BTC Club」钱包数量已增至 150,770 个，创下 2026 年 1 月以来的最高纪录。然而，该群体在过去四周内累计抛售了超 1 万枚 BTC。目前这些大钱包总共持有约 1666 万枚 BTC，占全网供应量的 82.85%，平均每个钱包持仓约 110.5 枚。这呈现出一种背离状态：大户钱包的数量在增加，但该群体掌控的总供应量却在快速下降。

分析指出，近期比特币价格跌至 63,000 美元附近，促使更多小规模钱包达到了 10 枚 BTC 的持仓门槛，但这批大户的整体行动方向对多头依然不利。分析师强调，市场下一个真正的看涨确认信号，并非仅仅是钱包数量的增长，而是其持有供应量的回升。当这 82.85% 的供应份额重新开始上升时，才能说明这些核心大玩家正转向激进积累，这将构成更具说服力的反弹信号。

items.author: Liam 'Akiba' Wright
items.content:
Quick Take
- The World Bank Group will explore settling development payments in USDC with Citi and Circle in eligible borrower countries.
- The World Bank Group says FundsChain tracks disbursements for more than 350 projects across 96 countries under existing payment procedures.
- The announcement leaves open where USDC would enter the payment chain and what currency recipients would receive.
The World Bank Group said Nov. 17 that it would work with Citi and Circle to explore using USDC to settle development payments.
The group wants to see whether a dollar stablecoin can make those payments faster, cheaper, and more transparent.
Under the proposal, Citi would provide links to established banking networks, while Circle’s infrastructure would help issue USDC and settle payments in it.
The World Bank would examine where that route could work alongside its existing arrangements, which rely on correspondent banks to handle payments across banking networks.
The initial exploration will engage borrower countries where digital assets are supported and permitted and focus on an intermediary-based model. The World Bank gave no launch date or list of participating borrowers, and said it would explore working with other banks over time.
What FundsChain already does with USDC
The World Bank uses its original FundsChain platform to give project teams a record of where development money goes.
Authorized users can trace payments from the initial disbursement to the final recipient and inspect supporting documents. The group says more than 350 projects across 96 countries are on the tracking platform.
Borrowers use the same process to apply for withdrawals, and projects continue paying suppliers and beneficiaries as before. FundsChain lets project teams document transactions through designated project accounts and local accounts farther down the payment chain.
The records can also feed into expenditure statements that borrowers submit through the bank’s client portal.
Linking an invoice to a transaction lets authorized reviewers check what a payment covered. That oversight can extend beyond the initial transfer to a borrower and into the spending that happens within a project.
The bank has separately explored whether it can build spending rules into payments themselves. In a July update, it said a FundsChain Evolution pilot had gone live in Ethiopia using programmable money to place conditions on how the funds can be spent.
The proposal leaves open where USDC would enter the payment chain, whether recipients would get tokens, and how any tokens would be converted to local currency.
Those details would determine what the change in settlement would mean for the people and organizations that ultimately receive the money.
items.title: Citi and Circle join World Bank in tests with USDC, unlocking a massive aid shift

--- Top Comments ---

[sgarland]: > What we learned along the way… Deleting rows doesn’t shrink SQLite files This is true of every RDBMS I am aware of. It would be horribly inefficient to constantly run page merges in order to be able to free some of them. Whenever I read things on posts that are a. discussed in documentation b. should be apparent from first principles, I immediately lose faith in the product.

[anacrolix]: I spent years trying to squeeze this use case out of sqlite. All roads lead to tears, it is  not  made for this use case. I wrote  https://github.com/anacrolix/possum  for this exact use case. It has a few rough edges but it absolutely hauls ass for caching on disk. Incidentally it uses sqlite for transaction/TTL metadata which is more suited to sqlite but it's  still  the bottleneck. sqlite transaction commit overhead is too high and uncompetitive without batchi...

[lukax]: OpenStack Swift uses SQLite for storing metadata. Each account has one SQLite db. Each container also initially had one SQLite db but in 2018 they added support for sharding so if a container has more than 1 million objects, the container is split into multiple SQLite databases. The performance is not ideal. Ceph scales much better.

[articulatepang]: I wonder if they tried storing diffs instead, and compacting them once in a while. These are user preferences for UI setup, and they have a lot of write traffic. But probably each user changes their preferences only by a little bit each time. Their 1MB writes would go down to just the small diffs. They could store the diffs and transparently apply them before sending to the client. After some timeout or maybe after a certain number of diffs have accumulated, squash them all and write back. Th...

[bob1029]: > JSON blobs An alternative to faster blob storage is to represent the blob's schema in SQL directly. If most blob updates are incremental you can eliminate a significant amount of storage IO and garbage collection this way. One SQLite database per blob type with a metadata SQLite db that tracks each. We could leverage powerful AI reasoning models to produce SQLite schemas and virtual table adapters for each encountered JSON schema type.

Bitcoin ETF assets fall to three-month low as 2026 net outflows top $2.5B
US spot Bitcoin ETFs lost $306.4 million Wednesday, pushing their combined assets to $77.7 billion as Bitcoin briefly traded below $63,000.
US spot Bitcoin exchange-traded funds (ETFs) ended Wednesday with $77.7 billion in net assets, a three-month low, as net outflows for the year topped $2.5 billion.
The funds recorded $306.4 million in net outflows on Wednesday, according to SoSoValue data. The funds held about 1.25 million Bitcoin (BTC) at Wednesday’s close, according to Walet Pilot.
BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) held the most Bitcoin, with about 779,870 BTC, followed by the Fidelity Wise Origin Bitcoin Fund (FBTC) with 172,080 BTC and Grayscale Bitcoin Trust (GBTC) with 122,730 BTC.
Bitcoin briefly dipped below $63,000 on Wednesday. It traded at $63,545 at publishing time, down 1.7% over the past 24 hours, according to CoinGecko.
Vikram Subburaj, CEO of crypto exchange Giottus, said in a statement shared with Cointelegraph that institutional selling and expectations of tighter US monetary policy continued to weigh on market sentiment.
He also cited onchain data showing that long-term Bitcoin holders had reduced their positions by around 121,151 BTC over 30 days.
Selling pressure also extended to US spot Ether (ETH) ETFs, which recorded around $40 million in outflows Wednesday, bringing their 2026 net withdrawals to roughly $895 million.
Related: Goldman Sachs reports $1.22B in Ether ETFs as ETHA share count jumps
items.title: Bitcoin ETF assets fall to three-month low as 2026 net outflows top $2.5B

韩国AI作弊风波升级：满分学霸直播自证前身亡，警方调查或将终止

动察 Beating AI 快讯，11 月 19 日，韩国法学研究生入学考试（LEET）史上首位满分考生李振宇（32 岁），在首尔一家旅馆被发现身亡。

当天上午，他原本打算在媒体面前直播解答韩国高考语文试题，以证明自己的真实水平，回应 AI 作弊质疑，但最终没有现身。

李振宇曾自述，自己早年高考成绩只有第 6 至 8 等级（韩国实行九级制，数字越大成绩越差），后来却考入首尔大学牙科学院。今年 7 月，他又答对 LEET 全部 70 道题，成为这项考试自 2008 年设立以来首个满分考生。

争议来自他此前公开的一份试卷。其中连续 3 道题的涂改前答案，恰好对应上一道题的正确选项。网友怀疑，他可能在抄录外部提供的答案时发生错位。

韩国另一名税务师考试状元此前已承认，自己通过微型摄像头拍摄试题，再利用 AI 获取答案。这起案件让李振宇受到更多质疑。李振宇则坚决否认作弊，称试卷反复涂改是因为考试后半段注意力下降。

11 月 18 日，多名律师正式向警方举报李振宇。次日，他未能出席公开验证，随后被发现身亡。警方在现场找到疑似遗书的便条，内容提到身心疲惫，但没有承认作弊。目前具体死亡原因仍在调查。

由于当事人死亡，针对他的刑事调查预计将终止。不过，韩国教育部门已要求保留他此前参加高考的答卷，是否进一步调查作弊疑云尚未确定。
