Strobaek 表示，市场正在计入人工智能未来带来的收入，这一规模「在不久的将来某个时候」将达到数万亿美元。他说，在科技股经历了大约一个半月的「洗牌」之后，这轮回调创造了他所称的「一个有吸引力的入场点」。不过，Strobaek 认为，受 AI、能源、基础设施和安全领域投资推动，强劲的经济周期仍在为股市提供支撑，而盈利增长——尤其是在美国和新兴市场——过去两年半至三年带来了强劲回报。

items.content:
Bitcoin, stocks wobble as Fed’s Waller talks of ‘shock’ 50-point rate hike
Bitcoin price action dropped below $63,000 after fresh hawkish comments from the Fed as Nvidia earnings optimism faded.
Bitcoin dropped below $63,000 after Wednesday’s Wall Street open as US stocks dipped on inflation concerns.
Key points:
- Bitcoin price weakness saw a dip to $63,000 on Wednesday amid a weak start for US equities.
- Fed governor Christopher Waller warned that officials may “need to shock people” with a 50-basis-point interest-rate hike in December.
- Analyst David Eng called Bitcoin selling pressure “extreme,” citing 30-day net capital outflows of $8.7 billion.
Waller: Fed may need to perform interest-rate “shock”
Data from TradingView showed Bitcoin (BTC) trading down 3% on the day, having incrementally sold off in the hours prior to the US trading session.
BTC/USD one-hour chart. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView
The weakness accompanied commentary on future Federal Reserve financial policy by governor Christopher Waller. Speaking to CNBC, Waller argued the case for hiking interest rates by 50 basis points at the December meeting of the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) — more than the current market consensus of 25 basis points.
With CPI inflation above the Fed’s 2% target for five years, he warned that businesses were becoming comfortable passing on 3% annual price rises “or higher” to consumers.
“You might need to, like, shock people to say, ‘Wait a minute; 3% is not the number you should be thinking about going forward,’” he said.
Waller described the need for “aggressive actions” to tackle inflationary trends, which he noted were spreading into areas not directly impacted by current geopolitical catalysts — the US-Iran war and associated spike in oil prices.
The latest data from CME Group’s FedWatch Tool showed markets still overwhelmingly favoring a 25-basis-point hike in December, with the odds of that outcome above 95%.
Fed target-rate probabilities by FOMC meeting (screenshot). Source: CME Group
Not everyone shared confidence in the case for policy tightening. Commenting on the Fed’s hawkish posture, economist Robin Brooks argued that the recent cooling in oil prices meant that upping rate-hike commitments was unnecessary.
“I don’t think any of the hawks on the FOMC have made a convincing case that underlying inflation - taking supply shocks out - is running hot,” he wrote in analysis on Tuesday. Brooks described the prospect of further rate hikes as a “terrible mistake.”
Related: Bitcoin realized loss metric beats June high as open interest eyes 2-year low
Analyst: Bitcoin needs $290 million daily inflows
US stocks opened lower on the day, attempting a brief turnaround before sliding back into negative territory. The S&P 500 was down 0.3% on the day, while the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite Index fluctuated around its daily open, shrugging off renewed optimism over the AI sector following Nvidia’s Q3 earnings beat.
Nasdaq Composite Index one-hour chart. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView
Bitcoin remained without an upside catalyst, seeking to break down from a trading range between $64,000 and $66,000 in place since Nov. 15.
Independent analyst David Eng warned that sell-side pressure remains “extreme” at current price levels. Eng cited $8.7 billion in capital outflows over the past 30 days, along with net outflows of $2.1 billion from the US spot Bitcoin exchange-traded funds (ETF) year-to-date.
“Bitcoin doesn’t need another $8.7 billion of buying every month to recover. It needs the balance between buying and selling to improve. At the current 30-day pace, a $290M/day improvement would eliminate the measured net outflow,” he argued on X.
items.title: Bitcoin, stocks wobble as Fed’s Waller talks of ‘shock’ 50-point rate hike

items.author: Oluwapelumi Adejumo
items.content:
Quick Take
- Anthropic's Claude Opus 5.5 completed a research assignment in under three hours that typically takes human contractors 16 hours.
- Epoch AI found the model delivered contractor-level work at a lower cost, raising questions about the future of outsourced research jobs.
- Epoch is considering shifting contractors toward reviewing AI-generated work, although errors still require human intervention.
Anthropic's Claude Opus 5.5 completed a research assignment in under three hours that typically takes human contractors 16 hours, according to Epoch AI.
The AI research organization reported on Nov. 17 that the model produced work comparable to that of its professional contractors, raising the possibility of automating parts of its research operations.
The assignment involved researching EcoDataCenter 1 for Epoch's data center database, a process requiring researchers to examine news reports, regulatory filings, and satellite imagery to establish details about the facility.
Epoch provided the AI models with its contractor guidelines, research tools, and evaluation criteria before assessing their work against the standards applied to human researchers.
Claude Opus 5.5 scored 87.5% on the assignment, completing it in just under three hours at a lower cost than hiring a contractor. Another Anthropic model, Claude Fable 5.2, delivered an even stronger result, scoring 97.5%. However, it required approximately six and a half hours and cost more than a human contractor.
Both models met Epoch's standards for core research, although their submissions still required revisions to equipment classifications, image annotations, and written descriptions.
By comparison, OpenAI's GPT-6.2 Astra scored 65% on the same assignment, missing important information and estimates that Epoch said the available evidence could have supported.
AI could change how research contractors work
The findings have prompted Epoch to reconsider how it allocates work between AI models and human contractors.
The organization said it is considering shifting some contractor time away from gathering and compiling research toward reviewing AI-generated submissions and performing other data center analysis.
Such a transition could let AI systems handle much of the initial research while human workers focus on checking findings, correcting errors, and preparing the material for publication.
However, the results also exposed differences in the economics of using AI for professional work.
While Opus completed the assignment faster and cheaper than a contractor, Fable's higher-quality output cost more, despite also finishing considerably faster than a human researcher.
The models also struggled with parts of the assignment that required visual interpretation, particularly labeling satellite images and identifying equipment.
These shortcomings help explain why Epoch has not proposed eliminating human involvement entirely, even as its models approach contractor-level performance.
Instead, the organization is considering a workflow in which AI produces the initial research and contractors refine the results, potentially reducing the human labor required for each database entry.
items.title: Anthropic’s Claude completes a 16-hour human research job in under 3 hours

items.author: Liam 'Akiba' Wright
items.content:
Quick Take
- US capital-goods import prices rose 1.5% in October, the biggest monthly increase in a series published monthly since December 1988.
- Preliminary US industrial production fell 0.4% from September even as manufacturing output increased 0.3%.
- CME’s November 17 commentary put December hike odds at 95% for 25 basis points and 5% for 50 basis points.
US prices for imported capital goods such as computers and machinery rose 1.5% in October from September, the biggest monthly increase since the Bureau of Labor Statistics began monthly publication in December 1988. Industrial production fell 0.4% in the Federal Reserve's preliminary estimate.
The two reports, released November 17, matter for Bitcoin traders who finance positions with borrowed dollars. Softer output can make a case for lower rates, while rising equipment costs show that price pressure extends beyond fuel. Before the Fed minutes, interest-rate futures pointed to higher rates into early 2027.
The BLS reported that computers, peripherals and semiconductors, electrical equipment and machinery drove the increase in capital-goods prices. Nonfuel import prices rose 0.8%, up from 0.5% in September. Fuel import prices rose 3.6% after rising 6.3% in September, and overall import prices rose 1.1% in October.
How much of the equipment price increase will reach consumers remains uncertain. The BLS also left some annual comparisons blank because the 2025 federal shutdown prevented the agency from collecting the year-earlier survey data.
The Fed's preliminary industrial production estimate put October's drop in output at 0.4% after a 0.7% rise in September. Utilities output fell 4.3% and mining fell 0.8%. Manufacturing rose 0.3% but edged down 0.1% excluding motor vehicles and parts. Overall production was still 2.1% higher than a year earlier.
Futures pricing points to a December Fed hike
The Fed held its policy target range at 3.75% to 4% in October, with two officials favoring a quarter-point increase. In its November 17 commentary, CME Group put the FedWatch odds of a quarter-point December hike at 95% and the odds of a half-point hike at 5%.
At 3:01 a.m. ET on November 18, with the effective federal funds rate at 3.88%, Frenzy Capital's estimates from CME fed funds futures put the expected effective rate at 4.14% after the Fed's December 9 decision, 4.32% after January 27 and 4.48% after March 17.
At 3:01 a.m. ET on Nov. 18, 2026, CME futures implied an effective rate of 4.141% after Dec. 9, 4.320% after Jan. 27 and 4.486% after Mar. 17. The observed rate was 3.880%.
The Fed explains how expected short-term rates can influence borrowing costs across the economy. For traders who borrow dollars to finance Bitcoin positions, that higher expected path can keep financing expensive even as parts of the economy slow. For crypto-backed borrowers, comparing loan rates and fees also means checking collateral requirements and repayment terms.
The Fed scheduled its October minutes for release at 2 p.m. ET on November 18. The October meeting took place before either November 17 report came out. The next test for traders is whether January and March rate expectations move after the minutes and before the Fed issues updated economic projections in December.
items.title: Bitcoin faces a new threat as US prices surge at fastest pace in 38 years

items.author: Jacob Lyon
items.content:
Ledger users buying wallets from Dubai-based Virgin outlets and German resellers have lost $1 million in a single day to suspected spyware-draining incidents.
X user “New Babylon Order” claimed $507,000 worth of USDT was stolen from his Ledger Stax device on November 14.
The device was said to have been bought brand new at official Ledger reseller Dubai Virgin Megastore on October 11, just two days after Ledger wallets sourced in Malaysia were drained for over $86 million.
They claim the seed phrase was generated on the device and remained private, suggesting the device contained spyware broadcasting the phrase to criminals.
New Babylon Order has since sent the device to a forensics lab and filed a report with Dubai police.
Another Virgin-sourced Ledger wallet drained
Another Ledger user, going by the username “Rewinsky,” claims they were drained of 1,300 SOL ($93,000) on November 14 after buying a $280 Ledger Flex wallet from the Dubai Virgin Megastore.
This device was opened and found containing spyware. Former Mt. Gox CEO Mark Karpelès confirmed the incident and said he was “sorry to hear about it.”
Read more: Ledger’s SDK snitched users’ transaction data and device info
Crypto analyst “Iris” discovered that Rewinsky’s crypto thieves also stole $630,000 from two Tron wallets belonging to another victim within seconds of the Ledger wallet draining.
$320K drained from German-sourced Ledger wallet
Today, a third user called “Mikaelxp14” claimed $320,000 was drained from his Ledger Flex wallet on November 14.
They say this wallet was purchased from the Germany-based official reseller MediaMarkt. They shared the transaction details, but there’s been no confirmation as to whether or not the wallet contains spyware.
Karpelès, however, asked to see the device interior and noted that “there is likely an antenna of some sorts there.”
Ledger says it found no evidence of MediaMarkt tampering
Multiple Ledger users were robbed of a collective $86 million in October after criminals installed spyware across devices sold by official Malaysian reseller Cryptobilis.
Ledger eventually asked multiple South Asia resellers to suspend sales, but said that it couldn’t find “any sign of tampering” with devices from its official German reseller MediaMarkt, and that “no loss of funds related to implants has been reported anywhere in Europe.”
One X user called “Johannes,” who claimed their MediaMarkt-purchased wallet contained spyware, says Ledger stopped responding to them after it received his package containing the tampered device.
Read more: Trezor cuts reseller network by 80% after finding more spy implants
Protos has reached out to Ledger and Virgin for comment and will update this piece should we hear anything back.
Bad year for hardware wallets
Ledger was also briefly serving malicious code this week as part of the Optimizely exploit that saw 186 major websites, including the BBC, CNN, and Zoom, inadvertently spreading crypto-stealing malware.
It’s also been a tough few months for Ledger rival, Trezor, which also discovered devices containing spy implants.
Trezor also suffered a third-party data breach this week that leaked the full names, phone numbers, delivery addresses, email addresses, and order date/details for 27,000 orders.
Got a tip? Send us an email securely via Protos Leaks. For more informed news and investigations, follow us on X, Bluesky, and Google News, or subscribe to our YouTube channel.
items.title: Ledger users drained for $1M in suspected spyware incidents

items.author: Decrypt Agent
items.content:
In brief
- A Leipzig judge has offered to end the trial of the alleged Movie2K operator if he hands over 40,000 BTC and pays €38 million ($42 million).
- Prosecutors believe the 43-year-old still holds around 56,000 BTC, meaning he could keep around 16,000 BTC, worth roughly €940 million ($1 billion).
- The deal comes as Germany prepares new powers to seize crypto of unclear origin, after selling nearly 50,000 BTC from the same case in 2024.
The alleged operator of defunct movie piracy site Movie2K could walk away from his trial in Germany and remain a billionaire, under a deal offered by the judge in the case.
The presiding judge at the Leipzig Regional Court has offered to drop tax evasion and money laundering charges against the 43-year-old main defendant if he hands over 40,000 BTC, public broadcaster MDR reported last week. He would also have to pay €38 million ($42 million) in compensation for potential victims, according to MDR.
Saxony's Office of the Public Prosecutor General confirmed the offer to news agency dpa, tech outlet heise reported on Tuesday. The 40,000 BTC would be worth around €2.36 billion ($2.6 billion) at current prices, according to heise.
But prosecutors believe the defendant holds a total of about 56,000 BTC. If he accepts, he could keep around 16,000 BTC, worth roughly €940 million ($1 billion) today and more than €1 billion when the offer was made.
A co-defendant has been offered a deal to hand over 600 BTC and pay €17 million ($19 million), and his lawyer said she could accept it, according to MDR. The main defendant's lawyers are considering the offer. The trial resumes on December 3 and could end before Christmas.
BTC price on November 22, 4:59PM UTC
Charges hard to prove
Movie2K offered hundreds of thousands of pirated films before shutting down in 2013. Its operators made money from advertising and subscription traps, and invested much of it in Bitcoin when it traded far below today's prices.
The copyright violations are time-barred, so the trial, which began in February, has focused on money laundering and tax evasion. The judge has reportedly expressed doubts about proving some of the charges, in part because legally and illegally acquired Bitcoin may have been mixed in the defendant's accounts, heise reported.
The main defendant was arrested abroad in 2023, and in early 2024 handed over nearly 50,000 BTC. Authorities in Saxony sold the coins later that year, raising about €2.64 billion ($2.9 billion), which is held in a state judicial treasury account. The money still belongs to the defendant until there is a final ruling, according to heise. Germany's government was left holding less than $300 million in Bitcoin after the sales.
Blockchain analytics firm Arkham said last year that German authorities had failed to seize some 45,000 BTC linked to the site.
The offer comes days after German lawmakers approved new powers allowing customs officials to seize assets, including crypto, of doubtful origin without first opening a criminal case. Under that law, owners of significant assets would have to show they were lawfully obtained.

items.author: Oluwapelumi Adejumo
items.content:
Quick Take
- US data center construction plunged 28% in Q3, marking its first quarterly decline in more than a year, according to Cleanview.
- The slowdown threatens momentum behind an estimated $1 trillion AI infrastructure buildout, with implications for chipmakers, utilities and investors.
- October's sharp rebound raises the prospect of a record fourth quarter, leaving questions about whether the slowdown will persist.
US data center construction fell 28% in the third quarter of 2026, marking its first quarterly decline in more than a year as questions mount over the sustainability of the artificial intelligence infrastructure boom.
According to data released by Cleanview, developers began construction on facilities representing 8.4 gigawatts of power capacity between July and September, down from a record 11.7 GW in the preceding quarter.
The number of buildings starting construction also fell to 65 from 96, although the quarter still ranked third-highest in Cleanview's records and was up 55% from the same period last year.
The slowdown raises questions about an industry whose expansion has become central to the global AI investment boom.
Michael Thomas, founder of Cleanview Energy, estimated that data centers whose construction began this year will cost approximately $1 trillion to build and equip. He said:
“A lasting slowdown would reach the utilities planning new power plants, the companies making chips and turbines, and a stock market that has bet heavily on AI.”
The findings are based on Cleanview's analysis of thousands of satellite images tracking construction activity at more than 1,300 data center buildings across the United States.
October rebound raises prospect of record quarter
Despite the third-quarter slowdown, construction activity rebounded sharply in October, with developers starting facilities representing 4.6 GW of capacity.
That was the second-highest monthly total Cleanview has recorded and nearly double the capacity that began construction in October 2025.
Three major projects accounted for approximately 35% of the month's activity. These included 720 megawatts at Nscale's Monarch campus in West Virginia, 461 MW at Related Digital's Stargate Michigan campus and 450 MW at Crusoe's Abilene campus in Texas.
Together, the projects represented approximately 1.63 GW of new construction starts, highlighting the scale of investment still flowing into AI infrastructure.
In view of this, Thomas said it was too early to conclude that the third-quarter decline signaled a lasting slowdown.
This is because October's strong rebound could push fourth-quarter construction starts to a record 14 GW if the pace continues through November and December.
items.title: America’s $1 trillion AI data center boom just suffered its first slowdown in over a year

Anthropic IPO引爆散户热情，首日净买入约2.5亿美元，达SpaceX两倍

BlockBeats 消息，11 月 18 日，随着 Anthropic 计划于周四登陆纳斯达克，散户投资者参与热情高涨。Vanda Research 预计，Anthropic 上市首日散户净买入规模可能达到约 2.5 亿美元，约为 SpaceX IPO 首日散户净买入规模的两倍，这也将创下该机构追踪数据中的单日散户净买入纪录。

Anthropic 计划以每股 70 至 78 美元的价格发行 8.25 亿股，股票代码为 ANT，消息人士称最终发行价可能高于这一范围。散户投资者预计最多可获得本次 IPO 发行份额的 20%。按此前发行区间上限计算，公司估值约为 1.405 万亿美元，募资规模最高可达 644 亿美元。

不过，市场对本次 IPO 的态度并非一致。部分散户看好 Anthropic 的 AI 领先地位，愿意积极参与认购；也有投资者担忧估值过高、宏观金融环境趋紧以及 IPO 配售份额有限，选择等待上市后回调再买入。

Vanda Research 策略师 Jai Malhi 表示，目前散户和机构投资者均有充足资金参与此次 IPO。与今年 6 月 SpaceX 上市时市场情绪高涨不同，当前 AI 交易正经历调整，投资者情绪相对低迷，反而可能降低 Anthropic 超出市场预期的难度。

Anthropic 截至 9 月 30 日的九个月营收已超过 330 亿美元，同比增长 1200%，但公司累计支出承诺约达 9000 亿美元，主要用于算力和基础设施。市场仍在关注其巨额 AI 投资能否持续转化为实际收入和利润。

items.author: Bennett Tomlin
items.content:
There was a brief period, driven by mania around Michael Saylor’s BTC treasury firm Strategy — then called MicroStrategy — when companies became convinced that holding crypto was a surefire path to stock market success.
However, investor sensibilities have shifted, and many digital asset treasury firms have found it difficult to sustain their market valuations.
Protos has used public filings and stock market data to analyze the performance of several of these firms.
Many of these firms have failed to perform as well as the token they hold, in some cases, like Justin Sun-advised Tron Inc, quite egregiously.
Justin Sun’s daddy’s firm
Tron Inc. is a TRON (TRX) digital asset treasury firm chaired by Weike Sun, Justin’s father.
Controversially, the firm received its TRX from Justin Sun-owned HTX, even after HTX was sanctioned.
The public markets have buffeted this firm, which is down approximately 87% from its peak.
Read more: Justin Sun’s TRON stock nears delisting price
As disclosed by Tron itself, it holds its TRX at TEySEZLJf6rs2mCujGpDEsgoMVWKLAk9mT.
This has allowed Protos to document its TRX holdings over time.
Tron has also become a “Super Representative” on the TRON network, validating transactions and earning fees from this line of business.
However, it’s worth noting that Tron is one of the digital asset treasury firms that still trades above the value of its crypto, measured in this case by its multiple to net asset value (mNAV).
Does Strategy have a strategy?
Strategy is the archetypal digital asset treasury firm, leading the pivot years ago with its BTC acquisitions.
It’s also a rare example of a firm that’s outperformed BTC over that period.
More recently, it’s moved away from simply purchasing BTC to increasingly complex financial instruments like its STRC.
It’s even started to sell its BTC holdings, occasionally.
Despite these sales, it’s still acquired a massive trove of BTC, representing over 4% of the asset mined so far.
Read more: Why Saylor’s STRC isn’t really a money market or bank account
Strategy’s software and business intelligence business lines are nearly entirely vestigial, not meaningfully affecting the firm’s financials compared to its BTC bets.
Tether’s troubled play
Twenty One is the Tether-related firm that has underperformed compared to the BTC it holds.
While BTC has lost about a quarter of its value, Twenty One has plummeted 63%.
Read more: Jack Mallers leaves Twenty One after overseeing 91% decline
It’s also not acquired much BTC.
The firm also replaced its earlier chief executive, Jack Mallers with Raphael Zagury.
SoftBank, which was involved in the launch of this firm, also sold its stake to Tether.
Zagury claims the firm is “evaluating opportunities across mining, lending, treasury, and energy.”
Newer isn’t always better
Evernorth Holdings, a recently launched XRP digital asset treasury firm, has struggled immediately.
This firm has lost over half of its value in the little over a month since it has listed and is rapidly approaching the value of its XRP holdings.
Read more: XRP treasury firm Evernorth Holdings falls to new low
Can it sustain the hype?
One of the exceptions to the general pattern is Hyperliquid Strategies, which has increased substantially since its listing but is down 44% from its peak.
Though realistically, these values have tracked each other very closely, with the firm trading slightly below the value of its crypto holdings as of November 17.
Why not just use an ETF?
Read more: Bitcoin crashes below $60K after 13 days of ETF outflows
Fundamentally, it seems like digital asset treasury firms are struggling to figure out what differentiates them in an environment with increasingly diverse crypto-focused ETFs.
Firms that just hold crypto aren’t providing a meaningful differentiation from these offerings, and firms that introduce other types of financial engineering, like Strategy are introducing new types of risk as well.
Meanwhile, firms that hoped to invest in or acquire firms related to the token they hold face the problem that Zagury described in a letter to Twenty One shareholders, namely, “A bad acquisition can destroy years of value creation.”
Though the amount of value creation performed is a matter of debate.

items.author: Cointelegraph by Korbinian Kettnaker
items.content:
Bitcoin Covenants Part 6: FE Covenants — Enforcing covenants through cryptographically restricted signing keys
FE covenants encode spending constraints into the signing key, so only transactions that satisfy a predefined condition can be signed.
This is Part 6 in the technical article series about Bitcoin covenants by Cointelegraph Research. To read the previous article, click here.
Changing Bitcoin’s consensus rules is not merely a technical process. It requires that the network’s node operators, miners, developers and economic actors coordinate around a change. This coordination is difficult to achieve, which is why Bitcoin’s base layer has gradually ossified.
Researchers have spent the last several years investigating whether covenant behavior could be enforced without touching consensus rules. In May 2024, Jeremy Rubin, the original author of the OP_CTV proposal (BIP-119), offered an answer in a paper titled FE’d Up Covenants. His design proposed using functional encryption (FE) to move the covenant out of Bitcoin Script and into the signing key.
In ordinary public-key cryptography, a private key can sign any message. In hypothetical FE-based covenants, signing would be restricted to a predefined set of valid transactions. Bitcoin nodes would verify the signature with OP_CHECKSIG exactly as they do today, obviating the need for a soft fork.
Functional encryption: keys that only sign what the rules allow
Functional encryption (FE) generalizes public-key encryption. In ordinary cryptographic schemes, a private key can be used to fully decrypt a ciphertext and arrive at the plaintext. In FE, a master secret is instead used to issue subsidiary functional keys, each of which reveals only one chosen function of the plaintext. The holder of the functional key for a function f and the ciphertext of a secret x can compute f(x) but never gets to reveal x as a plaintext message.
In the academic literature, FE was first formalized by Dan Boneh, Amit Sahai and Brent Waters in 2011. Constructions for arbitrary functions followed from 2013, with polynomial runtime but overheads far beyond the resources of current computing technology. Furthermore, their security rested on new, untested building blocks called multilinear maps. Only in 2021 did researchers develop constructions from well-founded cryptographic assumptions, which could in principle open the door to practical implementations of FE.
The f in an FE scheme can be any feasibly computable function. However, in Bitcoin covenant constructions, f is a signing function. Its output is a Bitcoin signature for a transaction tx. Because this signature depends on both a private key and the transaction that is being signed, it takes at least two inputs, which is why Rubin’s design uses multi-input FE. For a covenant that only permits a single spending transaction, akin to OP_CTV, two inputs suffice. General, expressive constructions take more arguments, as in Rubin’s f(k, tx, program, proof).
Crucially, f does not sign directly with the private key k that is supplied in an encrypted form. Instead, the function derives a new key pair by tweaking k with a hash of the covenant’s spending policy. Signatures produced by f are valid for the tweaked public key, not for the base public key P itself.
Setting up FE-based covenants
To enable FE-based covenants from these primitives, a setup authority is required. It generates a Bitcoin key pair (the private key k and the public key P) as well as an FE key pair (the master secret msk and the FE public key mpk). It publishes P, mpk, k encrypted to mpk, and the functional key for f, which it derives from msk. The setup authority then needs to be trusted to destroy k and msk. Otherwise, it could sign spends that violate the covenant. With this setup completed, an indefinite number of new covenants may be created.
Every covenant has its own dedicated key pair, obtained by tweaking (k, P) with the spending policy. The private key of this tweaked key pair exists only inside f and is never revealed. The public key can be derived from P by anyone who knows the hash of the desired spending policy. This way, covenant receiving addresses can be generated. In practice, the receiving address would commit to a 2-of-2 script that requires a signature from a key the user controls alongside the FE signature. This is to keep unauthorized parties from triggering a transaction permitted by the covenant.
To create an FE signature for a covenant spend, the signer takes a tx that conforms to the spending policy and encrypts it to mpk. Using the encrypted tx, together with the encrypted k and the functional key published by the authority, they can then evaluate f. The function f signs tx with k tweaked by the hash of the spending policy. A transaction that breaks the spending policy of the address that holds the coins could at best be signed for some other, differently tweaked public key that does not control the funds.The function f can also be designed to block such a signature outright.
The general version of FE-based covenants with f(k, tx, program, proof) is strictly more expressive than OP_CTV. The general function proposed by Rubin takes a program that checks a condition on the transaction at spend time, and a zero-knowledge proof that the program accepts the transaction.
This zero-knowledge proof facilitates the implementation of the FE scheme, but does not add to it conceptually. A single fixed f works either way. Without the proof, f would have to be a general interpreter that runs any given program on tx itself. Such an f is large and costly to evaluate under FE. With the proof, f only has to verify a succinct proof. This could make it possible to enforce arbitrarily complex covenants without the need for more complexity in f. The proof also lets a spending policy depend on data outside the transaction, such as the result of an off-chain computation.
Why FE-based covenants remain infeasible for now
Goldwasser et al. (2014) introduced multi-input FE and built it on indistinguishability obfuscation. Multi-input FE and obfuscation are known to imply one another. Ananth and Jain (2015) showed that even single-input FE for general circuits yields obfuscation once it is made compact. The cryptographic primitive this design needs is therefore at least as hard to build as so-called indistinguishability obfuscation itself. Implementations of this principle remain at toy scale.
Carmer, Malozemoff and Raykova (2017) needed 3.7 hours to obfuscate a 12-bit pseudorandom function, a toy circuit of about 62,000 gates with a 64-bit key, far smaller than ECDSA signing on 256-bit numbers. The obfuscated program took 120 GB of disk space, and an evaluation ran for 67 minutes with 128 GB of RAM. The cost of implementing such a scheme would fall on whoever produces the signature, not on Bitcoin nodes. The authors called this “still far from practical.”
Furthermore, FE schemes that are practical cover only narrow function classes, such as the inner products of Abdalla et al. (2015), and the type of ECDSA signing required for Bitcoin covenants is not among them. Rubin’s paper concedes this point and lists under-developed cryptography and the setup trust assumption among its downsides. CTV-style opcodes remain far more efficient in bytes and verification, but require a base-layer change.
In our next article, we turn to Un-FE’d Covenants, which Rubin proposed to approximate covenant behavior without relying on impractical FE schemes. It replaces FE with oracle signers bonded through BitVM. [alloc]init’s Bitcoin PIPEs began in 2024 as an FE design and moved in 2026 to witness encryption. This proposal will also be covered in a follow-up article.
items.title: Bitcoin Covenants Part 6: FE Covenants — Enforcing covenants through cryptographically restricted signing keys

CoinShares sells all treasury ETH, halves SOL holdings for buybacks
The October sales raised $19.3 million, nearly half the $40 million CoinShares can spend on buybacks before its next annual meeting.
European digital asset manager CoinShares sold its entire Ether treasury position and half of its Solana treasury holdings in October, raising $19.3 million to fund share buybacks.
CoinShares raised $16.6 million from the Ether sale and $2.7 million from the Solana sale, the company said in its third-quarter results on Wednesday.
CoinShares reported treasury holdings of 6,562 Ether (ETH) at a fair value of $17.6 million and 50,213 Solana (SOL) valued at $5.9 million as of Sept. 30. The company also held 235 Bitcoin (BTC) worth $19.6 million at quarter-end.
CoinShares’ board approved up to $40 million in buybacks on Oct. 22 under a five-year authorization that shareholders granted in September. The authorization covers up to 32.9 million shares, or 25% of shares outstanding. The $40 million program runs until the company’s next annual meeting, expected in the second quarter of 2027.
“That’s nearly half of the $40 million authorized by the Board and gives us the flexibility to act when conditions allow,” said Jean-Marie Mognetti, co-founder, president and CEO of CoinShares, referring to the sale proceeds in a Wednesday press release.
CoinShares also reported $7.4 billion in total assets under management, up from $5.5 billion at the end of June, driven by rising crypto prices and $125 million in net inflows during the quarter. Revenue fell 45% from a year earlier to $27.7 million, including $19.1 million in asset management fees.
CoinShares’ shares fell 5.41% to close at $3.15 on Tuesday, ahead of the earnings report, leaving them down 63% from their $8.61 close on the company’s April 1 Nasdaq debut.
Related: Crypto adoption blooming in Germany, while UK is falling ‘behind,’ says CoinShares researcher

Morning Minute is a daily newsletter written by Tyler Warner. The analysis and opinions expressed are his own and do not necessarily reflect those of Decrypt. And check out our daily news show 'FOMO HOUR' covering all of the top stories and market action.

🖥️ Nvidia Beats, Board Says ‘No’ on Jensen
Six days after Jensen Huang resigned as CEO of the company he co-founded 33 years ago, Nvidia delivered the best quarter in its history. And told him he isn’t coming back.
The numbers first.
- Revenue of $115.8 billion, up 103% from a year ago, against roughly $109.1 billion expected.
- Data center alone was $107.6 billion, up 110% and now 93% of the company.
- GAAP net income of $65.3 billion, more than double last year.
- Adjusted earnings of $2.68 a share against $2.47 expected.
Fourth-quarter guidance came in at $130 billion against the $125.3 billion Wall Street wanted, with China assumed at zero.
And the CFO raised their 2028 revenue outlook to 75% year-over-year growth.
Just an absolute smash all around.
Then board chair Harvey Jones got on the call and said it plainly. “The Nvidia board does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO.” The directors unanimously accepted his resignation, and Jones declined to answer anything about the circumstances or the independent investigation still running.
Huang had publicly offered to come back hours earlier, saying he would do it if directors believed it served shareholders and employees. Trump and Elon Musk both backed the idea. A petition passed 182,000 signatures including nearly 9,000 self-identified Nvidia employees. None of it moved the room.
Nvidia has hired Heidrick & Struggles to run the permanent search. Colette Kress stays interim CEO while remaining CFO, with Jones saying the board has “every confidence in Colette’s leadership, integrity and ability to deliver.” The board also created a National Security and Export Control Oversight Committee, chaired by director Suzanne Nora Johnson, to receive reports from the company’s national security and trade compliance teams.
And after all of that—the stock rose about 3%.
A 6% revenue beat, guidance $5 billion above consensus, a new product cycle shipping, and the market gave it two percent. Shares sit roughly 35% below their October peak near $240. Nvidia perps on Hyperliquid were doing nearly a billion dollars of daily volume through the week, bouncing off $150 before settling near $162.
As for impact on the broader AI trade, Nvidia proved AI demand is not collapsing. You cannot manufacture $107.6 billion of data center revenue, and margins at 74.8% mean nobody is discounting to move product. The demand-collapse thesis died on Tuesday.
Two details do belong to the bears though. Growth is decelerating from 103% to roughly 77% once you strip the extra week out of Q4 guidance. And gross margin guides down about three points, from 74.8% to between 71% and 72%. Slowing growth plus compressing margins is how multiples come down regardless of how big the absolute numbers get.
The honest read is that the AI business is fine and the AI trade has stopped responding to it. For crypto that matters more than it should, because the correlation that dragged Bitcoin from $87,000 to the low $60s over six weeks ran through this exact trade.
Now we wait for the Fed on December 9 and insight into the 2027 rate hike cycle (or lack thereof) to determine the likely near-term fate.

items.author: Cointelegraph by Helen Partz
items.content:
Sanctions fears loom over Russia’s regulated crypto trading launch
Russia’s crypto trading rollout faces uncertainty as companies weigh sanctions exposure, while Moscow Exchange prepares to launch crypto trading in December.
Russia’s push to bring cryptocurrency trading under government oversight is raising concerns that greater transparency could expose market participants to international sanctions.
Some companies are reluctant to join the Bank of Russia’s public registry of crypto exchangers because they fear becoming sanctions targets, a person familiar the regulatory discussions told Cointelegraph on Wednesday.
Industry representatives repeatedly asked the central bank to keep the registry private, but the regulator refused, arguing that crypto businesses should follow the same requirements as traditional financial service providers, the source said.
The concerns come as the European Union prepares its 22nd sanctions package against Russia, which is expected to include new restrictions on crypto platforms.
Russia’s crypto registry grows to 30 but trading launch remains blurry
Russia’s new rules allowing retail investors to buy Bitcoin (BTC), Ether (ETH) and Tether’s USDt (USDT) took effect on Monday, and the central bank’s registry listed 30 authorized exchange operators as of Wednesday.
The list includes major lenders Sberbank and VTB, but registration alone does not establish whether customers can already complete transactions.
Related: KuCoin suspends services in Russia and Belarus
Alexander Nam of HSE University’s Center for Decentralized Finance and Digital Financial Assets Research said the market still faces technical and regulatory hurdles, including investor testing, order execution, settlement and custody.
“Being included in the registry does not in itself mean readiness to fully serve investors,” Nam told Cointelegraph.
Alexander Brazhnikov of the Russian Association of Cryptocurrency and Blockchain told Cointelegraph that he could not identify a registered operator offering confirmed retail access as of Monday.
EU sanctions plans loom over Russia’s December crypto launch
Moscow Exchange (MOEX), Russia’s main securities trading venue, plans to launch crypto trading on Dec. 1, with investors accessing the market through brokers rather than directly through the exchange. Cointelegraph contacted VTB, T-Invest Lab and MOEX for further details on their respective crypto trading launch plans but had not received responses by publication time.
The European Commission reportedly plans to present its next sanctions package ahead of a Nov. 26–27 European Council summit, days before MOEX’s scheduled launch.
Russian President Vladimir Putin said Wednesday that Western sanctions had backfired and strengthened Russia’s economy, speaking at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shenzhen.
Russia’s broader crypto activity has declined despite its push to establish a regulated trading market. The value of cryptocurrency transactions fell 14.7% to $284.1 billion in the year ended June 2026, according to Chainalysis. The country still accounted for roughly 44% of Eastern Europe’s crypto activity.

高利率持续挤压企业偿债能力，全球信用市场或迎新一轮违约潮

BlockBeats 消息，11 月 18 日，据彭博报道，多家大型资产管理机构高管在彭博伦敦全球信用论坛上警告，全球信用市场正进入新一轮风险释放阶段。彭博调查显示，超过 90% 的受访者预计，低评级公司到 2027 年末的违约率将高于今年，摩根大通分析师则预计，杠杆贷款违约规模将同比增长逾一倍。

高利率持续加重企业偿债压力，市场对美联储和欧洲央行下月加息 25 个基点的预期升温，若加息落地，浮动利率债务占比较高的杠杆企业将面临更高融资成本。Davidson Kempner 全球信用部门联席主管 Chris Krishanthan 表示，市场中已经出现真实的恐慌情绪。

软件行业成为信用风险的重点领域。随着人工智能带来的行业颠覆风险加剧，部分高负债软件企业的经营前景承压，债权人与股权投资者在债务处置问题上陷入僵局。凯雷集团联席总裁 Mark Jenkins 表示，双方目前都不愿率先让步，但相关企业的债务问题最终仍需要解决。

与此同时，私募信用市场也面临流动性和增长压力。尽管 2026 年上半年的基金赎回压力近期有所缓解，但行业仍受到市场审视。Ares Management 欧洲直接贷款联席主管 Matthew Theodorakis 表示，赎回压力较上半年已有所消散，但行业需要通过实际投资业绩证明自身策略的有效性。

items.author: Cointelegraph by Christina Comben
items.content:
How to preserve wealth and access funds during a national emergency
As geopolitical and technological threats multiply, the big question is whether you can hold on to your wealth and access funds when the system fails.
Amid kinetic war, cyberattacks and the prospect of the power grid failing, governments around the world have been encouraging citizens to prepare for major disruption.
In the UK, citizens have been stocking up on tinned food and bottled water in response to the government’s Be Ready campaign.
With fighter jets streaking across the skies of the Middle East, talk of a dirty bomb attack on Washington and the world’s largest software company going offline for a day, the possibility of disaster striking close to home is starting to look more realistic.
But what do you do with your money in times like these? How can you protect your wealth, but still be able to access it when the system fails?
There are two key aspects: choosing assets that maintain value even as the world goes up in flames, and being able to access funds during an emergency.
On the first point Maximilian Kunkel, chief investment officer for ultra-high-net-worth clients at UBS Global Wealth Management, tells Magazine, “We would caution against thinking of any single asset as ‘safe’ in all circumstances.”
Instead, he says wealthy investors should focus on building a portfolio that is “resilient across different scenarios,” with enough liquidity and diversification across asset classes, currencies and geographies.
Bitcoin, gold and the limits of ‘safe’ havens
The corporation’s 2026 global family office report, representing families with an average net worth of $2.7 billion, found 64% cited major geopolitical conflict as a concern over the next 12 months. These investors are not flocking to crypto for wealth preservation however.
“24% of family offices reported exposure to crypto or digital assets, but among those invested, allocations were typically only around 1%.”
Hadley Stern, head of institutions at Silence Laboratories and founder of Fidelity Digital Assets, explains that financial institutions may now place Bitcoin in the same category as gold, but it does not yet enjoy the same reputation as a safe haven.
“Gold has thousands of years of history [...] Bitcoin has less than two decades. But the reasoning people use is the same: a scarce asset that isn’t anyone else’s liability,” he says.
Related: Will gold’s ‘infinite mint bug’ make Bitcoin more valuable?
He advises against using it as a reliable hedge in a crisis; “I’d be careful with the hedge story,” he says. “Bitcoin is still volatile, and in a sell-off it often trades like other risk assets.”
Cash, by contrast, is handy for emergencies “for liquidity and paying bills,” but not for “holding value over long stretches,” he says.
Michael D’Alessio, chief operating officer at digital asset trading platform Talos, tells Magazine, there are early signs that Bitcoin is beginning to behave more like gold. He said that through the volatility around the US midterm elections Bitcoin’s correlation with equities remained high. However, over the same period, its correlation with gold also rose sharply, to around 0.75 on a 30-day basis as of early August:
“That’s a meaningful shift, and it’s exactly the kind of signal institutional desks are now watching.”
BTC vs gold, 30-day rolling correlation of daily returns. Source: Talos/Coin Metrics
The risk is not just losing money; it’s losing access
The collapse of Mt Gox, or more recently the failure of Paraguay’s Ueno Bank show that “the asset is only as safe as the system holding it,” according to Stern.
Rather than automatically moving into Bitcoin or gold when tensions rise, risk committees are asking different questions:
“Where is the asset? Which jurisdiction is it in? Who can freeze it? What happens if a counterparty or a payment rail is down for a week?” he says. “Those used to be back-office questions. Now they come up at the board level.”
Kunkel said that concern over major geopolitical conflict is encouraging wealthy families to consider “not only asset allocation, but also where assets are held, currency exposure, liquidity and jurisdictional diversification.”
The UBS report found that 88% of family offices hold bankable assets in two or more jurisdictions, while 30% are increasing or considering increasing currency diversification.
Related: Half of UK wealth advisers say clients’ crypto is ‘invisible’ to them: CoinShares survey
The institutional version of a full pantry
Fortunately the banks and custody providers are making practical disaster preparations too.
“Regulators expect firms to plan for severe but plausible events,” Stern explains, such as a cloud outage, a cyberattack, a key vendor failing or a market closed for days, and “show they can keep their most important services running through them.”
The UK government is advising citizens to stock up on supplies. Source: Gov.uk
For custody providers, that means testing whether assets can still be moved if a signing location goes offline, and how quickly operations can recover if a data center is lost. Stern says while households might prep for an emergency by stocking a full pantry:
“The institutional version is not depending on any single thing: one custodian, one key holder, one cloud, one bank.”
Similarly investors need to work out which assets you can reach quickly and which you can’t, and “keeping enough liquidity to get through a bad stretch without being forced to sell.”
Kunkel says capital preservation “does not mean eliminating volatility, but maintaining enough liquidity and diversification to withstand volatility” without becoming a forced seller.
When the balloon goes up, diversification can protect a portfolio from a market shock, but it can’t guarantee access to funds if the infrastructure supporting it fails. A safe haven isn’t just about owning the right things; it’s about being able to access them when the system stops working.

items.author: Oluwapelumi Adejumo
items.content:
Quick Take
- Bitcoin's crash toward $62,000 added approximately 66,000 BTC to a key short-term-holder cost-basis band, Glassnode reported.
- Nearly 20% of short-term holders' coins now sit between $62,000 and $66,000, making the region critical to Bitcoin's next move.
- Exchange buying signals are improving, but fading Coinbase demand raises questions about whether the support zone can withstand another selloff.
Bitcoin's plunge toward $62,000 on Nov. 15 coincided with a sharp increase in coins concentrated around the selloff low, potentially strengthening a key support zone.
In its Nov. 17 report, Glassnode estimated that approximately 66,000 BTC entered the $62,000 to $66,000 short-term-holder cost-basis band during the two heaviest days of selling.
The price range, which initially formed around Bitcoin's August low, now accounts for roughly 20% of short-term holders' coins, making it an important level to watch if selling pressure returns.
Bitcoin buyers emerge around key support zone
Exchange trading data suggests buyers have begun absorbing some selling pressure after the crash.
Glassnode reported that sellers dominated trading during the selloff before buyer-initiated volume overtook seller-initiated activity in the 24 hours preceding its Nov. 17 snapshot.
Standing buy orders within 5% of Bitcoin's market price also outweighed sell orders by approximately 2.3 to 1 across Binance and Coinbase. The largest single Binance buy level since August was near $60,000.
However, the recovery in buying demand has been uneven.
Bitcoin briefly traded at a premium on Coinbase during the Nov. 15 crash, but that advantage disappeared by Nov. 17. A separate Coinbase Premium Index from Axel Adler Jr. showed Bitcoin trading at a 0.110% discount on Coinbase relative to Binance that day.
More recent trading activity nevertheless suggests renewed buying interest.
With Bitcoin trading as high as $65,365 in the last 24 hours, Blockmetric data showed aggressive buying on Binance's spot market exceeded selling by about $5.5 million during the six hours ending at 07:54 UTC.
The platform also recorded $12.7 million in standing Binance buy orders between $62,500 and $62,600, reinforcing the evidence of demand around the lower end of Glassnode's support zone.
The combination of growing holder concentration and stronger exchange buying suggests the $62,000 to $66,000 region could play an important role in Bitcoin's next price move.
If Bitcoin retreats toward $62,000, the critical test will be whether buyers can absorb renewed selling pressure. Sustained buyer-led trading and a recovery in Coinbase's premium would strengthen the case for the support zone holding.
items.title: Bitcoin buyers pile 66,000 BTC into critical $62,000 support zone

items.content:
Tokenized Nvidia market cap surges 159% amid Jensen Huang’s exit
Nvidia stock tokens reached $401.9 million in combined value as Jensen Huang stepped down and the chipmaker posted record quarterly revenue.
The combined market value of tokenized stocks tied to Nvidia shares rose about 159% from Nov. 8 to Tuesday, while the chipmaker’s Nasdaq-listed shares fell nearly 17% from their last close before co-founder Jensen Huang publicly admitted to an extramarital affair.
The value of Nvidia (NVDA) tokens tracked by Token Terminal rose from $155 million on Nov. 8 to $401.9 million by Tuesday.
Nvidia shed about $750 billion in market value, falling from $4.5 trillion at the Nov. 6 close to $3.75 trillion at Tuesday’s close, according to Yahoo Finance data.
Huang acknowledged the affair in a message to Nvidia employees on Nov. 8, nearly two weeks after The New York Times reported that US intelligence officials suspected Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang of spying for Beijing. China denied the allegations.
Related: ARK sells $85M in Nvidia shares ahead of chipmaker’s Q3 earnings results
Nvidia supplies chips that cloud providers such as Google Cloud and Microsoft Azure use to train and run AI models, making its earnings a gauge of global spending on AI infrastructure.
Tokenized stocks are blockchain tokens designed to track the price of a share. In one common setup, an issuer creates tokens backed by shares held by a custodian.
Binance, for example, lists an Nvidia token that can trade when Nasdaq is closed. It gives investors exposure to Nvidia’s share price without shareholder rights. The market value can rise as more tokens enter circulation, even if Nvidia’s share price falls.
Nvidia posts record revenue after Huang’s exit
Huang resigned as president and CEO of Nvidia and stepped down from the company’s board Thursday. Nvidia named Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress interim CEO.
On Tuesday, Nvidia’s board said it “does not intend to reinstate” Huang, shortly after the chipmaker reported record third-quarter revenue of $115.8 billion, up 103% from a year earlier and above Wall Street estimates. Data center sales more than doubled to $107.6 billion, accounting for about 93% of total revenue. Nvidia forecast fourth-quarter sales of about $130 billion.
Nvidia’s shares rose 2.82% to $159.80 in Wednesday premarket trading as of 12:50 pm UTC (07:50 am ET), according to Yahoo Finance.

items.author: Ryan Gladwin
items.content:
In brief
- President Trump’s TRUMP meme coin hit an all-time low of $0.896 over the weekend and is down almost 40% since the midterms.
- Analysts say the Democrats taking Congress, and their plans to use subpoena power on Trump’s crypto ventures, add more pressure.
- They expect the token to keep declining whether or not Trump is in office, pointing to its lack of utility and a large share of supply still to unlock.
President Trump's official meme coin has reached new lows since he suffered a major blow in the U.S. midterm elections. The token has dropped almost 40% since election day, and analysts warn that new congressional scrutiny could push it lower.
Over the weekend, the TRUMP coin touched $0.896, marking the lowest point the token had ever stooped. It has since bumped 8%, sitting at $0.965, which is still down almost 40% from election day and 98.7% from its all-time high of $73.43, set the day after it launched, per Decrypt data.
Luke Nolan, senior researcher at CoinShares, told Decrypt the midterms "added pressure to an already struggling token." Trading volume increased around the vote, and he believes some traders had bet on a Republican surprise win. He said there was a "visible unwind" that led to a "sharp drawdown" after the election results rolled out.
"Democrats take both chambers in January and plan to use their subpoena power on his crypto ventures. His net approval rating has almost never been lower," Max Shannon, senior associate at Bitwise Europe, told Decrypt. "It is still possible this continues to decline and, therefore, has a negative effect on these Trump-affiliated assets."
Other Trump-linked assets have also taken a hit. Since the election, World Liberty Financial's WLFI token has dropped 7.5%, per Decrypt data, and shares of the Trump Media & Technology Group have dropped 32%.
What is TRUMP?
Trump launched TRUMP on January 17, 2025, three days before his second inauguration, which Shannon described as "close to the peak of his popularity." Since then, the coin has faced significant scrutiny over how much the President and his family have profited from it. (The First Lady following suit and launching her own meme coin didn't help matters.)
The president’s crypto ventures also became a sticking point for the Clarity Act, a bill that aimed to provide a formal legal structure for most cryptocurrency activity. Democrats scrutinized the Trump family's involvement in the crypto industry, which profited them more than $1 billion in a year.
A July draft would have barred public officials and employees, along with their spouses, from issuing or sponsoring digital assets while in office. That draft didn’t extend to officials’ children, including Don Jr. and Eric Trump, and the provision would have expired in January 2029.
The bill failed a key Senate procedural vote in September. Patrick Witt, former executive director of the President’s Council of Advisers for Digital Assets, later said the “political issue of ethics really consumed everything else.”
TRUMP has "no value accrual, and it has been left in the dust of this narrative," Shannon said. "Google Trends shows searches for $TRUMP essentially flatlining since June 2025."
Nolan agreed, saying the coin’s appeal was "largely speculative," with no clear link between holding it and sharing in any underlying business success. The most it offered, he said, was the exclusive dinner to the top holders, which was both popular and controversial, depending on who you asked.
"In my view, that was just an attempt to prop up the token without actually creating any long-term demand for it," he said.
Interest in these dinners has dried up too. Ahead of the third gala scheduled for the event of the month, 185 holders of the token were invited to register, but only 130 wallets showed on the final leaderboard. Those wallets held a combined $8.6 billion worth of TRUMP, according to Reuters, which is a 94% decline from the first dinner.
Then there's the "unappealing" token supply structure, Nolan said. The majority of tokens were allocated to Trump-linked entities and are being slowly unlocked, which means demand needs to keep growing to soak up newly injected supply.
"That is a difficult position for an asset whose main attraction is attention around one individual," he said.
And what happens when Trump loses power? He has said he "would love" to serve a third term, but that remains unconstitutional—so the clock is ticking on his presidency.
"I think overall Trump leaving office probably means the token continues its gradual decline," Nolan told Decrypt. "Any big Trump headlines probably make it experience the same dead cat bounces (sharp rallies) we have seen it have during short periods of time."
Shannon thinks Trump doesn't even need to lose power for the token to keep going down. He said that it is "incredibly unlikely" that the token reclaims its highs, as it would require it to boost 82x, too many investors have been burned, and the majority of the supply is still to be unlocked.
"I think the meme coin was doomed from the start, and like with most meme coins, creating long-term demand is a Sisyphean task," Nolan told Decrypt.

BlockBeats 消息，11 月 18 日，据德国通讯社（DPA）报道，一名德国法官提议，若 Movie2k 案件被告交出 4 万枚 BTC（按当前价格约合 26 亿美元），可考虑撤销相关案件。与今年 4 月提出的方案相比，此次条件有所变化：此前方案要求被告转交约 5.6 万枚 BTC，并以缓刑作为处理条件；新方案下，被告仍可保留约 1.6 万枚 BTC。

德国政府此前已于 2024 年夏季出售从 Movie2k 案件中没收的约 5 万枚 BTC，套现约 29 亿美元。此次法官提出的方案仍属于提议，案件是否撤销及最终处置条件尚待确认。

Anthropic IPO将为早期投资者带来巨额回报

BlockBeats 消息，11 月 18 日，2025 年，投资公司 Iconiq 对 Anthropic PBC 进行首次投资时，这家人工智能开发企业的估值已达 1830 亿美元——超过了全球几乎所有其他科技初创企业。如今，Anthropic 正在稳步成长为人工智能领域的巨头。随着该公司即将登陆华尔街，Iconiq 的投资也有望带来巨额回报。

据知情人士透露，Iconiq 已经向 Anthropic 注资超过 60 亿美元，按照后者最新 9650 亿美元的私募估值，目前 Iconiq 持股价值约为 170 亿美元。如果 Anthropic 如一些人所预期的那样，以高达 2 万亿美元的估值完成公开募股，Iconiq 的这笔投资——也是该公司历史上最大的一笔交易——价值可能会翻一番。

Anthropic 即将进行的公开上市，有望为自 2021 年该公司成立以来支持它的顶级风投机构、科技企业及独立投资者创造数十亿美元的回报。受益者名单中既有具有远见卓识的早期投资者，也包括相对较晚入场的投资者，他们因该公司过去一年来的迅猛崛起和估值飙升而获益。

苹果成AI动荡中的避险选择，估值跻身市场最高之列

BlockBeats 消息，11 月 18 日，过去几周，大型科技股经历剧烈动荡，美国中期选举以及黄仁勋突然被英伟达罢免继续冲击市场。但有一只股票在动荡中始终保持坚挺：苹果。投资者纷纷抛售与人工智能相关的股票，从芯片制造商、超大规模云服务商到新兴云服务商无一幸免，苹果股价却继续稳步走高。

今年以来，该股已上涨 29%，是科技「七巨头」中表现最好的股票，遥遥领先其他成员，同时也是标普 500 指数上涨的最大推动力量，对该指数今年 7.2% 的涨幅贡献了 28%。与此同时，苹果还以 5.1 万亿美元市值成为全球市值最高的公司。

原因相当简单。在许多超大市值竞争对手投入巨资追逐 AI 之际，苹果基本置身于这场竞赛之外，继续销售 iPhone 和 Mac，并准备等到这项新兴技术充分发展后，让用户通过苹果设备使用 AI。

items.author: Aaron Wise
items.content:
Recent outages at the National Security Agency, Federal Aviation Administration, National Weather Service, Microsoft, JPMorgan, and Apple are escalating a disturbing trend of US infrastructure destabilization.
As frontier AI advances its hacking capabilities, many people are concerned about rogue agents, cyber-extortion groups, and even state-sponsored hacking groups.
On Tuesday, the NSA’s internal classified network went down in what the agency called “temporary degradation during scheduled routine maintenance.”
The same day, a software update knocked Apple users off iCloud and the App Store. Ostensibly routine network maintenance disrupted the National Weather Service’s website for about an hour, too.
That was just one day, as widespread infrastructure failures have now stretched into their sixth consecutive day.
Six consecutive days of US infrastructure outages
Major outages began by Thursday, November 12, when a latent software bug left over 80% of Microsoft 365’s gateway servers unresponsive.
That outage disrupted Outlook and Teams for nearly 24 hours, and Downdetector logged reports from more than 90 countries and territories.
The Microsoft outage even broke the connectors feeding OpenAI’s and Anthropic’s AI services.
Friday was worse. A nationwide FAA ground stop was the longest since September 11, 2001. The prime suspect is a router installed by contractor L3Harris whose ex-CEO cashed out $21 million prior to the incident.
Operators canceled about 12,500 flights that day, and Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy puts the economic toll in the billions.
The weekend offered no relief. Workday serves more than 11,500 organizations, and it was down from Friday evening into Saturday. Many workers found they could not clock in or deal with payroll.
Follow-on flight disruptions continued through Sunday from the earlier FAA outage.
On Monday, a software bug in JPMorgan Chase’s on-premise hardware slowed transactions at the largest US bank, and Downdetector also showed user reports at Bank of America, US Bank, and Wells Fargo, including Zelle service outages.
Also on Monday, United Airlines grounded or delayed departing flights for more than 90 minutes after pilots reported losing aircraft data.
Read more: Linux earns ‘worst bug in the history of the internet’ status
‘98% certainty this isn’t a cyberattack’
The disruptions follow a string of failures this year. US infrastructure failures in 2026 include Linux, Virginia data centers, an August Microsoft 365 outage, Philadelphia’s air traffic control, and a CSX railroad outage.
Donald Trump’s administration doesn’t want to attribute any of the incidents to foreign cyberattacks. US Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin claimed, “98% certainty this isn’t a cyberattack.”
Even President Trump shrugged yesterday, “Things like that happen. It’s fine.” Asked about the FAA flight outage, he downplayed the situation, saying, “Essentially, what you saw was very old equipment that had a heart attack.”
Unconvinced, a Republican Senator countered, “If this is all a coincidence, it’s like the greatest coincidence in the history of the world.”
Tech and infrastructure outages continue to generate headlines this week, and Protos is covering events live as they unfold. As we update this liveblog, new entries will populate below.

items.author: Decrypt Agent
items.content:
In brief
- Anchorage Digital's Diogo Mónica warned that AI tools that can find and exploit vulnerabilities on their own will make the coming year "absolutely brutal."
- Solana Foundation security chief Michael Coates said more than $7.5 billion in crypto has been stolen this year, most of it in the Binance hack.
- Coates pointed crypto teams to the foundation's free STRIDE security framework, while both executives urged firms to lock down devices and keys.
Crypto companies face a wave of AI-powered attacks over the coming year, on top of an already relentless threat from North Korea, security leaders warned at Solana's Breakpoint conference in London.
"The next 12 months are going to be absolutely brutal," said Diogo Mónica, co-founder of crypto bank Anchorage Digital. "They're going to be a slaughterhouse."
Over the past three to six months, AI systems have gone from finding vulnerabilities to building full exploits and carrying out every step of an attack on their own, Mónica said on a panel chaired by Gordon Corera, co-host of The Rest Is Classified podcast. Aggressive hacking tools now let anyone with no security knowledge simply tell a model to "please hack this website," he said.
Michael Coates, chief information security officer at the Solana Foundation, said AI has "dramatically lowered the cost and the barrier to hacking." Projects that once escaped attention will now be targeted opportunistically, he said.
'Part of their GDP'
North Korea remains the biggest threat to crypto firms, Coates said in a separate presentation. More than $13 billion in crypto has been stolen over the past decade, over $7.5 billion of it this year alone, with some $6 billion drained in a single breach: last month's hack of Binance, which the FBI has blamed on North Korea. "This is how they fund their programs in North Korea," he said.
Coates described the Binance attack as a chain of familiar tactics. A developer downloaded poisoned software from a sponsored search result, and an engineer later took a job interview on a work device and downloaded software as part of it. That gave the attackers a foothold to move through the network and reach signing services, which they used to authorize malicious transactions rather than steal the keys themselves, he said.
Fake job interviews are a "telltale tactic of North Korea," he said, along with poisoned tools and deepfake video calls. North Korean hackers have stolen $400 million using deepfake calls alone. When North Korean operatives can't get hired directly, they use people in the U.S. to take jobs on their behalf, then connect remote keyboards and mice so attackers can access the company's network, Mónica said.
The U.S. Treasury recently sanctioned 11 people over just such a North Korean IT worker scheme. Anchorage now onboards new staff in person at its U.S. office, Mónica added, and every employee works on a locked-down Chromebook, logging into remote machines for development, which he said removes 90% to 95% of its corporate attack surface.
'Protect the keys'
Coates pointed teams to STRIDE, a free security framework the Solana Foundation launched in the spring. It sets out 18 core controls tailored for crypto, and protocols covering more than 74% of DeFi's total value locked on Solana, including 10 of the top 11, have gone through it, he said. The foundation is also using AI to reverse-engineer newly launched programs and find flaws before attackers do, which he said has prevented more than $5 million in potential losses in the past month.
Both executives warned against basic mistakes. Connecting email inboxes to AI agents invites prompt injection attacks, Mónica said, while Coates urged teams to "protect the keys," using hardware security keys for logins and properly configured multisig wallets, with plans for key rotation and loss. "That's where we see the attackers going," Coates said. "They're getting the entry points through the basics. They're pivoting around to get the keys, and that's where they're unleashing their fury."

items.author: Oluwapelumi Adejumo
items.content:
Quick Take
- Surging Texas electricity prices made shutting down more profitable than mining Bitcoin for some operators, contributing to a 9.13% difficulty drop.
- Riot's $24.7 million in earlier power credits shows how miners can earn revenue by returning electricity to the grid instead of producing BTC.
- As miners return online, Bitcoin's next difficulty adjustment could erase nearly all the relief from the Nov. 14 reduction.
Surging Texas electricity prices made shutting down more profitable than mining Bitcoin for some operators in early November.
The disruption contributed to Bitcoin's 9.13% mining difficulty reduction on Nov. 14, its largest since June, as expensive electricity forced miners to reconsider whether keeping their machines running was worthwhile.
In a Nov. 17 analysis, mining services firm Luxor found that West Texas electricity prices exceeded the mining revenue of a machine operating at 25 joules per terahash during 45% of the hours between Oct. 29 and Nov. 14. That compares with just 9% during the preceding difficulty period.
The pressure intensified between Nov. 7 and Nov. 11, when average daily electricity prices ranged from $64 to $122 per megawatt-hour. Meanwhile, the modeled mining equipment generated approximately $54 in revenue for every megawatt-hour consumed, before electricity and other operating costs.
Luxor estimated that higher electricity prices alone accounted for roughly four-fifths of the increase in unprofitable mining hours, suggesting energy costs drove the disruption rather than Bitcoin's declining price.
The resulting shutdowns reduced the computing power securing Bitcoin's network, contributing to the difficulty adjustment that lowered the measure to 134.82 trillion from 148.36 trillion.
Why switching off can pay more than mining Bitcoin
While miners exposed to wholesale electricity prices could avoid losses by shutting down, companies with favorable power contracts had another opportunity.
Bitcoin mining company Riot Platforms, for example, can temporarily suspend operations and return contracted electricity to the grid in exchange for credits when market prices exceed its fixed electricity rates.
According to its third-quarter SEC filing, Riot earned $24.7 million in power curtailment credits during the three months ended Sept. 30, including $22.9 million from voluntarily reducing electricity consumption.
Those earnings preceded November's electricity surge but demonstrate how the arrangement works.
Consider a miner generating $54 in Bitcoin revenue per megawatt-hour while paying a fixed electricity rate of $35.
Continuing operations would produce $19 after electricity costs. However, if wholesale electricity prices reached $100 and the operator could return its contracted power, it could receive a $65 credit instead.
Under those assumptions, switching off would generate $46 more per megawatt-hour than continuing to mine.
That difference helps explain why electricity markets can influence Bitcoin mining activity independently of cryptocurrency prices.
Bitcoin's 9% difficulty relief faces a rapid reversal
However, the relief from November's shutdowns may prove short-lived.
Luxor estimated that Bitcoin's computing power recovered to approximately 1,100 exahashes per second as West Texas electricity prices eased between Nov. 13 and Nov. 15, even as Bitcoin's price continued falling.
The recovery accelerated block production after the difficulty reduction, raising the prospect of another substantial adjustment.
Through Nov. 17, Bitcoin blocks had averaged approximately 9.11 minutes since the reset, faster than the network's targeted 10-minute interval.
If that pace persists throughout the current difficulty period, the next adjustment could increase difficulty by approximately 9.85%, reversing nearly all the previous reduction. Even if block production slows to 10 minutes for the remaining period, the early acceleration would still produce an estimated 2.72% increase.
The extent of that rebound will depend partly on whether Texas electricity prices remain low enough to keep miners operating.
items.title: Bitcoin miners found a way to profit without mining BTC, but the advantage may not last

Anthropic上市前夜请来迪士尼前公关掌门人，曾为白宫和希拉里操盘

动察 Beating AI 快讯，按照计划，Anthropic 将于 11 月 19 日正式登陆纳斯达克，股票代码为 ANT，预计融资超过 600 亿美元。就在上市前夜，公司请来了迪士尼前首席公关官 Kristina Schake，由她负责企业公关业务。

Schake 的履历相当特殊。她曾担任奥巴马政府第一夫人米歇尔的公关主管、希拉里 2016 年总统大选的副公关主管，还负责过拜登政府的新冠疫苗宣传及 Instagram 的全球公关。

2022 年，她进入迪士尼担任全球公关高管，随后升任首席公关官。任职期间，她参与应对了两场股东代理权争夺战，以及 CEO 更替等重大事件。今年 3 月，她随迪士尼领导层交接离职。

Anthropic 正面临一场复杂的舆论考验。公司一边强调先进 AI 可能带来的严重安全风险，一边向投资者展示 AI 取代大量现有工作、推动收入高速增长的潜力。巨额算力支出、AI 泡沫争议和监管压力，也让这场上市备受关注。

Perplexity推出多模型API：Claude拒答可切GPT，63道编程题多解3道

动察 Beating AI 快讯，Perplexity 发布 Orchestrator API，将 GPT、Claude、Gemini、Grok，以及 GLM、Kimi、DeepSeek 等 45 款以上模型整合到同一个接口。开发者只需一套 API 密钥，就能调用不同公司的模型，统一结算费用。

它提供两层自动调度。第一层解决服务稳定性：例如 Anthropic 的 Claude 接口报错、限流或超时，系统就尝试切换到 AWS Bedrock 提供的同款 Claude，不需要开发者手动处理。

第二层是按任务自动选择模型。开发者可以用自然语言指定规则，例如简单代码修改交给便宜的 GLM-5.3 Flash，复杂故障排查交给 Claude Opus 5.5，跨模块设计交给 GPT-6.1 Sol。系统会读取当前对话，由一个专门的决策模型判断该用谁。即使中途切换模型，也能继续读取此前的完整对话。如果后来切回原模型，还可以尝试复用它之前留下的缓存，减少重复计算。

Perplexity 还测试了一个特殊用途：当 Claude 因安全限制拒绝正常任务时，改用 GPT 继续处理。团队针对网络安全、生物学和拒答后的请求设置了切换规则。在 Terminal-Bench 4.1 的 63 道编程题中，Claude Fable 5.2 单独完成 38 道，加入路由后完成 41 道，但每道任务的估算成本也有所上升。

Anthropic预计今日完成IPO定价，机构如何看待估值和目标价？

BlockBeats 消息，11 月 18 日，Anthropic 预计今日完成 IPO 定价，明天（11 月 19 日）起在纳斯达克以代码 ANT 正式开始交易。官方招股书给出的发行价区间是每股 70 到 78 美元，对应完全稀释后估值最高约 1.4 万亿美元。这比早前市场传闻的接近 2 万亿美元目标有所下调，但仍大幅高于今年 5 月最后一轮私募的约 9650 亿美元。

目前多家机构已经给出了自己的估值展望，分歧比较明显。

独立投研机构 Morningstar 的基准情景给出约 1.7 万亿美元（与当前 Trade.xyz 上相同）的公允价值，认为当前 IPO 定价区间偏低，中点位置有大约 24% 的上行空间。他们的牛市情景超过 3 万亿美元，熊市情景则只有约 5000 亿美元，主要假设未来五年收入复合增速在 47% 左右。⁠

研究机构 New Street Research 更乐观一些，直接给了「买入」评级，12 个月目标价 105 美元，相对发行区间有 35% 到 50% 的上涨空间。他们预计公司收入将从 2026 年的大约 530 亿美元，到 2030 年突破 5000 亿美元，同时计算能力从年底的约 5 GW 扩张到 30 GW。⁠

印度 Ashika Institutional Equities 则将焦点放在 2027 年收入上，基准情景预计约 1110 亿美元，谨慎情景 885 亿美元，乐观情景可以到 1370 亿美元以上。按这个收入算，当前 IPO 定价对应的 2027 年 EV/Sales 大约在 9.5 到 10.7 倍，和 AI 基础设施公司的中位数接近。

纽约大学教授 Aswath Damodaran 根据招股书数据估出的股权价值大约在 1.475 万亿美元，处于早前讨论区间的偏低位置。

总体看，机构对收入高增长的方向比较一致，但对估值上限的判断差距较大。核心分歧在于计算成本能否持续下降、企业客户采用速度，以及和 OpenAI 等对手的竞争格局。

原文链接 https://m.theblockbeats.info/flash/378016

黄仁勋下一站猜测：Semafor记者预测其或筹集500亿美元再创业，重返英伟达概率为零

BlockBeats 消息，11 月 18 日，在最新一期 Prof G Markets 节目中，Semafor 商业记者 Rohan Goswami 预测，黄仁勋不会重返英伟达，而可能与长期支持他的朋友筹集并投入 500 亿美元创办新企业。对于黄仁勋回归英伟达的可能性，Rohan 给出的判断是 0%。

DB Live 创始人 Deirdre Bosa 则认为，黄仁勋仍存在回归可能。她指出，黄仁勋是主动辞去 CEO 职务，而非被董事会直接解雇；马斯克此前签署要求黄仁勋复职的网络请愿书，并公开表示聘请黄仁勋将是自己的荣幸，反映出硅谷科技圈对他的支持。不过，外界声援并不意味着英伟达董事会会改变决定。

两位嘉宾还讨论了黄仁勋离开对英伟达及 AI 产业生态的影响。Deirdre 认为，英伟达未来一至两年的产品路线图已基本确定，但长期能否延续技术领先，取决于继任者能否保持黄仁勋的战略判断力，并应对谷歌 TPU、亚马逊 Trainium 等产品的竞争。

需要注意的是，500 亿美元再创业属于 Rohan Goswami 在节目中的个人预测，并非黄仁勋已公布的计划；目前也没有证据表明黄仁勋与马斯克旗下企业就任职或合作展开正式谈判。

替投行新人做Excel和PPT，Model ML融资2.5亿美元，晋升独角兽

动察 Beating AI 快讯，伦敦 AI 创企 Model ML 宣布完成 2.5 亿美元 B 轮融资，估值达到 15 亿美元，正式晋升独角兽。本轮由 General Atlantic 和 QED Investors 联合领投。

Model ML 专门替投行初级分析师和咨询顾问处理繁琐工作，包括搭建 Excel 财务模型、制作融资和并购演示 PPT、撰写尽职调查报告。

它的 AI 智能体能接入企业内部数据和 Office 软件，掌握整笔交易的背景。例如，一笔交易的关键财务假设发生变化，AI 就能同步修改相关 Excel 表格，并更新对应的分析和演示材料，不用分析师逐份修改。智能体还可以主动跟踪企业新闻，判断对交易的影响，提前准备分析报告。

Model ML 会根据任务选择不同模型，部分工作交给自家微调的开源模型。按照公司自测，这些模型在适用的金融任务上，运行成本仅为前沿大模型的 2%，大多数情况下速度快 5 倍，准确率相当甚至更高。

Model ML 披露，今年第三季度的年化经常性收入同比增长 12 倍，日活跃用户增长 26 倍。

金融 AI 赛道的竞争已经相当激烈。另一家专攻投行工作的创企 Rogo，今年 4 月融资 1.6 亿美元，估值达到 20 亿美元。OpenAI 和 Anthropic 也已推出面向金融专业人士的 AI 产品。

Cognition推出Devin Bots：一个人管20个AI，每周处理1900个PR

动察 Beating AI 快讯，AI 编程公司 Cognition 发布 Devin Bots，让 Devin 从执行单个编程任务，升级为能够长期管理整个项目的 AI 工程主管。

你只需要交代目标，比如「让安卓 App 始终跟上 iOS 版本」，它就会自己发现问题、拆分任务、指挥多个 Devin 并行写代码、测试和审查。遇到需要人工决策的事项，再集中向你汇报。整个过程可以持续数周，无需人工不断分配新任务。

Cognition 展示了一个内部案例。一名工程师让 Devin Bot 负责开发公司的安卓 App。44 天里，AI 自己创建和处理工单，最终关闭 1217 个工单，合并 1134 个代码修改请求（PR），并把 App 推进 Google Play 公开测试。期间，负责监督的工程师只发了 183 条消息，其中 22 天完全没有发消息。

另一个案例更夸张。Cognition 成员 Jenny Xu 的手游工作室只有她一名真人，却有约 20 个 AI 员工，分别负责开发、测试、版本发布和用户反馈。她只需要与一个名叫 SuperJenny 的总管 Bot 沟通。工作室每周处理的 PR 从约 50 个增加到 1900 个，并保持每周发布新版本。

Devin Bots 现已上线，支持每月 200 美元的 Max 套餐及每月 80 美元起的 Teams 套餐。每月 20 美元的 Pro 套餐暂不包含该功能。

TD Cowen维持SharpLink买入评级及13美元目标价，下调ETH价格预期

BlockBeats 消息，11 月 18 日，TD Cowen 周三维持以太坊储备公司 SharpLink（SBET）买入评级及 13 美元目标价，但因 ETH 单笔交易销毁量明显下降，下调对 ETH 价格走势的预期。

TD Cowen 预计，ETH 将于 2026 年第四季度末达到约 2,413 美元，较第三季度末下降约 10%，此后价格升值路径也将更加平缓。分析师 Lance Vitanza 指出，尽管以太坊网络活动保持强劲，但交易量增长并未带来相应的 ETH 销毁量，促使该机构采取更谨慎的价格预测。

与此同时，TD Cowen 看好 SharpLink 的主动资金管理策略。该公司 ETH 持仓从第三季度末的 892,708 枚增至截至 11 月 16 日的 896,003 枚，近期增量主要来自质押收益，而非新增购买，累计质押奖励已达 31,820 枚 ETH。公司还向 Lido 配置了 2 亿美元，并投资 Galaxy Sharplink Onchain Yield Fund，以提高 ETH 持仓收益。

TD Cowen 认为，若 ETH 价格回暖，SharpLink 有望通过增加每股 ETH 持有量，大幅跑赢现货 ETH ETF；若 ETH 价格持续低迷，质押收益也有望覆盖公司运营成本。

OpenAI联创John Schulman：AI对齐应成为公共科学，不能由少数科技公司主导

动察 Beating AI 快讯，Thinking Machines 联合创始人、OpenAI 联创 John Schulman 在 A16Z 播客节目中表示，AI 对齐不应成为少数几家科技公司的专属研究，而应发展为一门面向全球的公共科学，让更多人参与 AI 价值观的塑造，避免过度依赖少数公司的判断。

随着递归自我改进（RSI）逐渐取得进展，AI 已开始辅助模型研发。OpenAI 首席研究官 Mark Chen 透露，AI 研发流程已出现 RSI 加速效应的早期信号，目前进展约为 25% 至 50%，但 AI 仍难以独立判断有价值的研究方向，尚未实现自主研发下一代模型。

Mark Chen 同时警告，随着模型自主性增强，若其目标与人类意图不一致，长时间运行可能产生意料之外的次级目标。不过，更强大的 AI 也有望反过来帮助研究人员监控模型行为、发现并修复对齐问题。

John Schulman 强调，AI 对齐不仅是技术问题，也涉及由谁决定 AI 应遵循的价值观，用户和社会应拥有更多参与和塑造 AI 价值观的空间。

原文链接 https://m.theblockbeats.info/flash/378009

「大空头」Michael Burry质疑英伟达延迟提交10-Q，炸裂业绩未能打消疑虑

BlockBeats 消息，11 月 18 日，英伟达第三季度营收达 1158 亿美元，显著超出市场预期，但公司表示将在未来数周内提交正式季度报告（10-Q），引发知名做空者 Michael Burry 关注。

Burry 在 X 平台转发相关质疑帖文并回复「Exactly（正是）」。该帖质疑，英伟达为何先公布业绩安抚投资者，却未同步提交包含完整财务信息的 10-Q 文件，并将此事与曾陷入财务披露争议的企业作比较。
